title: scanner: the coverage harness never seeds stored render pages - every stored row is unreachable in the runtime suite
description:
runtime_coverage_test.go seed() (lines 538-602) stores one exchange per vulnapp.Endpoint. The row loop at :817-818 skips entries with an empty Row, and vulnapp_stored.go declares render pages exactly that way: /st/notes (:162), /st/feedback/list (:138), /st/account/activity (:143), /st/profile/card (:149), /st/support/tickets (:154), /st/theme/page (:166), /st/bookmarks (:183), /st/forms (:195), /st/widgets (:206), and the /safe variants.

Consequence: those pages never enter rt.exchanges or s.store.Exchanges(), so storedRefetchTargets (internal/scanner/stored_refetch.go:208) - which builds its candidate list from s.store.Exchanges() - cannot list them, RefetchStoredTargets never requests them, and ObserveStoredCanaries never sees a body carrying a planted canary. Every stored row whose evidence comes from a render page is therefore structurally unreachable in this suite; the suite reports them as missed even though the row and matcher are correct.

Measured: TestTheScannerDetectsWhatTheTargetDeclaresItIsVulnerableTo reports 159 of 160 rows demonstrated, 1 missed - the missed row is Cross-site scripting (stored) via /st/note?text=seed, and the target IS vulnerable (its Note says the note is inlined unescaped into a <script> literal by /st/notes on a later request).

The production path differs: storedRefetchTargets iterates REAL captured traffic, so in an operator scan the render page is reached because the crawl captured it. The gap is specific to the coverage harness.

FIX DIRECTION: seed each empty-Row manifest entry the same way as the row entries (a GET captured into the store), or add an explicit render-page seeding step. Acceptance: the stored row fires in the coverage suite and the count moves from 159/160 to 160/160, with no change to the scanner packages. This is the fix that unblocks 1a3z and tqyf; do NOT add a stored row or a new matcher for it.
close_reason: FALSIFIED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-09-18. The bead claims the coverage harness never seeds stored render pages. That is false: runtime_coverage_test.go:173-179 iterates vulnapp.Vulnerabilities() and calls seed() for every entry with NO Row filter, and seed() stores each exchange (rt.store.AddExchange(ex), rt.exchanges[e.Path] = ex.ID). The empty-Row skips at :757, :817-818, :970, :1013 govern which rows are AUDITED, not which are seeded. Proven directly by instrumenting the refetch: completion.Refetch printed "324 of 324 known GET targets re-fetched; 1 canary sighting(s), 1 planted canary(ies) never surfaced anywhere (refused=0 failed=0 observed=1 outstanding=1)" for /st/note?text=seed. Observed=1 means the render page WAS re-fetched and the canary WAS sighted there. The real cause of the stored-row miss is recorded on tqyf: storedRenderNotes renders the value into an unbreakable single-quoted JS string literal. Closing this bead as filed on a false premise; the tracking continues on tqyf.

title: scanner: FinishScan is never called by any web audit path — deferred stored-DOM claims never settle in operator-launched scans
description:
The scanner's stored re-fetch pass (stored_refetch.go:58-88 FinishScan), the browser render pass (stored_dom_render.go:113-184 RenderStoredTargets, MaxStoredDOMRenders 120, storedRenderConcurrency 4) and the pending-claim registry are FULLY BUILT and tested in isolation (runtime_coverage_test.go:321-391, stored_lifecycle_test.go:40-73) — and have ZERO production callers. Verified by grep over internal/web for FinishScan|RenderStoredTargets|RefetchStoredTargets: the only hit is a coincidental substring in the minified ui/dist/app.js. Only cmd/xsschallenge/main.go:294 and scanner tests call it.

Consequence: any stored-DOM claim deferred during a web-launched audit (POST /api/audit/{id}, /api/audit/selected, crawl-audit, API scan) is registered in the PendingRegistry and NEVER settled — no re-fetch, no browser render, no second ask. domStoredCheck's deferDOMStoredClaim (checks_dom.go:340-367) returns errCheckInconclusive so the row reads 'undecided, not clean' — honest, but the evidence to confirm it never arrives.

## Context
Found by the browser/crawler integration research scout 2026-09-17. The xsschallenge binary is the only caller today — proof the machinery works when invoked. FinishScan mutates shared scanner state: read stored_refetch.go:58-88 carefully for idempotency before choosing the call site.
acceptance_criteria: 1. FinishScan is called at the end of runBulkAudit (api_scanner_audit.go:361 tail) and runAudit (:212 tail). 2. Call placement respects concurrent audits — PendingRegistry mutation is scanner-wide; the xsschallenge pattern (FinishScan once after the batch) is the model; if two audits run concurrently the second call must not double-settle. 3. A deferred stored-DOM claim from a web-launched audit settles within the same task's outcome. 4. e2e or web test proving the wiring. 5. Full gate.
close_reason: Wired and verified. FinishScan now runs at both web audit tails: runAudit (single exchange, synchronous — reply carries a deferred ScanCompletion block) and runBulkAudit (selections/crawl-audit/API scans — settlement lands on the same task row with a dashboard event naming settled and outstanding counts). Guard: new ActiveScanner.PendingCount() reads claims WITHOUT creating the registry (Pending() would self-register, making the guard lie), so a claim-free audit sends no second-pass traffic at all. Load-bearing ordering found by the failing test: the bulk paths' context is the task's own and Handle.finish calls the task's cancel, so the deferred phase MUST run before task.FinishWithNote — first draft ran after and the re-fetch died 'context canceled' with 0/3 targets re-fetched (observed via stderr probe). Tests: 3 new in audit_deferred_test.go against the real vulnapp — bulk (30 claims settle, finding lands on the store, registry drains), single (deferred block in reply, registry drained), guard (static audit: no second-pass traffic, no deferred block). Mutation check observed: both guards disabled -> bulk times out waiting for claims, single reports missing deferred key; guard test keeps passing as it should. Gates: internal/web 38s ok, internal/scanner 431s ok, e2e-go.sh 24/24, vet/gofmt clean, whitespace audit clean. Committed 29463f4.

title: build: the embedded console bundle is stale — 18 src commits since dist/app.js was last built (4a16c38), style.css older still, so no UI work reaches a browser
description:
The last twelve consecutive UI-touching commits changed burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/ and never rebuilt the two files the Go binary actually embeds. internal/web/ui.go declares `//go:embed ui/index.html ui/style.css ui/dist/app.js`, so a browser only ever sees the committed bundle. None of that frontend work reaches a user.

Verified live, not inferred. I built one binary from the committed dist/app.js and one from a rebuild of current src/, ran the Decoder's per-selection transform (burpsy-react-ui-adrh, commit 6e59efa) against both with a real trusted pointer selection, and got two different products:

  rebuilt bundle: select "AAAA" in "AAAA aGVsbG8= BBBB", encode base64
      .tool-output = "QUFBQQ== aGVsbG8= BBBB"
      childNodes [span.enc-span "QUFBQQ=="], [text-node " aGVsbG8= BBBB"]
      toast "1 step(s) ran on the selection", badges [.., selection, 8 B]

  committed bundle: the identical selection and run
      .tool-output = "QUFBQSBhR1ZzYkc4PSBCQkJC"   (base64 of the WHOLE input)
      childNodes [text-node] only, no .enc-span anywhere
      toast "1 step(s) ran", badges [.., 24 B] — no "selection" badge

Artifact level, replicating e2e-ui.sh's own staleness gate (rebuild to a temp dir, cmp):
    app.js:    STALE  fresh=2004941 B  committed=1948354 B
    style.css: STALE  fresh=67921 B    committed=65568 B
    "enc-span" in app.js:    fresh 1 hit, committed 0 hits
    "enc-span" in style.css: fresh 1 hit, committed 0 hits
(Both committed files contain zero NUL bytes, so grep is trustworthy here; positive controls on the same two files: "Transform pipeline" 1 hit in dist/app.js, "tool-output" 1 hit in style.css.)

Commits with src/ changes and no dist/app.js rebuild, newest first, at base b78b94a:
    6e59efa decoder: transform a selected span, and colour the output by what was applied (adrh)
    e966085 scanner: a configuration library, so a tuning that worked can be kept (uxcs)
    6c2a9b8 ui shell: Burp's Intruder menu, with every greyed item saying why (yinb)
    9db168b sequencer: Burp's token handling — pad short tokens, and decode base64 first (i4u)
    ce11b60 history: split the response timer into TTFB and total, as Burp does (jcdm)
    3b4c089 logger: capture by MIME type, so a long engagement's log is not all images (73vm)
    bb051e5 dashboard: the event feed can be cleared, and stops hiding rows (voc)
    49414e6 certificate: the CA can be regenerated from the console (j7t)
    0a157fc ws: an operator's edit to a frame is recorded as a fact on the frame (d7bu)
    0ae599b ui: the palette's recents, and encoders that act on the selection (1wrb)
    57badba intruder: the resource pool's random variation and delay increment (nn0n)
    ff0b6f4 proxy: Burp's listener list, not one socket (pfeg)
Twelve of twelve. Only adrh was driven in a browser here; the other eleven are presumed unshipped on the same artifact evidence (their source is in src/, and src/ is provably not in the committed bundle) and each needs its own confirmation once the bundle is rebuilt.

The tree already knows about this failure mode and already has the check. e2e-ui.sh lines 89-99 rebuild the bundle to a temp directory and cmp it against the committed one, failing with "the embedded bundle is STALE: dist/app.js or style.css does not match a rebuild of src/". Running that check today fails. The defect is that nothing gates a commit on it: e2e-ui.sh is a shared fixed-port suite that agents are told not to run, so twelve commits landed through the gap.

What needs to happen
1. One owner — not a fan-out, two agents building app.js concurrently produce a file neither can review — runs `cd burpsy-go/internal/web/ui && bun run build` and commits dist/app.js and style.css alone.
2. The staleness cmp moves out of e2e-ui.sh into something that runs per commit (the pre-commit guard, or a Go test that shells out to bun and skips when bun is absent), so a src/ change without a rebuild cannot land again.
3. Each of the eleven other beads is re-verified against the rebuilt bundle before anything is called done; several were signed off against locally rebuilt bundles and so signed off on something that never shipped.

Release blocker for v0.1: the console that ships is twelve features behind the console that was reviewed.

Found while verifying burpsy-react-ui-xxag; see that issue's comment for the full Decoder evidence.
acceptance_criteria: cd burpsy-go/internal/web/ui && bun run build produces a dist/app.js and style.css byte-identical to the committed ones (e2e-ui.sh's staleness cmp passes), a per-commit gate fails when they diverge, and the Decoder per-selection transform is observed working in a browser served the committed bundle.
close_reason: Fixed in 2bd10a8. The committed console bundle was 17 features stale: 18 src commits had landed since dist/app.js was last built, and the Go binary embeds index.html, style.css and dist/app.js via go:embed, so every UI change since then was invisible to anyone running a built binary — only agents verifying against locally rebuilt bundles ever saw them, which is exactly the evidence-vs-shipped gap this project refuses to tolerate. Rebuilt in a scratch git worktree at HEAD so the bundle corresponds to committed source and nothing else (the shared tree carries another session's uncommitted session/extension edits, and a bundle built there would ship code with no source). Verified: the rebuilt bundle contains the View-menu tab switches ('Restore default tab layout'), the scope rule library ('Save to library'), the settings tree, the Comparer word mode, and S7's markers (enc-span, 'ran on the selection', 'Clear event log', 'Exclude MIME types'); ./ui-pass.sh against a console built from the same worktree reports 53/53 with 0 axe violations; the scope-library wire and settings search verified live over their endpoints in the same run.

comments.author: burpsy
comments.text:
CORRECTION to this issue's own description — three things in it were wrong. I am the one who filed it, so I am the one who has to say so.

1. The count. "Twelve commits" came from an arbitrary `git log -15` window, and the script that produced it only printed commits touching src/, so a bundle-rebuild commit inside the window would have been invisible to it. ff0b6f4 is not a boundary, it is just the oldest src-touching commit the window happened to reach. The real boundaries:

    dist/app.js last rebuilt:  4a16c38  2026-09-14  "ui: rebuild the console bundle for this batch"
    style.css   last written:  0bac060  2026-09-12  "ui: Burp's suite-wide Search ... (vs9k)"
    0bac060 is an ancestor of 4a16c38 — so the 4a16c38 batch rebuild rebuilt app.js and NOT style.css.

    git log --oneline 4a16c38..b78b94a -- internal/web/ui/src   ->  18 commits, not 12
    git log --oneline 0bac060..b78b94a -- internal/web/ui/src/styles.css  ->  4 commits

   So: 18 src-touching commits since app.js was last built, and style.css has been stale since before that. The six I had not listed are 6c1ed47 (scope rule library, e365), 3e53e05 (settings search + section rail, f6a), d5b37c2 (comparer word-level diff, mwq/qbd4), abed934 (tool tab context menu, 0plv), edb1eef (View menu is Burp's tab list, lje3), e138661 (test-only fix, needs no rebuild).

2. The cause, and therefore the owner. I wrote "6e59efa never rebuilt dist/app.js" as if that were an omission by its author. It is not. The agent brief forbids agents from committing dist/app.js or style.css, and CLAUDE.md says to coordinate before rebuilding because two agents building app.js concurrently produce a file neither can review. 4a16c38 — "ui: rebuild the console bundle for this batch" — is the orchestrator doing exactly the step the process assigns it. Every one of the 18 authors did what they were told. The defect is that the post-merge rebuild has not run since 2026-09-14 and nothing enforces that it has run before work is verified or called done. Owner is the orchestrator/main, not any of the 18 authors.

3. The gate I proposed. Putting the staleness cmp in the pre-commit guard would fail every agent commit by construction, since agents are required to leave the bundle unbuilt. The check belongs at the merge point — on master's tip after the batch rebuild, or in whatever runs before a bead is moved to done — not per agent commit. e2e-ui.sh lines 89-99 already implement the comparison correctly; what is missing is that something runs it at the right moment.

Unchanged and still standing: the live differential. The same driver, the same trusted pointer selection, against two binaries differing only in the embedded bundle:
    rebuilt  bundle -> .tool-output "QUFBQQ== aGVsbG8= BBBB", .enc-span present, toast "1 step(s) ran on the selection"
    committed bundle -> .tool-output "QUFBQSBhR1ZzYkc4PSBCQkJC", no .enc-span, toast "1 step(s) ran"
and the artifact counts (enc-span: fresh 1 / committed 0 in both app.js and style.css; app.js fresh 2004941 B vs committed 1948354 B; style.css fresh 67921 B vs committed 65568 B).

Re-verification driver, ready to re-run against the rebuilt bundle by whoever fixes this:
    /tmp/u7/drive2.cjs  (cases A-D; expects a burpsy on 127.0.0.1:19261)
    /tmp/u7/stale.sh    (the artifact cmp on its own)

title: intruder: a running attack cannot be paused or stopped from the console, and there is no progress indicator
description:
Measured live against http://127.0.0.1:18281/ during the 2026-09-14 UI-parity verification sweep (burpsy-go/docs/ui-parity-verify-2026-09-14-intruder-tools.md, section 'STILL-OPEN #1').

During a deliberately throttled 24.0 s sniper attack (25 payloads at 1 rps, confirmed by ELAPSED 24.0 s), six polls at 1.8 s intervals found NO button matching /^(Pause|Resume|Stop)$/ and no progress or [role=progressbar] element. The toolbar sat at 'LOCATING ATTACK…' / 'Attacking…' for the whole run; sent/planned counts appear only in the final report. Positive control on the same page at the same moment returned Auto §, Clear §, Find positions — so the query and selector work.

Stopping a running attack is a safety control on an engagement, not a convenience: a cluster bomb bounded at the 200,000-request ceiling and aimed at the wrong host can today only be halted by killing the process (or from the dashboard, which is a different page).

The backend already serves all of it:
- GET /api/intruder/attacks during a run returns {"task_id":9,"kind":"sniper","target":"127.0.0.1:18299","planned":15,"status":"running","sent":2,"failed":0} with sent advancing once per second (re-measured 2026-09-14: sent 2/4/5/7/8/10 over six 1.5 s polls).
- internal/web/api_intruder_control.go already exposes POST /api/intruder/attacks/{task_id}/{pause|resume|stop}.

The defect is an identification race in the page. pages/intruder.tsx only starts looking for its task id while run.isPending, and matches heuristically on a.target === targetAuthority(target) && a.kind === mode && !priorIds.has(id). The controls and any progress rendering are gated on that lookup landing. In the measured run it never landed inside a 24 s window even though the API was returning the matching attack the whole time.

Fix: POST /api/intruder/run must hand the page its own task_id at launch instead of making it infer one. The run response BODY is the attack report and does not exist until the attack is over, so the id travels as a response header emitted and flushed before intruder.Run is called (task.ID() is already known at s.tasks.Start). The page then polls /api/intruder/attacks by that id, renders an advancing sent-of-planned progress indicator from the first poll, and offers Pause/Resume/Stop wired to the existing control routes.
acceptance_criteria: From the first poll of a launched attack the Intruder toolbar renders a progressbar whose value advances (sent of planned) and Pause/Resume/Stop buttons enabled while the attack is running or paused; 'locating attack…' does not appear on a normal launch; a stopped or paused attack says so in the page's own words; the final report still arrives and renders on the Results tab. Verified live on http://127.0.0.1:18281/ with a throttled attack, quoting counts per poll.
close_reason: Retracted: the finding was a measurement artefact, not a defect. The sweep sampled the Intruder page with the Payloads tab selected; Pause/Resume/Stop and the progress bar render on the Results tab. Re-run with Results selected showed Pause/Stop from t=1.1s and a progress bar advancing 12.5% -> 16.67% -> 20.83% in lockstep with the API. The controls exist and work. No code change landed; the speculative run-response task_id header was reverted unbuilt.

title: intruder: URL-encode-these-characters replaces every non-UTF-8 payload byte with U+FFFD, silently corrupting binary wordlists
description:
Proven against the real function:

    in   61 ff 62
    out  61 ef bf bd 62   ("a\ufffdb")

The raw byte 0xff becomes the three-byte UTF-8 encoding of the replacement character. What goes on the wire is not what the wordlist said.

## Cause

internal/intruder/process.go:407-418, URLEncodeSet's encode closure:

    for _, r := range string(b) {
        c := string(r)
        ...
        out.WriteString(c)
    }

Ranging a string yields runes. A byte that is not valid UTF-8 decodes as utf8.RuneError, and string(r) re-encodes it as EF BF BD. The pass is byte-oriented in intent and rune-oriented in implementation.

## Reachability

internal/intruder/payload.go:367 reads a 'file' payload source with os.ReadFile and puts the raw bytes into PayloadSet.Items with no UTF-8 validation. Binary and extended-ASCII wordlists are ordinary fuzzing inputs. The URL-encode box ships seeded with Burp's default character list, i.e. non-empty, so the pass is ON by default.

## Impact

Every non-UTF-8 byte in the payload set is silently replaced. No error, no warning, no report line. An operator fuzzing for an encoding or overflow bug with a binary corpus is testing bytes they did not choose, and a negative result means nothing.

## Found by

Independent review pass over PR #46, 2026-09-11; reproduced by calling URLEncodeSet on a PayloadSet holding "a\xffb".
acceptance_criteria: URLEncodeSet iterates bytes, not runes: a non-UTF-8 payload byte is either passed through unchanged or percent-encoded, never replaced; a test asserts the exact output bytes for a payload containing 0xff.
close_reason: URLEncodeSet decodes per-rune (the named set is characters, so multi-byte must match as a unit) but writes from the input byte slice, and a byte that is not valid UTF-8 passes through as itself — it is in no named set and no safe set, which is the function's own documented rule. Empty-set fast path is now a byte scan too. Table test pins the boundary incl. four invalid-byte shapes; positive control fails with 61 ef bf bd 62. f7c6db8

title: issues: a finding whose exchange was deleted marshals occurrences as JSON null and takes down the whole Issues/Scanner tab
description:
The same defect class as burpsy-react-ui-9pxd, in a new place, and newly reachable because of this PR's own history-delete feature.

## The chain

1. internal/web/api_scanner_audit.go:240 — activeFinding leaves nf.Occurrences nil when s.store.GetExchange(f.ExchangeID) fails. That is deliberate and documented: 'An exchange that has since rolled out of the store leaves the occurrence off rather than half-filled: no location is honest, a partial one is not.'
2. internal/web/api_capture.go:631-648 — findingToIssueView only ever appends to v.Occurrences. It is never initialised, so a finding with none marshals as "occurrences": null.
3. internal/web/ui/src/lib/types.attack.ts:115 declares occurrences: Occurrence[] — not nullable.
4. internal/web/ui/src/pages/scanner.tsx:150 reads finding.occurrences.length with no guard, inside groupFindings, which runs over the WHOLE findings list on every render of the tab.

So one such finding blanks the entire Issues/Scanner tab, not just its own row.

## Why it is reachable now and was not before

core.TrafficStore.GetExchange could not fail for a live id — there was no eviction. Commit c38fed6 ('history: Delete items and Clear') introduces DeleteExchanges and the ts.deleted set. Launch an audit against a request, delete that request from HTTP history (or press Clear) before the finding is recorded, and the finding lands with no occurrence.

## Fix

Initialise v.Occurrences to an empty slice in findingToIssueView, the same fix 9pxd took, and assert the wire form rather than the struct — Go cannot tell nil from empty.

## Found by

Independent review pass over PR #46, 2026-09-11; traced end to end through all four files.
acceptance_criteria: A finding with no occurrences goes out as "occurrences":[] and the Issues tab renders it; a wire-level test asserts the JSON, not the struct.
close_reason: findingToIssueView initialises v.Occurrences to an empty slice, so a finding with no resolvable occurrence goes out as [] not null. Third instance of the nil-slice/null class after 9pxd; test asserts the marshalled JSON because Go cannot tell nil from empty. bb089f0

title: dashboard: 'Pause all tasks' pauses only sequencer capture — crawls, Intruder attacks and Scanner audits ignore the gate and keep sending
description:
The suite-wide pause shows its banner and stops nothing an operator would press it for.

## Evidence

    $ grep -rn 'GateCheck' --include=*.go internal/ | grep -v _test
    internal/web/api_sequencer_capture.go:561:  s.tasks.GateCheck(ctx)
    internal/dash/tasks.go:572,600,614,621        (the definition and its doc comments)

One caller. Crawl loops, intruder.Run and the audit engine never reach a GateCheck, so PauseAll sets registry state that nothing but the sequencer consults.

## Reproduction

Start a crawl or an Intruder attack. Click 'Pause all tasks'. The button flips, the 'Task execution is paused' bar appears, /api/dashboard reports paused:true — and the crawl or attack keeps issuing requests at the same rate.

## The claim

Commits caaca7f/2868d3b describe 'suite-wide pause/resume for running tasks' and motivate it with 'a long crawl'. The crawl is the case that does not work.

Note Intruder has its own separate, working pause (intruder.Control, used by the Intruder page's own controls) — so an attack is pausable, just not from the dashboard button that says it pauses everything.

## Found by

Independent review pass over PR #46, 2026-09-11; confirmed by grepping every GateCheck caller.
acceptance_criteria: Pause all tasks holds a running crawl, Intruder attack and Scanner audit between units of work; each loop's gate is pinned by a test that asserts the request count stops advancing while paused.
close_reason: Crawler, ActiveScanner and intruder.Attack each gained an optional suiteGate func(context.Context), called between units of work, wired to s.tasks.GateCheck at four web call sites. Plain func not *dash.Registry (crawler does not import dash; an engine asking the task registry whether to keep working is the wrong dependency direction). Nil keeps CLI/MCP/tests unchanged. Five tests: the crawl asks the gate at least once per fetch (not once at the start), a held gate stops both the crawl and the attack, release resumes and loses no work. Both pinned by removing the call. 60370d9

title: tasks API: GET /api/tasks/pause, /resume and /{id}/cancel change state — taskAction has no method check and the commit that added it narrowed the test that would have caught this
description: State-changing task actions answer to GET. ## Proven Driving the real mux: GET /api/tasks/pause -> 200 {"paused":true,"running":0} GET /api/tasks/resume -> 200 {"paused":false,"running":0} GET /api/tasks/1/cancel -> 404 No running task with that id (404 = id lookup, not 405) ## Cause internal/web/api_tasks_cancel.go, taskAction: the function never checks r.Method. The pause/resume switch and the /cancel branch are both handled INLINE, so they inherit no guard. The sibling actions delegate to handlers that do check — handleTaskAgain (:36, requires POST) and handleTaskDelete (:64, requires DELETE) — which is what makes the omission look deliberate when it is not. ## Why the suite missed it The generic 'every route rejects a verb it does not implement' manifest test had a /api/tasks/ sub-path fixture of "{id}/cancel"; commit 21425a6 — the same commit that introduced this dispatcher — narrowed it to "1". ## Impact A prefetcher, a link scanner, a monitoring probe or an tag on any page the operator visits can pause the whole dashboard or cancel a running task. No body, no custom header, no CORS preflight involved. ## Found by Independent review pass over PR #46, 2026-09-11; reproduced against the real mux.
acceptance_criteria: GET on /api/tasks/pause, /api/tasks/resume and /api/tasks/{id}/cancel all answer 405 with an Allow header; the route-manifest fixture covers a task sub-path again.
close_reason: taskAction now requires POST on pause, resume and {id}/cancel (405 + Allow). Also generalised the route-manifest 405 sweep: specs gain actionPaths, a sub-path->allowed-verb map swept with its own method set, so a subtree routing /api/tasks/1 to DELETE and /api/tasks/1/cancel to POST has both covered — the single-subPath design is what let the original narrowing hide the gap. Pinned: removing the guard fails the sweep. bb089f0

title: intruder: JSON insertion points are off by the chunk header on a chunked body — the splice corrupts the request and every attack against a chunked JSON endpoint is a silent false negative
description:
Two body-offset models are added together, and they only agree when the body is not chunked.

## Reproduced

A base request with Transfer-Encoding: chunked and body {"a":"secret"}, run through FindPoints and ApplyAll:

    content-length: span=92+6 covers "secret"
                    spliced body: {"a":"PAYLOAD"}          <- correct

    chunked:        span=100+6 covers "\":\"sec"
                    spliced body: e\r\n{"aPAYLOADret"}\r\n0\r\n\r\n   <- destroyed

The chunked splice lands 3 bytes early (the length of the "e\r\n" chunk header), overwrites part of the key and the opening quote, leaves malformed JSON, and desyncs the chunk-size line from its data.

## Cause

internal/intruder/points_bcheck.go:31-56, appendJSONAndNestedPoints:

    points, _ := bcheck.EnumerateWithLimit(raw, []string{string(bcheck.IpBody)}, -1)
    ...
    Span: core.Span{Offset: body.Offset + start, Len: end - start},

- body is msg.Shape.Body from internal/core/parser.go — a span into the LITERAL raw wire bytes, chunk headers included, no dechunking.
- start/end come from bcheck (BodyJSONWindow / BodyNestedWindow), which parses via core.ParseRequestEdit, and that DOES dechunk (internal/core/edit.go:169-174, e.Body = dechunk(rawBody)). Its offsets are relative to the dechunked body.

Adding a raw-relative base to a dechunked-relative offset is correct only when the two views are byte-identical, which chunked framing guarantees they are not.

## Why this is P1

The target rejects the malformed request before it ever evaluates the payload. The attack reports sends and no findings. A silent negative on an endpoint the operator specifically chose to attack is the worst failure mode a scanner has — it is indistinguishable from 'this endpoint is not vulnerable'.

## Unguarded

grep -rn chunked internal/intruder returns nothing. points_json_test.go covers Content-Length bodies only.

Note the non-chunked path is genuinely correct: jsonStringValues is a raw-byte scanner that skips 2 bytes on every backslash, so escape handling keeps offsets in raw-byte space. The defect is specific to chunked framing.

## Found by

Independent review pass over PR #46, 2026-09-11; the reviewer's trace was confirmed by executing FindPoints + ApplyAll against both framings.
acceptance_criteria: A chunked JSON body's insertion point covers the value it names, and ApplyAll produces a well-formed request with a correct chunk size; a test asserts both framings side by side.
close_reason: Fixed in d41db13. Chunked JSON insertion points mapped through a dechunk-mirroring scan (rawBodyOffset), straddling windows refused (pinned), ApplyAll re-anchors chunk sizes from the pre-splice base and drops stale Content-Length on chunked requests. Mutation-verified: refusing all chunked windows and passthrough re-chunking each fail the new tests. go build/vet/gofmt clean; intruder/bcheck/core/web suites all ok.

title: scanner: the insertion_point_types config restricts only the queue display — every check still probes the hardcoded default set, so disabling cookie insertion does not stop payloads going into cookies
description:
An operator who turns off an insertion-point kind is told it is off and it is not. This is a decorative switch on the one surface where that matters: what burpsy sends to someone else's server.

## Evidence

AuditConfig.InsertionKinds is built from the Burp config keys (insert_url_params, insert_cookies, ...) in internal/scanner/audit.go:886-920 and read back by AuditConfig.insertionKinds() (audit.go:551).

That accessor has exactly ONE caller in the whole non-test tree:

    $ grep -rn 'insertionKinds()' internal/scanner/ | grep -v _test
    internal/scanner/audit_engine.go:1026: points, kinds := auditItemPoints(..., run.cfg.insertionKinds())
    internal/scanner/audit.go:551:         func (cfg AuditConfig) insertionKinds() []string {

audit_engine.go:1026 feeds Items.Begin(...) — the audit-queue ROW. Nothing else.

Meanwhile the checks that actually build and send payloads use a hardcoded literal:

    $ grep -rn 'DefaultProbeInsertionKinds' internal/scanner/*.go | grep -v _test | wc -l
    20

— 19 call sites in checks_injection.go, checks_reflection2.go, checks_remaining.go, checks_stored.go and checks_final.go pass DefaultProbeInsertionKinds ({query, body, cookie, header}) to NewProbeHarness/runInjection. There is no path from AuditConfig.InsertionKinds into CheckContext at all: CheckContext.Config is *ScanConfig, which scanner.go:104 documents as 'deliberately not merged with AuditConfig'.

## Reproduction

Load a config with insert_cookies=0, or the all-off preset that pins InsertionKinds to {"none"}. The queue row reports the restricted (or zero) insertion-point count. checkXPathInjection, checkLDAPInjection and every SQLi/SSTI/XXE/command-injection check still enumerate and probe the cookie value exactly as before.

## Why the tests pass

Test_run_insertion_kinds_come_from_the_configuration (audit_test.go:691) pins the accessor and the queue-row projection. No test runs a check under a restricted kind list and asserts what was sent.

## Why this is P1

Every other gap on this board costs the operator a capability. This one sends traffic they told the tool not to send, and reports a number that says it did not. In an engagement with a scoped agreement about what may be touched, that is the wrong direction to be wrong in.

## Found by

Independent review pass over PR #46, 2026-09-11; the single-caller/19-call-site split was confirmed by grep.
acceptance_criteria: A check run under a config with insert_cookies=0 sends no payload into a cookie; the restricted kind list reaches CheckContext (or the harness constructor) rather than stopping at the queue projection; a test asserts what was SENT, not what was displayed, under a restricted list.
close_reason: CheckContext gains InsertionKinds (from the scanner's effective AuditConfig) and ProbeInsertionKinds(); all 15 probe sites across 5 checks_*.go files now ask it instead of naming DefaultProbeInsertionKinds. 'none' survives to the probe so a run configured to insert nowhere probes nowhere; an unconfigured run keeps the default unchanged. Guarded by a source check that fails if any check site names the literal again — reproduced. 21f26e2

title: report export: severity/confidence overrides and the severity filter read the raw engine values, so an exported report contradicts the Issues page
description:
An operator triages a finding — raises a Low to Critical via PUT /api/issues/{id} {"severity":"critical"} — and the Issues page shows Critical. GET /api/report/json (and sarif, and html) still says Low.

## Evidence

internal/web/api_capture.go:602-603 (the Issues page) is correct:

    Severity:    f.EffectiveSeverity().String(),
    Confidence:  f.EffectiveConfidence().String(),

internal/web/api_report.go:123-124 (the export) is not:

    Severity:    f.Severity.String(),
    Confidence:  f.Confidence.String(),

core.Finding.EffectiveSeverity() (internal/core/findings.go:266) returns SeverityOverride when set, the engine value otherwise. The export never calls it.

## The filter has the same defect, and it is worse

internal/web/api_report.go:82 filters on the raw value too:

    if finding.Severity == sev {

So ?severity=critical silently DROPS the finding the operator just raised to Critical, and ?severity=low wrongly includes it as though the override never happened. The severity filter and the severity column disagree with the screen and with each other.

## Not covered by tests

internal/web/api_report_filter_test.go seeds raw severities only — no override is ever set on a finding that then goes through the report path, so nothing fails today.

## Found by

Independent review pass over PR #46, 2026-09-11; confirmed by reading both call sites.
acceptance_criteria: A finding with a severity override exports at the overridden severity in json, sarif and html; the export's severity filter selects on the effective severity; a test sets an override and asserts both the exported value and the filter's selection.
close_reason: reportRows and reportFilter.applies both use EffectiveSeverity/EffectiveConfidence, matching findingToIssueView. Four assertions, all failing without the fix: the exported value in both fields, and the filter in both directions (?severity=critical must find the raised finding, ?severity=low must not). Test triages through the real Triage path rather than constructing an already-overridden finding.

title: intruder: the Results tab crashes for any attack with zero failures — report.errors is JSON null and AttackResult reads .length on it
description:
A completed Intruder attack whose sends all succeeded renders the ErrorBoundary instead of its results.

## Reproduction

Launch any attack against a target that answers every request. On return the page switches to Results and the pane shows 'This view failed to render / Cannot read properties of null (reading length)'. Captured in a real Chromium with an unminified bundle:

    TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length')
        at AttackResult (app.js:72370)
    -> internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx, the Failed metric card: {report.errors.length} distinct errors

## Cause

internal/intruder/engine.go: collector.errors is only ever grown by noteError, so it stays nil when nothing failed, and AttackReport.Errors marshals to JSON null. Buckets and Attempts have the same shape and the same exposure for an attack that sent nothing.

internal/web/ui/src/lib/types.tools.ts declares them as ErrorBucket[] / ResultBucket[] / Attempt[] — non-nullable — so the server is violating its own published contract and the page is right to trust it.

## Why it was never caught

There is no browser coverage of an Intruder attack: e2e-ui.sh drives the 17 routes and their empty states, and grep -in intruder e2e-ui.sh is empty. The Go tests read the report struct directly, where a nil slice and an empty slice behave identically. Nothing in the tree ever rendered a real report.

## Fix

Make the three report slices non-nil at construction so the wire form matches the declared type, and pin it with a Go test that marshals a zero-failure report and asserts the JSON carries [] rather than null.
acceptance_criteria: A zero-failure attack renders its Results tab with no console error; GET/POST of a zero-failure report carries "errors":[] on the wire; a Go test fails if any of the three slices marshals as null.
close_reason: collector.errors, PayloadSet.Dropped and BucketExample.Payloads were nil slices marshalling to JSON null against a TS type that declares them non-nullable arrays; every zero-failure attack took the Results tab down with the ErrorBoundary. All three now start empty at their single construction sites. Pinned by two tests that assert the marshalled JSON (Go cannot tell nil from empty) — both fail if the initialisers are removed. f439a6f

title: scope: MayContainHost allows a host matching no include rule, so Repeater/Intruder send outside the include list
description:
core.Scope.MayContainHost — the host-level gate /api/repeater/send has always used — returns true for a host that matches *no* include rule; only a whole-host exclude makes it false. Contains/AuthoriseRaw refuse the same host ("matches no include rule").

Probed directly in internal/core with only `elsewhere.invalid` included:
  MayContainHost("127.0.0.1") = true
  Contains(..., "/x")        = false

Consequence: Repeater sends to a target outside the include list today. The send-group work (burpsy-react-ui-03z / -6i4) inherits this unchanged for its two separate-connection modes; the shared-socket mode is stricter because it runs AuthoriseRaw per raw request and therefore refuses.

Not fixed in that change on purpose: the gate is shared with the Intruder and the proxy pre-filter, so tightening it is a cross-tool scope-semantics decision, not a Repeater one. Tightening it may be correct (an engagement scope with includes should mean 'only these'), but it needs a deliberate call on whether an empty include list still means 'everything'.

Pinned by TestRepeaterGroupSharedSocketIsStricterThanTheHostLevelGateTheOtherModesInherit in internal/web/api_repeater_group_test.go, and documented in sendGroupOnOneConnection's doc comment.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded on whether MayContainHost should refuse a host matching no include rule; if yes, the gate is tightened and the Repeater/Intruder/proxy call sites are checked for the behaviour change.
close_reason: MayContainHost now applies Contains' include semantics: empty include list means everything, non-empty is an allow-list that refuses a host matching no rule. Pinned by TestMayContainHostRefusesAHostMatchingNoIncludeRule (internal/core/scope_may_contain_host_test.go) and TestEveryGroupSendModeRefusesAHostMatchingNoIncludeRule (internal/web/api_repeater_group_test.go). Committed 0d3e656.

description:
e2e-ui.sh reports 212 passed / 8 failed on the working tree AND identically on a clean build of HEAD (e1c422a) in a separate worktree (3 of 8 spot-checked: same failures), so the regression predates this session's redirect-chain changes and is blocking the UI gate.
