close_reason: Burp's Copy other payload exists so two parameters can be held identical while the Cluster bomb varies the rest -- the password and its confirmation case Burp names explicitly. burpsy refused it outside pitchfork, and the refusal was correct: cluster bomb's mixed-radix Fill advances each position's set at a rate that depends on that position's place in the radix system, so a copy stepped by its own ordinal coincided with its source on some requests and diverged on the rest. The test added here measures it -- 60 of 75 requests mismatched, which is 'right most of the time', the worst possible disguise for a correctness bug. The fix is small and exact: Fill already decodes each position's digit as (i/weight_j) % len_j, so a copied position takes the SOURCE's digit at the same ordinal, with the weights computed once per Fill so twenty positions decode twenty digits rather than four hundred. The engine needed no change -- Slot already carries Set and Payload and engine.go reads setBytes[Set][Payload], so a copy is a slot naming its source's set with the source's own ordinal. Pitchfork takes the same path and stays exact for a different reason (one ordinal, not one per radix digit). Sniper and battering ram remain refused, and the message now says why -- they advance ONE set across every position, so 'another position's payload' has no per-position meaning to copy from; the old message blamed cluster bomb, which is no longer true and would have been a lie in the refusal itself. A copy naming a forward, self or out-of-range position is still refused rather than clamped, because a copy that silently resolved elsewhere produces requests whose two 'identical' fields differ. The UI hint no longer says 'Pitchfork only'. Mutation-checked: restoring the own-ordinal copy fails both copy tests. go build/vet/gofmt clean, go test ./... green with the test cache cleared, tsc clean, bun test:lib 715/0, e2e-go.sh 24/24.

title: dashboard: a task's Issue activity, traffic and coverage panes show project-wide data, so a clean run reports other runs' findings
description:
QA PASS 2026-09-25 — a task's detail pane shows project-wide issues, traffic and coverage, so a finished run reports what it found and the operator cannot tell.

## What the pane claims and what it shows

`burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/dashboard.tsx` renders, inside the detail pane of ONE task:
- **Issue activity** (`:1130-1174`) — `activityFindings` is `[...issuesDetailed.data.findings].sort(by id desc).slice(0, 20)` (`:1080-1094` region). That is the project's finding feed with the task discarded, sorted and capped. The tab sits beside a specific task and the heading says "Findings as they were raised" with no qualifying word.
- **Traffic sources** (`:1339`) and **Recent traffic** (`:1407`) — the project-wide task-window counters, not this task's.
- **Coverage** — the project's coverage roll-up.

The findings are attributed to tasks internally; the API projects by `task_id` (burpy-go/internal/web/api_capture.go:849-851) and the audit report carries per-task counts. The pane simply does not ask.

## Burp's shape

running-scans/results/index.html:39-62 — select a task, then its tabs: **Issues** *"Provides details of all security vulnerabilities that the task has found"*, **Logger** *"Provides a list of all HTTP traffic generated by the task"*, **Event log**. Every one is scoped to the selected task, and the Summary tab (running-scans/results/summary.html) is likewise that task's.

## Why this is filed as an honesty defect, not a feature gap

A finished task's pane is how an operator answers "what did that scan actually find?". Here it answers with whatever the last 20 project findings were — another scan's findings, a collaborator's, or a manual recording — with the task's name in the header. Two concrete failures:
1. **A clean task shows findings.** A scan that found nothing displays other tasks' findings under its own name.
2. **A busy task is under-reported.** With more than 20 project findings, older findings this task raised are dropped by the slice while newer ones it never raised are shown.

Either way the pane attributes work to the wrong run, which is the failure mode this project treats as worse than an absent panel.

## Already-tracked correction

`burpsy-react-ui-i18` is CLOSED and its reason describes a project-wide reverse-chronological feed with the finding id as the ordering key — which is what the code does. The gap is the task scoping; the close did not claim it and should have, because the audit the bead came from treated "Issue activity" as the task's issues tab.

## Fix

- Filter `activityFindings` by the selected task's id, and say so when the task has none ("This task recorded no issues") rather than falling back to the project feed. A task-scoped empty state is a fact; a project feed under a task's name is not.
- Scope Traffic sources / Recent traffic / Coverage to the task, or label them "Project-wide" where that is what they are — the honest option is available and costs a heading.
- The projection already exists server-side; this is a query parameter, not a new endpoint.

title: settings: the export confirmation says three sections were affected and never shows the bundle's own eleven omissions
description:
QA PASS 2026-09-25 — a configuration export that carries 4 of 15 settings says "these 3 are affected", and the bundle's own coverage report is never shown.

## What is true

`burpsy-go/internal/web/api_config.go` is honest in the API: `configIncludedSections` holds 4 entries, `configOmittedSections` holds 11 (client_certificates, match_replace_rules, network_settings, platform_authentication, proxy_options, resource_pools, scanner_config, scheduled_tasks, tls_passthrough, upstream_proxy), and the bundle carries a `configCoverage{Partial, Included, Omitted}` that "travels inside the bundle so the file is self-describing". `Partial` is derived from `Omitted` so it cannot claim completeness while omissions exist. That is the right design.

## What the operator is told

`burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/app.tsx:1248-1252` — the success modal says, in full: **"Scope, intercept rules and session handling rules are affected."** It does not render the bundle's `omitted` list, does not say the export is partial, and does not mention `uninteresting_headers`, which IS included. An operator who exports a project to another burpsy, migrates, or keeps a configuration record is told their scope, intercept and session rules moved and nothing else was said either way.

## Why this is filed as a defect rather than a gap

The capability gap (which settings are in the bundle) is a deliberate, documented decision and is not what this bead is about. The defect is that **the honest answer already computed by the server is discarded at the UI**, so a partial transfer reads as a complete one. This project treats that as its worst outcome. The fix is small and does not require deciding what belongs in the bundle: render the returned `coverage.omitted` in the import/export confirmation, label the transfer partial when `partial` is true, and name the included sections from the response rather than from a hand-written sentence that has already drifted (it omits `uninteresting_headers`).

title: intruder: character_blocks is not Burp's character frobber — the per-character incrementing generator is absent
description:
QA PASS 2026-09-25 — `2g13` closed "character blocks/frobber" as one generator. They are different generators, and the one Burp documents is absent.

## The two are not the same thing

`CharacterBlocks` (`burpsy-go/internal/intruder/payload.go`, the `type CharacterBlocks struct` block) cycles a fixed alphabet to fill repeated blocks of a chosen length — `MinLen`/`MaxLen`/`Step`, all about block LENGTH. Burp's **Character frobber** (tools/intruder/configure-attack/payload-types.html:590-595) *"modif[ies] the value of each character position of an input"* and increments one character at a time, so a token's characters can be walked through their values to find which one tracks session state.

A repeated-block generator cannot do that. It has no input value to increment; it only has an alphabet and a length range. The close reason's "character_blocks/frobber" naming is what made this look delivered.

## What an operator loses

Character-by-character mutation of a session token or a parameter is how you find which position an authorization check or a parser actually depends on. Without it the operator can only mutate the token wholesale.

## Fix

- A `character_frobber` source: for each position in a base value, emit the characters of an alphabet in order at that position with the rest held fixed. The base is the operator's current value, which is the mode's defining input and the reason it cannot be expressed as blocks.
- A per-position total the operator can see before launch, like every other generator's.
- Rename the existing type's UI label to "Character blocks" and stop calling it a frobber, so the two stop sharing a name in the close reasons as well as in the UI.
close_reason: Burp's Character frobber and burpsy's CharacterBlocks are two generators, and the close reason that named them together ('character blocks/frobber') is what made the absence look delivered. CharacterBlocks cycles an alphabet to fill repeated blocks of a chosen LENGTH -- alphabet, MinLen/MaxLen/Step, and no input value to vary. Burp's Character frobber 'modifies the value of each character position of an input' and increments one character at a time, and its input is the operator's CURRENT value. Character-by-character mutation of a session token is how an operator finds which position an authorization check or a parser depends on; without it the token can only be mutated wholesale, which cannot separate 'the signature covers all of it' from 'the signature covers the first ten characters'. Three decisions are named in the code. Position-major, so one position is walked across the whole alphabet before moving on and the first divergence from the valid token surfaces in the first few payloads. Characters rather than bytes, so a multi-byte character is one position -- the mutation that delegates the frobber to the blocks generator reports FIVE positions for the two-character base 'e-acute snowman' and splits the snowman in half, which is the conflation made concrete. And the base's own character is emitted first where the alphabet contains it, so an operator can tell whether a position matters; where the alphabet lacks that character, no payload is the base and none is manufactured, because claiming an unperturbed position that was perturbed is the same overclaim as a copy that matches most requests. An empty alphabet defaults to printable ASCII rather than refusing (that is what a token's characters are); an empty base is refused and names the base, because there is nothing to increment. The console label read 'Character blocks (frobber)' on a menu item that WAS the blocks generator; it now reads 'Character blocks' with 'Character frobber' as its own entry and its own fields. The two stale doc claims are corrected so the generators stop sharing a name in the close reasons as well as on screen. Mutation-checked both directions: delegating to the blocks generator fails 3 of 8 tests, and the character-major swap passes every test except the ordering assertion -- which is therefore the only defence of the order. go build/vet/gofmt clean, go test ./internal/intruder + internal/web green, tsc clean, bun test:lib 715/0, e2e-go.sh 24/24.

title: intruder: auto-pause shipped the predicate and the wire field but has no control, so the capability is unreachable
description:
QA PASS 2026-09-25 — auto-pause has an engine and a wire field, and no control anywhere in the UI.

## What shipped and what did not

`burpsy-react-ui-8f2` is CLOSED with a reason that describes a complete mechanism: the `AutoPause` predicate, appears/missing mode, simple-vs-regex, case sensitivity, a 400 for an uncompilable expression, an in-flight response collected whole, an attack-level `auto_paused` counter, and the `intruderRunReq.auto_pause` wire field. Every claim about the *engine* is true. The close reason never says whether an operator can turn it on.

They cannot. `grep auto_pause burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/pages/intruder.tsx` → no match, and the launch body at `intruder.tsx:1523-1572` is built without the field. The Settings tab (`intruder.tsx:2788-2894`) has no auto-pause controls.

## Why this is worse than absent

An operator who knows the feature exists — the API takes it, the report counts it — has no way to use it, and the only way to halt a spray is the manual pause, which requires watching the attack. The bead's own acceptance criteria required the operator-facing controls (Enable auto-pause, appears/missing, expression list, Simple/Regex, Case-sensitive); the close reason verified only the predicate. A capability the operator cannot reach is the same gap as a capability that does not exist, and the close reason reads as though it were delivered.

## What a fix needs

- The four controls in the Settings tab, in the same draft-state shape as every other attack setting: an enable switch, an appears/missing radio, a textarea of expressions, a Simple/Regex radio, and a Case-sensitive switch.
- The launch body sends `auto_pause` only when enabled, for the same reason the other settings are omitted rather than sent empty: an absent field and an empty expression list must not be two wire shapes for "I did not choose".
- A round-trip test through `intruder-config-file.ts`, so a saved attack resumes with auto-pause configured rather than silently dropping it — the same failure fmxv's settings had.
- The uncompilable-expression refusal already exists server-side and should be surfaced as a field error, not a toast after launch.
close_reason: The auto-pause ENGINE shipped complete with 8f2 -- the predicate, appears/missing mode, simple-vs-regex, case sensitivity, a 400 for an uncompilable expression, an in-flight response collected whole, an attack-level auto_paused counter, and the auto_pause wire field. Every claim about the engine was true. The close reason never said whether an operator could turn it on, and they could not: grep auto_pause in intruder.tsx matched nothing and the launch body was built without the field, so the only way to halt a spray was the manual pause, which requires watching the attack. A capability an operator cannot reach is the same gap as one that does not exist, and the 8f2 reason reads as though it were delivered. This change is only the four controls that reach the engine. The block is sent only when the switch is on AND at least one expression is typed, the same omission rule every other optional field follows, because an absent field and an empty expression list must not be two wire shapes for 'I did not choose'. The server reads an empty list as unconfigured (NewAutoPause returns nil, nil), which is what makes the omission honest, and a test pins the two by running both and comparing. The switch decides only whether the block is SENT; the expressions and mode are the attack's own settings, so toggling off and on must find the list intact. An uncompilable expression is surfaced NEXT TO THE EXPRESSIONS rather than only as a toast: the server answers 400, and a toast after a launch that visibly did nothing is the wrong place when the operator's next action is to edit the expression. The re-homing is narrow on purpose -- only a 400 whose body names auto-pause or an expression, because every other 400 belongs to something else in the form. Five config-file tests now carry the block with NON-default values, since defaults survive almost any bug; the round-trip that failed is the one fmxv's settings had. Two notes learned from writing the tests wrong first: the missing-mode test originally used a reflecting target and expected a mid-run pause, which CANNOT work because Control.Pause blocks until resumed, so a mid-run fire leaves the handler waiting and the assertions never run -- it now fires on the last request. And the mode inversion is pinned by a PAIR, because either test alone passes against a server treating missing as always-true; the mutation check confirms it is caught. Verified live in headless Chromium: checkbox present, off by default, expressions hidden while off, all four controls appearing when enabled, mode offering exactly appears/missing, field reporting its count, plus a screenshot and zero axe-core violations in the enabled state. The only console errors are a missing proxy CA file and a crawler endpoint, neither touched here. go build/vet/gofmt clean, go test green, tsc clean, bun test:lib 715/0, e2e-go.sh 24/24.

title: repeater: the ws tab cannot send — its own ws:// target spelling is refused before the dial
description:
## Claim

burpsy-react-ui-6ex landed a WebSocket Repeater tab whose Target field is seeded with the
`ws://host:port` spelling ("ws://127.0.0.1:8080" is the literal default in
internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx at HEAD). The send endpoint refuses that spelling
before it dials, so **every send from the ws tab fails** and the reply pane shows its idle
placeholder — which reads as "nothing happened" rather than "the send was refused".

## Evidence (measured at HEAD ec9ad84, in a detached worktree whose porcelain was clean)

    POST /api/repeater/ws-send {"target":"ws://127.0.0.1:1", ...}
      -> 400  unknown scheme "ws"

Cause: internal/web/api_repeater_ws.go's prepareWsSend hands req.Target to targetParts
(internal/web/api_types.go), which accepts only http/https/bare host:port:

    switch strings.ToLower(scheme) {
    case "https": tls = true
    case "http", "": tls = false
    default: return "", 0, false, fmt.Errorf("unknown scheme %q", scheme)
    }

The UI offers `ws://` (and `wss://` for TLS), the wire understands neither. My own live pass
hit this: four UI sends produced no tool-log row and no pane update until the target was
changed to a bare host:port, at which point the same tab sent fine and rendered the echo.

## Fix direction

Translate the ws spellings on the ONE path where ws:// is what the operator meant
(prepareWsSend), rather than widening targetParts — widening the shared helper would let an
HTTP send be given a ws:// target and silently dial plaintext. A `ws://` naming no host must
be refused, not guessed at ("unknown scheme" and "no host" are different facts).

## Acceptance criteria

A ws:// and a wss:// target both reach the dial (wss asks for TLS), a bare host:port still
works, `ws://` with no host is refused with a reason naming the target, and a test asserts
all four.
close_reason: ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED, measured at HEAD ec9ad84 in a detached worktree with clean porcelain: POST /api/repeater/ws-send {"target":"ws://127.0.0.1:1"} -> 400 unknown scheme "ws". prepareWsSend handed req.Target to targetParts, which accepts http/https/bare host:port only, while the ws tab's own Target field is seeded with ws://host:port (literal default "ws://127.0.0.1:8080" at HEAD). So every send from the ws tab was refused before the dial and the reply pane kept its idle placeholder, which read as "nothing happened". FIX: wsSchemeTarget translates ws:// / wss:// on the ws-send path only (widening the shared targetParts would let an HTTP send be given a ws:// target and silently dial plaintext); wss asks for TLS; "ws://" with no host is refused with a reason naming the target. Also restored Burp's DIRECTION CHOICE, which the landed work dropped (its code comment said "the direction choice is to-server here" with no control for it): the tab now offers To server / To client, and the wire's existing 400 + reason for to-client is surfaced in the reply pane (new `failure` prop) instead of being invisible. The HTTP response editor no longer renders under the ws panes (two panes answering different questions was what hid the bug). VERIFIED: two new Go tests, mutation-checked (removing the translation fails them with exactly unknown scheme "ws"/"wss"); live on a console built from the commit against a local echo origin — ws tab sent "live wire" and rendered "Reply 1 · text · 14 B  echo:live wire", To client showed the wire's refusal verbatim, switching back sent again and rendered "echo:direction probe". tsc clean, test:lib 710/0, gofmt clean. Commit 098017f.

title: tests: TestASkippedExchangeWhoseResponseLaterLandsIsAuditedOnceAsRetried races the next tick for the retry slot — ~40% flake
description:
## Claim

`TestASkippedExchangeWhoseResponseLaterLandsIsAuditedOnceAsRetried` (internal/web/liveaudit_retry_test.go:68) fails intermittently with "pending retry slot is empty: the give-up must file the id it skipped", measured 5/12 single-run failures at pristine HEAD in a detached worktree (1109eb1). Not related to any change under test — reproduced identically on a gofmt-only tree (1/12; same test, noise in the rate).

## Root cause (measured)

The test waits for `Skipped() != 0`, then immediately reads `pendingRetryID()` and requires `pending == true`. But the sweep is entitled to consume that slot on its very next tick: `takePendingRetry` (liveaudit.go:444-458) clears the slot "whether or not it landed" — the retry is ONCE by design (iyqg), and a tick 5ms after the give-up clears the slot before the test's read. The test observes a transient the product deliberately does not hold:

    give-up tick T0:   recordSkipped(1, id) -> skipped=1, pendingRetry=id+1
    test poll (≤5ms):  sees skipped==1, reads pendingRetryID()
    tick T0+5ms:       takePendingRetry -> pendingRetry=0 (response still nil)

The give-up loop's own condition is only `Skipped() == 0`, so the test can lose the race between the give-up and the next tick.

## Fix direction

Poll for the pair of facts the test actually depends on — skipped==1 AND the slot holding OUR id — within the existing 15s budget, and only then fail. Alternatively land the response before the give-up and assert the retry consumption instead of the slot's existence, which is the fact the rest of the test already waits on (`Retried() == 1`). The former is the smaller change; the latter removes the transient entirely.

## Do not

Do not widen `takePendingRetry`'s clearing rule or add any hold to the product state — the once-only retry is iyqg's contract and the flake is in the test's observation window, not the sweep.

Surfaced while landing dp8p (the liveaudit.go gofmt fix): the web package suite this test sits in must be green to trust that gate.
close_reason: Test-side fix, no product change. The flake was the test's: it polled Skipped() then read the pending-retry slot as if held, but takePendingRetry clears the slot on the first tick after the give-up whether or not the response landed (iyqg's once-only contract), so a background 5ms tick was entitled to empty it first - measured 5/12 failures at pristine HEAD, 1/12 on an unrelated tree. Rewritten to drive liveAuditTick by hand (the liveaudit_coverage_test.go pattern): the give-up is asserted tick by tick, the filed id is checked to be the test's own /late exchange, the response lands between two driven ticks, the next tick takes the retry (retried==1, slot cleared), and one more tick proves no third chance. The tick arithmetic is now explicit: tick 0 admits the two seeded exchanges before it first waits, so the give-up is the liveAuditStallTicks-th no-progress tick, the (ticks+1)-th in all. Measured in a worktree at HEAD with only this file changed: 0/40 failures in isolation (was 5/12), the retry family green, the whole internal/web package green (28.9s), gofmt and vet clean. Commit e0397a5.

title: scanner: the stored-XSS row misses /st/note while the fixture declares itself vulnerable there
description:
## Claim

The `internal/scanner` runtime coverage suite fails at HEAD: 159 of 160 rows demonstrated, missing `Cross-site scripting (stored)` at `/st/note?text=seed`.

## Evidence

Measured 2026-09-22 against HEAD 629740a, twice, in detached worktrees whose `git status --porcelain` was empty. `/tmp/verify-s9ma` at 9cd2424 and `/tmp/verify-7suo` at 629740a both reproduce it:

```
--- FAIL: .../rows/Cross-site_scripting_(stored)_via_/st/note?text=seed
    runtime_coverage_test.go:846: the target is vulnerable here (a note submitted here is inlined unescaped
    into a <script> literal by /st/notes on a later request) but "Cross-site scripting (stored)" was not reported.
    rows reported instead: ASP.NET debugging enabled, ... Input returned in response (stored), ...
    runtime detection: 159 distinct catalog rows demonstrated across 162 endpoints, 1 missed
```

Note what IS reported for that exchange: `Input returned in response (stored)` and `Suspicious input transformation (stored)`. So the stored family runs and the capture path works; it is specifically the XSS-stored row that does not fire.

## What is NOT yet established

Whether this is a detector regression or a fixture/environment artefact. Two candidates worth ruling out before touching a detector:

1. The deferred render phase. `vulnapp_stored.go:159` declares the case as `{Path: "/st/note?text=seed", Row: "Cross-site scripting (stored)", Stored: true, Note: "a note submitted here is inlined unescaped into a <script> literal by /st/notes on a later request"}`. The row depends on `/st/notes` being re-fetched by the deferred phase. Commit 0714504 ("run the stored-DOM deferred phase once, not once per endpoint") changed exactly that sequencing, taking the suite from 1115s to 478s. Check first whether the deferred phase still covers this endpoint after that change.
2. Headless-Chrome / DISPLAY. The project already knows autofocus and onfocus payloads never fire headless, and that `cmd/xsschallenge` refuses to score without a DISPLAY. This suite reported the other 159 rows, so Chrome is present, but the stored XSS row may still be the one needing a real window.

## Do not

Do NOT fix this by relaxing the pin to 159 or by marking the row skipped. The suite exists to prove detection; a pin lowered to match a regression is the exact defect this codebase treats as worse than the failure. If it turns out to be environmental, the honest outcome is a bead stating the precondition, not a lowered number.

## Fix direction

Bisect between 0714504 and HEAD on this one endpoint first. If the deferred phase lost coverage, restore it. If it is a detector regression, fix the detector and confirm the row returns WITHOUT changing any other row verdict.
notes: SCOPE FINDING 2026-09-22 (Main): this miss is being fixed by a peer in the uncommitted WIP at internal/vulnapp/vulnapp_stored.go, which rewrites storedRenderNotes from `var note = "<value>"` to a bare-expression assignment with a comment explaining that a quoted literal correctly contains the value, so a scanner refusing to call it a breakout is RIGHT and such a fixture cannot demonstrate stored XSS at all. Do NOT implement independently — coordinate with the owner of that file. Still binding: never lower the runtime-coverage pin to 159.
close_reason: Fixture bug, not a detector regression, and not the deferred phase or headless Chrome either. The old storedRenderNotes wrote the stored note inside a quoted JS string literal (var note = '<value>'), and jsBreakoutConfirmed is RIGHT to refuse that shape - a canary still enclosed by a literal did not break out (xss_jscontext.go:210), the exact anti-false-positive direction. A fixture whose canary can only ever be contained cannot demonstrate the row. Proven at the predicate level with a temporary in-package probe: jsBreakoutConfirmed=false for the old shape, true for the bare-expression shape (note = <value>). The fix is the fixture only: the render now assigns the stored note as its own expression (var note = 'sticky'; note = <value>), the shape an app concatenating user input into a script body actually produces. Measured in a worktree at HEAD with ONLY this file changed: go test ./internal/scanner/ -run TestTheScannerDetectsWhatTheTargetDeclaresItIsVulnerableTo now reports 160 distinct catalog rows demonstrated across 163 endpoints, 0 missed (was 159, 1 missed); wantDemonstrated stays 160 and no other row verdict changed (single-row and full-suite runs both green; /st/note row PASS in 4.29s). Commit 9a21f11.

title: scanner: no stored HTML/text-node breakout row - xsschallenge stored case misses
description:
The xsschallenge `stored` case plants a value over HTTP (cmd/xsschallenge/main.go:167) and renders it raw on a DIFFERENT page (main.go:170, c.viewPath). The scanner plants its own canary and settles it at FinishScan, calling inContext on the render-page body.

There is no stored row that recognises a canary reflected RAW into a text node or into HTML body content. The available stored rows are: Cross-site scripting (stored) [script-context only, now a real JS-lexer confirm], CSS injection (stored), Open redirection (stored), Link manipulation (stored), Form action hijacking (stored), Client-side HTTP parameter pollution (stored) - none of which is "raw markup breakout in the body".

So a stored reflection into a plain text node reports nothing, which is the miss. The fix is a new stored row (or a new matcher on an existing one) that confirms an HTML breakout the way the REFLECTED side already does via confirmMarkupBreakout: parse the render-page body and check the canary reached markup, not escaped text.

Evidence it is a row gap and not a confirm gap: 1a3z proved the script row now runs a real lexer confirm and the challenge is STILL unchanged at 21/23. Localise with a single-row unit test over a seeded render body, never via the scorecard (its deferred attribution at main.go:309-313 is over-broad and adds every deferred finding to every seed).
notes: MEASURED CAUSE 2026-09-18. The instrumentation was run; this is what it printed: "stored re-fetch for /st/note?text=seed: 324 of 324 known GET targets re-fetched; 1 canary sighting(s), 1 planted canary(ies) never surfaced anywhere (refused=0 failed=0 observed=1 outstanding=1)". Read Observed=1 carefully: the canary WAS planted, WAS stored, WAS rendered by /st/notes, WAS re-fetched, and WAS sighted by ObserveStoredCanaries. Every link in the refetch chain works. The earlier hypotheses (missing row, unseeded render pages, lost query string, header dilution, MaxStoredPlants truncation) are ALL falsified. TWO REAL DEFECTS remain: (1) storedRenderNotes (internal/vulnapp/vulnapp_stored.go:381-388) writes var note = (quote)(canary)(quote); - a single-quoted JavaScript string literal containing an alphanumeric-only token. That is correctly INSIDE a string, not at code position, so contextScriptBreakout / jsBreakoutConfirmed (checks_stored.go:235-264) correctly refuses to call it a breakout. The manifest Note at vulnapp_stored.go:161 says inlined unescaped into a <script> literal - literally true, but a literal is not a sink. A row named Cross-site scripting (stored) cannot be demonstrated by a fixture whose rendering context is an unbreakable JS string literal. (2) Outstanding=1 alongside Observed=1 means TWO canaries were planted for this endpoint, because PlantStoredCanaries (checks_stored.go:75-83) plants one per point from bcheck.EnumerateWith over cc.ProbeInsertionKinds() - which since commit 3aa13a7 includes header - while storedSubmitNote reads ONLY r.URL.Query().Get(text). The header canary can never surface, so Outstanding permanently overstates the unobserved set. FIX DIRECTION, do NOT add a row or a matcher (1a3z already added the correct one and it correctly refuses this fixture): change storedRenderNotes to place the stored value where an alphanumeric canary can reach code (e.g. after a closed quote in an existing statement, or into an HTML body), or change the manifest Note to stop claiming it demonstrates stored XSS. Separately, PlantStoredCanaries should not plant into insertion points the target handler cannot read.
close_reason: FIXED AND MEASURED 2026-09-18. Cause (as recorded on this bead): storedRenderNotes (internal/vulnapp/vulnapp_stored.go:381) rendered each stored note as var note = (quote)VALUE(quote); - a single-quoted JavaScript string literal. An alphanumeric canary inside a correctly-closed literal is exactly what SAFE output looks like, so contextScriptBreakout correctly refused it, and no fixture shaped that way could ever demonstrate the row. FIX: the handler now emits var note = (quote)sticky(quote); note = VALUE; console.log(note); - the stored value is assigned as a bare EXPRESSION, which is what an application concatenating user input into a script body actually does, and the only shape in which a token reaches executable position. This satisfies both halves of jsBreakoutConfirmed (xss_jscontext.go:210-238): the canary is at jsEncCode, and parser.ParseFile succeeds on the whole script. EVIDENCE, before and after: the subtest TestTheScannerDetectsWhatTheTargetDeclaresItIsVulnerableTo/rows/Cross-site_scripting_(stored)_via_/st/note?text=seed FAILED on four consecutive runs (196.43s, 196.79s, 197.20s, 208.12s) with "the target is vulnerable here but Cross-site scripting (stored) was not reported", and PASSES in 4.63s after the change. The DOM-based sibling passes too (214.08s). Matcher unit tests in checks_stored_script_test.go still pass (4 tests, 0.112s), so the stricter lexer contract was not weakened. NOT changed: no new row, no new matcher - 1a3z already added the correct one and it was right to refuse the old fixture. Also untouched: the Outstanding=1 artifact (a header canary planted into an endpoint whose handler reads only ?text=) remains, and is a separate narrower issue noted on this bead earlier.

title: scanner: cookie insertion points use a form codec - multipart raw-safe emptied part content
description:
Two real defects in internal/bcheck/insertion.go, found while investigating 2p9u (whose own premise is falsified: the cookie codec was NOT the cause of the xsschallenge cookie-pref miss).

DEFECT 1 (the serious one): Apply()s codingRawSafe case ran its refusal check but never assigned escaped, so escaped stayed "" and every multipart part content was emptied on the wire. Debug evidence: name="user"\r\n\r\n\r\n with coding=6. Fixed by restoring escaped = payload.

DEFECT 2: cookie values were encoded with the form codec. codingCookieValue is now an opaque octet run: & and = pass through verbatim (they are not cookie delimiters), while ; CRLF NUL and DQUOTE are refused rather than escaped because no escape exists - ; terminates the clause, so escaping it would change the payloads meaning.

Also repaired two fields a prior broken edit had swallowed: the loc: on the body-to-cookie relocation point (clampOffsets(0,0,...) removed nothing, so the cookie stayed empty) and BaseValue in expandNested. Nested percent-encoded JSON cookies now round-trip via a percentDecode fallback gated to cookie parents that nest.

ACCEPTANCE: 9 cookie tests in insertion_test.go pass, incl. verbatim-arrival, clause-terminator-refusal, relocate-to-cookie, and nested-JSON round-trip. build/vet/gofmt clean. NOT a detection change: xsschallenge was 21/23 before and after.
close_reason: Closed

title: live-audit: stall/skip is terminal and stalledAt has no operator action
description: From the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G4+G8b): after 10 ticks x 3s = 30s with no progress (liveaudit.go:555-562) the sweep advances past the exchange, counts it skipped and warns (:596-622) — the exchange is NEVER revisited (recordSkipped is terminal, no re-enqueue). The pane shows the stalled id but the only remedies are waiting 10 ticks or disabling the sweep (stalledAt has no operator action). Burp's event-driven model carries dispositions on out-of-scope/action-taken items rather than dropping them. Smallest honest shape: (a) an operator 'retry stalled' action on the pane that resets the cursor to the stalled id, and (b) re-enqueue a skipped id once rather than dropping it permanently, counting the retry distinctly from the first attempt.
close_reason: Both halves of the smallest honest shape shipped. (1) THE SKIP'S SECOND CHANCE: recordSkipped files the id it gave up on; the next tick's first act takes it back if its response landed — admitted through the same in-scope gate (a retry that bypassed scope would re-open an operator exemption), counted as retried and never folded into swept, because 'gave up on 1' and 'gave up on 1, took 1 back' are different coverage claims and the pane reports both. The retry is ONCE: the slot clears on the take whether or not the response landed. A probe-driven debug caught a real control-flow bug in the first draft: the no-progress early return swallowed a tick whose only batch was the taken-back exchange, so the retry never reached the audit — the early return is now gated on the retry batch, verified by the previously-hanging test passing in 0.16s. (2) THE OPERATOR'S Retry stalled ACTION: POST /api/scanner/live {retry_stalled:true} rewinds the cursor to the stalled exchange and CARRIES the stall budget rather than restarting it (an operator retry that silently granted a fresh thirty-second wait for the same answer would be a lie of its own); not stalled is a 409, not a silent 200 — the operator learns the stall already cleared. The pane's stalled badge gains a Retry stalled button beside the switch plus an 'N taken back' badge. Tests: liveaudit_retry_test.go 4/4 on the original stall test's harness — the late-landing second chance audited once with both counters visible in the view; the retry is once; the rewind's carried budget observable as the skip arriving within stallTicks+4 further ticks rather than ten fresh ones; 409 while not stalled. title: live-audit: no re-audit on request-content change — cursor is store position, not URL+content hash
description: From the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G1): burpsy's live cursor is a position in the exchange store (liveaudit.go:549-553, walked :572); once an id passes, nothing re-examines it even when the same URL is captured later with different parameters/body semantics. Burp keys live-audit items by URL with request-content change detection. Smallest honest shape: a per-URL content fingerprint in the sweep, so a changed request re-enters the audit queue and the re-audit is counted (not silently deduped). Pairs with the cross-task dedup bead (apfh): apfh suppresses re-audit of the SAME content; this one admits re-audit of CHANGED content.
close_reason: The smallest honest shape the issue named is live: the audit ledger's URL-keyed scopes (per-host, per-path, per-url) now append a request-content fingerprint, so changed content at the same URL re-enters the audit — admitted and counted, never silently deduped. core.RequestFingerprint is a 64-bit FNV-1a over the RAW REQUEST bytes computed once at the capture seam (the same place Mime/CookieNames/Title are decided — the one place the bytes are in hand; the field's doc says why FNV over a crypto digest: the input is burpsy's own bytes, the job is telling two captures of one endpoint apart, and a collision needs ~2^32 same-URL requests in a ledger that resets at 20k units). The WHOLE request is the content — a changed header/method/content-type on an identical body all re-key; a body-only split would re-open the silent dedup outside the split (killed by mutation). Exchange.RequestFP carries it, zero meaning not-computed so restored sessions and hand-built exchanges key exactly as before. UnitKey appends it to the three URL-keyed scopes ONLY — same content = same unit, so identical work stays collapsed and apfh's pairing is preserved (apfh suppresses the same content, this admits the changed); per-request/insertion scopes key by ex.ID, which a new capture always has a new one of. Tests: request_fingerprint_test.go 6/6 — changed content is a different unit across all three scopes; identical content still one unit (the collapse NOT broken); zero fingerprint keys as before; per-request scopes untouched; the fingerprint notices changed body/header/method, deterministic; and the end-to-end ledger contract (first capture runs, identical repeat refused, changed capture re-admitted with the admitted count naming two distinct units) — this last test caught its own author error: my first draft inverted Admit's boolean contract and the failure named the collapse as broken when the LEDGER was right. Mutations: per-URL fingerprint dropped FAILs, body-only fingerprint FAILs, zero re-keyed FAILs — all killed. Gates: go build/vet/gofmt clean; core + scanner suites green (scanner 497s under its own timeout); e2e-go.sh 24/24. title: scanner: LLM post-scan second look (Burp AI shape) — decision needed on endpoint
description: From the ML research (/tmp/smartscan-report.md §6): Burp has NO ML in its scanner core — the statistical battery (Zr8b) is classical FIPS/chi-square tests (already ported as the sequencer), 'training' in the literals is the license trial (Zepn:8713-8719), and Burp's actual AI is an LLM post-scan investigator: after crawl+audit finish it investigates findings gated by severity+confidence (Standard = High + Medium-tentative; Extended adds Low firm/tentative; Custom), 'checks each issue to determine whether it represents a real and exploitable risk', and writes evidence + remediation steps. It does not affect crawl or audit phases; Collaborator/Infiltrator issues are excluded. burpsy's seam: findings carry Name/Severity/Confidence/Evidence with evidence-tiered confidence (tentative/firm/certain) and dom_confirm's promote/retire loop — but no post-scan investigation pass. Smallest honest shape: a deferred phase on the scan task rows (the gxbk FinishScan pattern) or a /api/findings/triage surface, gated exactly like Burp's Standard profile; findings marked distinctly, never confidence-promoted past the evidence (enrich.go:3-6). DECISION NEEDED: requires an operator-supplied LLM endpoint (free OMP models are unreliable — 404s/429 lockouts). The count of investigated findings is the honest metric. DO NOT add an ML model to the engine core: Burp doesn't, the statistical niche is covered, and a nondeterministic verdict is at odds with honest counting.
close_reason: Burp AI's actual shape is live: an LLM POST-SCAN investigator over gated findings, with NO ML in the engine core (the research's own line, kept). THE ENDPOINT DECISION is recorded on the issue (operator standing directive): an operator-configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint, no compiled-in default — free OMP models are unreliable per the bead's own finding, and a default would send finding text to whoever owns it. (1) THE GATE, Burp's Standard profile: High any-confidence, Medium tentative-or-better, Low never swept, Collaborator never (an interaction id is not a transcript). (2) THE PASS: one chat completion per finding, temperature 0, the finding's own fields in the prompt; JSON/fenced/prose parsing with out-of-vocabulary -> investigate-further carrying the model's RAW words — the verdict that spends attention rather than guessing. (3) THE HONEST-COUNTING RULE, enforced three ways: TriageNote rides BESIDE Confidence/Severity and never moves either (pinned by unit AND end-to-end mutation); an endpoint ERROR leaves NO note; the run's answer counts investigated/outside-gate/errored, never a bare done. (4) THE SETTINGS DOOR: GET/PUT /api/settings/triage via the persist settings table — the API key WRITE-ONLY on the wire (GET answers configured/not), a keyless PUT keeps the stored credential, enabling without a base URL refused (the two-gate rule: configured AND enabled); the verb guard 405s before the persist check per the manifest's contract. (5) THE RUN DOORS: POST /api/issues/triage (the sweep) + POST /api/issues/{id}/triage (the operator's hand on one finding, outside the gate — the gate bounds the sweep, not the operator); the note lands on the STORED finding (SetTriage under the lock), outlives the pass, rides the issues view, clears through the same door. (6) THE UI: an LLM second look toolbar button with toasts stating counts and the two-gate refusal; a leaf-menu action for one finding; Settings › LLM triage section with the key write-only. Tests: scanner/triage_test.go 8/8 (gate truth table + Collaborator-excluded; JSON/fenced/prose parsing; out-of-vocabulary -> investigate-further with raw words; the note-never-moves-grades property twice; endpoint error leaves no note; outside-gate refusal names the gate), web/api_triage_test.go 5/5 (key never echoed; keyless PUT keeps the stored key; enable-without-base-URL refused and leaves the pass off; run door 503 names what is missing; store attach+clear). Mutations: Low-swept FAILs 2, unparseable->false-positive-likely FAILs, confidence-promotion FAILs — all killed. Gates: build/vet/gofmt clean; scanner 471.6s + web 41.6s + core + persist green; manifest verb/sort/confirmation-worthy/reachability green (settings/triage riskClassed riskCredential, added to the credential list in sorted order); tsc clean; bun test green; bundle rebuilt with the LLM section and both doors; e2e-go.sh 24/24.

title: scanner: operator insertion-point skip lists (skip_all_tests_for_parameters)
description: From the Burp scanner-logic research (/tmp/smartscan-report.md §1+§7): Burp lets an operator exempt parameters from testing — scanner.ignored_insertion_points.skip_server_side_injection_for_parameters and skip_all_tests_for_parameters (Zwh1.java:8-13, map_root.tsv:14969-14972, UI copy :11808-11811). burpsy has no way to exempt a parameter that must never be touched. Smallest honest shape: two name lists on EnumerateOptions (insertion.go:335-362); EnumerateWith filters points whose Name matches and the filtered count becomes a new Declined What (mirroring DeclinedPastLimitWhat at insertion.go:322-333). Ship ONE list first + document the two-tier split as declined (burpsy's check families do not yet partition into server-side-injection vs rest).
close_reason: The smallest correct shape the issue named — the skip_all_tests_for_parameters list, wire end to end, no half-built sibling. (1) bcheck.EnumerateOptions.SkipAllTestsForParameters, applied BEFORE the per-request cap: matching is case-insensitive (identifiers fold) and trimmed on entry; a named parameter's points are dropped from every kind, and the drop is counted in a Declined with its own DeclinedSkippedParamWhat — an audit that skipped a parameter it was told to skip must say so, or the operator's exemption reads as 'nothing to test here'. Pre-cap so skip+cap can never double-count one point. (2) The softer sibling (skip_server_side_injection_for_parameters) is deliberately NOT modelled, with the reason in the field's own doc comment: the check families do not yet partition into server-side-injection versus rest, and a skip list that cannot name what it exempts would silently test more than it claims to skip; Burp files with that key load with it honestly in UnrepresentableKeys. (3) AuditConfig carries the list; enumerateOptions threads it into every enumeration (probe harness, audit-item ledger, check context). (4) The queue row classifies as a THIRD skip status, AuditItemPointSkippedOperator, with an operator-naming label — one names THIS parameter on THIS engagement, a run-config toggle is global, and the operator needs to know which setting to change. (5) The configuration API: auditConfigView + applyTo overlay (absent=untouched, explicit []=cleared, no zero-value ambiguity for a list), trims names, REFUSES an empty name rather than dropping it (a name that silently vanishes is a parameter that silently goes back to being tested). Tests: skip_list_test.go 5/5 (every-kind drop with one decline row naming the control-measured count; case-insensitive without reordering survivors — order is observable; skip+cap never double-count, asserted from the decline rows; the queue classification + label + IsSkip; the config ride with zero-config=none) and skip_list_api_test.go 4/4 (trim; empty-name refusal; absent vs [] distinct; view round-trip). Mutations: filter-drops-nothing FAILs 2, case-sensitive FAILs 1, silent-skip FAILs 2 — all killed. Gates: build/vet/gofmt clean; bcheck+scanner+web green (scanner 729s under its own timeout — the first run's FAIL was the 600s default deadline, not a test); e2e-go.sh 24/24. title: scanner: cross-task audit dedup — REQUEST_TO_AUDIT_DEDUPLICATED disposition for the live sweep
description: From the Burp scanner-logic research (/tmp/smartscan-report.md §3+§7) and the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G1): Burp's Zeze.java:17 makes 'we already queued an audit for this request' a first-class queue-level disposition (REQUEST_TO_AUDIT_DEDUPLICATED). burpsy's AuditLedger is per-run (fresh per AuditWithin, audit_engine.go:802-810) — re-seeing an already-audited exchange re-audits it. Smallest honest shape: a host-scoped persisted ledger the live-audit sweep consults (liveaudit.go:631-653) so a re-seen exchange counts as a new Disposition-style row instead of re-audit work. Directly evidenced, small, high value for live sweeps over trickling traffic.
close_reason: Burp's REQUEST_TO_AUDIT_DEDUPLICATED (Zeze.java:17) is now a real disposition row for the live sweep. The seen ledger on LiveAuditState: host#fingerprint -> true (the fingerprint is 6n4d's RequestFP; the pairing is stated in the code — 6n4d admits the changed, apfh refuses the same, one gate must not break the other, and the pairing is TESTED in one test: changed content at the same path audits both captures while dedup stays 0). In the walk, already-seen content is counted as deduplicated and never added to the audit batch; the cursor advances either way. Zero fingerprints ALWAYS admit — refusing content the ledger cannot identify would dedup on 'unknown', a silent coverage hole wearing a success counter (pinned). Bounded like the dispatch ledger: past its cap it resets, counted on the state, evented, and reported as seen_ledger_resets — ON THE STATE, not a package global, because the mutation run with -count=2 caught the first draft's package-level counter leaking across runs (resets=2 for one reset), exactly the honest-counter class this repo exists to prevent; moved, count=3 clean. PERSISTED: SaveLiveSeenLedger/LoadLiveSeenLedger as one settings blob, written by the sweep in small batches (16 new keys per save — no write-per-request), restored at boot before the first tick, so a restart keeps the disposition. The batch counter clears on a failed save so it never retries forever. The view carries deduplicated beside collapsed (same saving, different scopes) and seen_ledger_resets beside ledger_resets. Tests: liveaudit_dedup_test.go 5/5 — re-seen identical content deduplicated and not re-audited (target sees first-capture probes only); the 6n4d pairing test; zero fingerprint admits twice; the ledger survives a NEW sweep run (cross-run) and a Persist/Load round-trip (restart) while still admitting new content; the cap resets visibly and the counter names it. Mutations: gate removed FAILs 2, zero refused FAILs, silent reset FAILs — all killed, and the count=2 run caught the global-counter leak before it shipped. Bonus in the same commit: the iyqg rewind test was hardened after a println-instrumented probe showed the post-retry skip can be delayed behind the sweep loop's synchronous AuditSession — the carried budget is now asserted as a FACT (cursor.at + stalls read under the retry lock right after the 200) rather than a race. title: scanner: 429/503 auto-backoff in the probe dispatch loop
description: From the Burp scanner-logic research (/tmp/smartscan-report.md §4+§7): Burp's resource pools watch response statuses and back the task off (project_options.resource_pools.auto_backoff, auto_backoff_after_429_status_returned, auto_backoff_after_503_status_returned, custom_auto_backoff_status_codes — map_root.tsv:17469-17504, 23192-23213). burpsy's pacing is session-wide time/request budgets only (audit_engine.go:886-897) — a rate-limiting target keeps getting hit at full pace. Smallest honest shape: after a 429/503 in the dispatch loop's response handling (audit_engine.go:1156-1193 area), delay the next step by a configurable backoff and count the back-offs in the outcome; config key on AuditConfig. A counter+sleep, not a resource-pool rewrite.
close_reason: Burp's resource-pool auto_backoff in the smallest honest shape the issue named: a counter and a sleep, not a resource-pool rewrite. (1) OBSERVATION IN BOTH SEND PATHS: sendTestRequestFull AND ProbeHarness.send mark the run's probeMeter on 429/503 — the dispatch-loop test caught the gap in the first draft (only the first path observed; the injection-driven tests never fired the wait and the failing elapsed claim was the honest signal that a second send path exists). Last status wins, nil meter safe. (2) THE WAIT: before each step when the meter is marked — ctx-bounded (a backoff that outlived the budget is a wait with no audit on the other side), re-checked every step (a recovered target stops paying), so a target that keeps 429ing keeps being waited on. (3) THE CONFIG: AuditConfig.AutoBackoffMs — unset inherits DefaultAutoBackoffMs=2000 (the range Burp's own backoff operates in); set-and-zero is the REAL OFF, a legitimate operator choice, distinct from unset on the auditConfigView/applyTo wire. (4) THE COUNTER: AuditOutcome.RateLimited — not a disposition (the work still ran) but an outcome row plus a summary sentence ('N step(s) delayed for rate limiting'), because a sweep that ignored N rate-limit responses must be distinguishable from one the target never throttled. Tests: auto_backoff_test.go 7/7 — including the two tests that exist ONLY because mutations survived: unset-reads-as-zero survived (every wait test set the key explicitly) -> the unset-default test added, mutation now FAILs; 503-dropped-from-harness-path survived (tests only drove 429) -> the 503 test added, mutation now FAILs. Two survivors became two tests; also: meter marks + last-status-wins + nil-safe; set-and-zero waits nothing; a positive 300ms backoff observably delays the audit; the outcome counts and the summary names; the config states stay distinct. Gates: build/vet/gofmt clean; web green (150.7s); scanner green under a 40-minute budget (2337s) — one 25-minute-deadline run hung inside chromedp's sleepContext on the stored-DOM subtest under three back-to-back suite runs' load (isolated rerun passed in 12s; the vulnapp never answers 429 so the backoff cannot reach that path); e2e-go.sh 24/24. No bundle change — the pane renders the outcome's summary string, which now carries the rate-limiting sentence.

title: scanner: light-audit tier — cross-request behavioral dedup of same-typed insertion points
description: From the Burp scanner-logic research (/tmp/smartscan-report.md §1+§7): Burp's Zq5 status bank (map_root.tsv:280-288,313,330) shows a light-audit tier — a cheap probe on the Nth occurrence of an insertion-point TYPE; if it behaves like earlier same-typed points, the rest of that type is skipped with a distinct 'Skipped due to repetitive behavior' status. burpsy audits every point at full price; a 300-parameter request pays for all 300. Smallest honest shape: a per-(IpKind, host) counter in newAuditRun (audit_engine.go:843); after N same-kind clean points on the same host, mark further same-kind points with a NEW status (not reusing Declined) and count them in the outcome so the partition identity (audit_engine.go:1222) holds. The type-occurrence half needs no similarity metric (Burp's :330 sentence is type-keyed, not content-keyed); the content-similarity half is declined unless response-diff infrastructure exists.
close_reason: The type-occurrence half of Burp's Zq5 'Skipped due to repetitive behavior' tier, exactly as the issue scoped it — the content-similarity half is DECLINED (needs response-diff infrastructure this engine does not have; a similarity rule that could not say what it compared would skip work it never justified; Burp's own sentence is type-keyed, not content-keyed). (1) auditRun.lightAudit: map[(kind, host)]uint32 of CLEAN same-type points, PER-RUN not per-item — Burp's tier is cross-request by construction, and a prior that reset per item would be the per-request cap by another name; on the run, not the scanner, for the same discipline the request meter holds. (2) RunLightAudit handle on CheckContext via the InsertionKinds context-value pattern; nil outside a dispatched audit reads as off (a unit test must not skip points on the strength of a run it never joined); the dispatcher resolves the threshold so the check side has no knob. (3) runInjection consults BEFORE the point's probes (a skipped point never sends — the whole saving); a point that runs with every probe's evidence == InjectionEvidenceNone RECORDS CLEAN — a signal means the type deserves full price again. (4) Counted three ways, never hidden: ProbeCoverage.PointsSkippedRepetitive (skipped != tested, the same honesty PointsCapped holds), AuditOutcome.PointsSkippedRepetitive + a summary sentence, and Considered() UNTOUCHED — the checks ran and answered; this number says how many points they did not test, which is why it sits beside RateLimited, not among dispositions. (5) AuditConfig.LightAuditSamplePerKind: unset inherits DefaultLightAuditSamplePerKind=20; set-and-zero is the real off (a compliance sweep's choice). THE TESTS CAUGHT TWO OF THEIR AUTHOR'S OWN WRONG CLAIMS before shipping: the first clean rule (no-probes-added) never fired because perPoint almost always returns probes — the rule must read evidence; and the kind-isolation test asserted a skip in a fixture with no second same-kind point — the assertion's error, not the tier's, rewritten to the true claim (2 query + 1 cookie, threshold 1 -> exactly one skip). Tests: light_audit_test.go 5/5, cap-aware (the per-check cap of 8 truncates before a 20 prior can rise in one request — itself the honest reading of how the two bounds stack: cap=per-request cost, tier=cross-request repetition), the cross-items test pinning the prior accumulating across requests (the feature's whole point), set-and-zero full price, nil tier never skips nor panics. Mutations: prior-rises-on-signal FAILs 2, per-item prior FAILs the cross-items test, silent skip FAILs the counting test — all killed. Gates: build/vet/gofmt clean; scanner suite green (511s); e2e-go.sh 24/24.

title: scanner: dynamic confirmation pass for static DOM-flow findings (Phase 12) — tentative DOM findings are never promoted or retired
description:
The static DOM pass (scanner/dom.go) emits Flows at 'tentative' confidence (dom.go:13-15, findings at :589-591) and its header promises a dynamic confirmation tier that does not exist (Phase 12 named, never built). Every tentative DOM finding therefore stays tentative forever — neither confirmed nor retired — in any scan, web-launched or otherwise.

The confirmation shape is already implied by existing primitives: domexec's ObserveTaint (taint.go:439-543) plants a canary in a source and observes sinks. A confirm pass that takes a tentative DOMFlow's source expression, plants the pass's own canary, and runs ObserveTaint can promote to firm on observation and retire to suppressed-negative otherwise.

## Context
From the browser/crawler scout 2026-09-17 (Tier 1 step 3). Burp's dynamic tier is the in-page Zp7 BurpDynamicJavaScriptAnalysis taint library; burpsy's outside-the-page CDP ObserveTaint answers the same source-to-sink question with a simpler trust model — the scout explicitly recommends NOT porting Zp7's in-page invade() and reusing ObserveTaint instead.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A confirmation pass keyed off the static pass's tentative findings, running only when a browser provider is attached (-dom). 2. Promote-to-firm and retire-to-suppressed both observable in a test with the vulnapp DOM fixture. 3. Findings carry their confirmed/suppressed state on the wire. 4. Without a browser attached, findings stay tentative and the caveat says so. 5. Mutation check. 6. Full gate.
close_reason: Phase 12 is built — the dynamic confirmation tier dom.go's header has promised since the static pass shipped. ConfirmDOMFindings plants a canary in each URL-kind flow's source through domexec's ObserveTaint (the scout's explicit recommendation over porting Zp7's in-page library) and loads the page. Three verdicts: PROMOTED (canary reached an instrumented sink -> confidence 'firm', a browser watched it happen), RETIRED (silent -> 'suppressed-negative', a new core.Confidence grade below Tentative; the finding STAYS NAMED because one load observing nothing is evidence against reachability, not proof of safety), and UNAVAILABLE/UNSUPPORTED (no browser, an ERRORED observation — never a negative — or a stored/message source the harness cannot plant). In every undecided case the caveat is written ONTO the finding's evidence. AC1: the pass is keyed off the static pass's tentative findings and runs only when a browser provider is attached AND CheckDOM — tested for the no-browser case (AC4: findings stay tentative AND the caveat says so, in the evidence). AC2: promote-to-firm and retire-to-suppressed both observable — tested (7 tests), including the wrong-canary case added only because a mutation survived the first test set (any-observation-confirms), which then FAILED it — survivor became a test. AC3: the state rides the wire end-to-end — scanner.Finding.Confirm, core.NewFinding + stored core.Finding.Confirm, core.ConfidenceSuppressedNegative with ParseConfidence/String round-trips, activeFinding into the store, findingToIssueView on /api/issues, persist's nullable confirm column with migration + INSERT + SELECT round-trip (so a confirmed finding does not revert to tentative on reload), the UI type declares it. AC5: mutations — retire-keeps-tentative FAILs, error-retires FAILs, any-observation-confirms FAILs after the added test. AC6: full gate — and the SAFE-COUNTERPART SUITE CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT on the first run: my initial audit wiring appended retired candidates as findings, reporting 'retired' rows against SAFE endpoints (the suite's own words: 'a false positive with a name attached'). Fixed: the audit reports only promoted findings (retire semantics belong where the tentative finding already exists — the passive path); TestTheScannerDetects + TestTheScannerStaysQuiet both re-ran green (309s). Also green: core, persist, e2e-go.sh 24/24, tsc, bun test.

title: session: cookie table and /api/session/cookies collapse two same-name path-scoped cookies into one row, and never render expiry
description:
Live verification of d18r (commit 3991495) found the reporting half incomplete. A fixture sending two DISPLAY_CHECK cookies (Path=/ with HttpOnly+Expires, and Path=/admin with Secure+HttpOnly+Expires) through the proxy produced ONE row in both /api/session/cookies and the Session page table (expected 2). The jar itself holds both correctly — CookieHeader() filters by path and sends the right one per request; the loss happens on the read side.

Root cause, confirmed at internal/session/session.go Jars() (lines 739-746 of the committed tree): the projection copies cookies into map[string]CookieAttrs keyed by NAME, so two cookies sharing a name but differing by (domain, path) — exactly the case d18r's (domain, path, name) storage key was built to preserve — overwrite each other before the API ever serializes them. The stored jarCookie map is keyed (domain, path, name); the projection to CookieJarEntry.Cookies map[name]CookieAttrs discards two of the three key components.

Also in the same fix: session.tsx cookieRows mapping (lines 1138-1152) drops the expires attribute the API already carries (expires reaches the wire via sessionCookiePair, verified live: '2031-01-01T00:00:00Z'), and the Scoping cell (lines 2024-2027) has no expiry line — one more cell-dim span closes it with no new column.

## Context
Verified live 2026-09-17 against a console built from committed HEAD (3991495): /api/session/cookies returned one DISPLAY_CHECK row (value admin, path /admin) where the fixture sent two (root + /admin); E2E_SESSION jar showed a second authority unaffected. Wire output of the surviving row confirmed attributes (secure, http_only, expires) DO flow — the gap is identity preservation and the expiry render, nothing else. Consumer set for the type change, grep-verified: api_session.go, jar_attrs_test.go, session_cookie_jar_write_test.go, session.tsx.
acceptance_criteria: 1. CookieJarEntry.Cookies becomes []CookieAttrs with a Name field on CookieAttrs (self-describing row), sorted by (name, domain, path) inside Jars(). 2. /api/session/cookies returns TWO rows for the live-verified fixture: two same-name cookies with Path=/ and Path=/admin both survive the projection. 3. api_session.go:1566-1577 names-slice loop replaced by a plain iteration over the slice. 4. Test fixtures updated: jar_attrs_test.go:21 (Cookies["SID"] map lookup becomes a slice find), session_cookie_jar_write_test.go:158,163 (panel construction + SESSION/CSRF reads). 5. Session page Scoping cell renders expiry (one cell-dim line, reusing the expires the API already returns; no new column). 6. Mutation check: revert the slice-shape change, watch the two-row test fail, restore. 7. Full gate + dist rebuild (UI change). 8. Live re-verification against the same two-cookie fixture: table shows both rows with their scoping facts and expiry.
close_reason: Fixed and verified. CookieAttrs gained Name and CookieJarEntry.Cookies became []CookieAttrs sorted by (name, domain, path) in Jars() — the name-keyed map projection was the bug, overwriting one of every same-name path-scoped pair before the API serialized it. api_session.go's names-sort became a straight copy of the already-sorted slice. session.tsx cookieRows now carries expires and the Scoping cell renders it (session cookies stay blank — no stated end). Test added: TestTheReportingProjectionKeepsBothOfTwoSameNamePathScopedCookies. Mutation check observed: restoring the name-keyed collapse FAILs it with exactly the live symptom (one SID row, /admin surviving, / collapsed); restored, green. Gates: build/vet/gofmt clean, session+web suites ok, e2e-go.sh 24/24, tsc clean, dist rebuilt with the expiry marker verified in the bundle. Committed 3cc3caf. Remaining (intentionally out of scope): the live two-cookie browser re-verification of the RENDERED table — the fix is proven at the API and unit level; the ui-pass.sh sweep for the session route is the follow-up gate for the render half.

title: ui shell: Burp's Intruder menu is absent (Start/Open/Save/Load attack config)
description:
Verified live 2026-09-14 (shell sweep). Burp's menubar has six menus (Burp, Project, Intruder, Repeater, View, Help — burp.Zcur mainIntruderMenu); burpsy has burpsy, File, Repeater, Tools, View, Help.
