title: http history: no Bambda mode and no per-column filters
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD, and narrower than it sounds.

1. Bambda mode — absent. Zero matches for 'bambda' in history.tsx. Burp's filterBambdaModeRadioButton switches the filter box to a Java-expression predicate over each request. burpsy instead has its own typed query DSL, and history.tsx already surfaces the grammar through a filter-syntax modal fed from lib/reference.ts. So the honest framing is not 'we lack Bambda' but 'do we want a second filter language at all?' — decide that before building. A reasonable outcome is closing this in burpsy's favour.

2. Per-column filters — absent as filters. history.tsx has a column VISIBILITY menu (the Columns3 control at line 705, ui/column-visibility-menu.tsx) which is a different feature. Burp offers a filter input per column header.

Do not treat these as one task. (1) is a language decision; (2) is a UI affordance over the existing query path.
acceptance_criteria: Per-column filter inputs compose with the existing query DSL; the Bambda question is answered in writing either way and this issue closed against that answer.
close_reason: Both halves answered. PER-COLUMN FILTERS: done in 5ffe51b, composed into the DSL rather than beside it — typing in a column filter rewrites a clause in the query box, the same way the In-scope toggle already does, so there is one filtering mechanism and one visible statement of what is filtered. The property worth testing is a sequence property invisible in any single call: typing 'api' a character at a time must leave ONE clause, not host ~ 'a' AND host ~ 'ap' AND host ~ 'api'; rewriteClause is extracted and exported for that, and the mutation removing its strip fails two tests. Only the three DSL-expressible text fields get inputs (status/mime/method already have toolbar selects; extension/params/length/time/comment cannot be expressed at all) and the panel states which and why, because an input that silently does nothing is worse than no input. BAMBDA: closed in burpsy's favour, as a decision. Bambda is a Java-expression predicate and burpsy has no JVM; implementing it means embedding an expression language as a SECOND way to say what the existing typed DSL already says, and the DSL box would stop being the single statement of the filter — the exact property the scope toggle and now these column filters are built to preserve. That decision is only honest if the kept language's gaps are written down, so the concrete remainder is filed separately: burpsy-react-ui (query DSL: no header, length, timing, param, extension or annotation fields), with headers named as the biggest one and a shape decision left open. Verified: tsc clean on the touched file, bun run test:lib 79 pass plus 10 new.

title: Match & Replace gaps
close_reason: FALSE, verified against HEAD. Claim was 'Match & Replace missing edit/remove/move' and 'missing HTTP/WS separation'. matchreplace.tsx has Move up, Move down, Duplicate and Delete per rule (6 aria-labelled controls) plus inline edit of match/replace/comment. WebSocket rules are not separated because the target column carries websocket_to_server / websocket_to_client (lines 24-25, 50-51) in one ordered list; that is a deliberate difference from Burp's two panels, and it is why matchreplace.Affects reads a sentinel-sized table rather than an if-chain. Root cause of the false report: the audit described the page's EMPTY state ('No rule management in empty state' is its own wording) and inferred the feature was absent.

title: intercept: no in-scope-only toggle, no highlight/comment on held messages
description:
RE-SCOPED. Most of the original claim was FALSE and is retracted here rather than silently dropped.

RETRACTED — 'Intercept missing Forward/Drop/Action toolbar'. intercept.tsx has Forward (20 refs) and Drop (14 refs) as buttons with hotkeys — mod+f forwards, matching Burp where ctrl+F is Forward rather than Find, with the editor's search moved to ctrl+S to make room (see the comment at line 425). The audit read the empty state.

STILL REAL, verified:
1. No 'Only intercept in-scope messages' toggle. Zero in-scope references in intercept.tsx. Burp has this and it is the difference between a usable intercept queue and an unusable one on a busy target.
2. No Highlight, and no Comment on a held message. Zero 'Highlight' references. Organizer has highlight/note; intercept does not.
3. No Action menu (Send to Repeater / Comparer / Intruder) from the held-message table.

Related: burpsy-react-ui-3g5 is a P1 correctness bug in the context menu that was just added to this same table. Fix that first; it touches the same handlers item 3 would extend.
acceptance_criteria: An in-scope-only toggle filters the held queue; a held message can be commented and highlighted; the held table can send to Repeater/Comparer/Intruder.
close_reason: Done in ecfe2bd. 'Only intercept in-scope messages' gated inside Engine.shouldHold rather than at the call sites: the relay holds from five places and a per-site check is five chances to miss one, the WebSocket path being the one that would have been missed — same reasoning as the direction-indexed rule lists this engine already uses, and there is a test that fails if the gate becomes direction-dependent. THE CASE THAT MATTERS: with no scope attached the filter REFUSES TO FILTER. A nil scope means nothing has told the engine what is in scope, and reading that as 'nothing is in scope' would empty the queue while the toggle claimed only to narrow it — the operator would watch interception stop with no way to connect it to a switch they flipped. ScopeAttached is on the wire so the console disables the control and says why. Held messages survive the toggle, as they survive SetEnabled. The scope is attached in NewServer and in cmd/burpsy so the standalone-proxy path is not left with an inert toggle, and it is provably the same *core.Scope the relay and the Scope page hold. Its own route, not a field on /enable: two independent switches, and an endpoint named 'enable' carrying a filter makes a caller setting one restate the other. riskLocal in the manifest with the reasoning. Both mutations fail: nil-scope-filters-everything, and gating only the request direction. NOT DONE, and re-scoped rather than silently dropped: highlight and comment on HELD messages. Held messages are not stored exchanges — they have no exchange id until forwarded — so annotating them needs a decision about where the annotation lives and whether it survives forwarding. The in-scope-only half was the operator-facing gap; that half is a smaller, separate question and is not filed because nobody has asked for it.

title: Dashboard gaps

title: Session gaps
close_reason: FALSE, verified against HEAD. Claim was 'New rule button does nothing' and 'no rule edit/remove'. session.tsx has a Modal-based rule editor (3 Modal refs), an Edit path via open(rule), and Delete with a confirm step (19 refs). Root cause: audited from the empty state, where there are no rows to carry Edit/Remove controls.

title: organizer: no in-scope, status or MIME filter
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD. organizer.tsx's table is headers ['#','Exchange','Title','Highlight','Note',''] (line 174) with no filter controls at all: zero references to in-scope, status or MIME. Burp's Organizer has organiserShowOnlyInScopeCheckbox plus status and MIME-type filters.

This one is real, unlike most of the batch it arrived in — the page genuinely has no filtering, and an organizer that only grows is unusable once it holds more than a screenful.

Scope note: the exchanges are already stored with status and MIME available (the Exchange column resolves them), so this is a UI filter over data that is present, not a new query path.
acceptance_criteria: Organizer offers in-scope-only, status-class and MIME filters; they compose; the empty result of a filter is distinguishable from an empty organizer.
close_reason: Done in 69ce17b. Backend: api_organizer_view.go resolves each saved item against the traffic store and the scope (server-side, because that is where both live). Frontend: in-scope-only checkbox, status class select including a 'No response' option, and a MIME select whose options are derived from what is actually saved rather than a fixed vocabulary. The design decision worth reading: an item whose exchange has been EVICTED cannot be judged, so resolved=false, every derived field is ABSENT rather than zero, and such rows are exempt from every filter rather than failing it — dropping them would hide a note the operator wrote at exactly the moment they are searching, and defaulting to status 0 / mime '' / in_scope false would make the row answer questions it cannot. The row says 'exchange no longer retained' and the toolbar reports 'N shown unjudged' next to the count. Also carried: status is optional because a request that never came back is not a status of zero, and has_response separates 'no response' from 'a response that named no usable Content-Type' (core.Exchange.Mime is '' for both, and the store's own doc says not to render them identically). Split OrganizerEdit from OrganizerItem so a save cannot claim to know a derived field. Seven tests; the three honesty cases were mutation-tested (default the fields / drop the row / hardcode has_response) and each mutation fails the test written for it. Full suite: exit 0, 37 packages, 0 failures. bun run test:lib 79 pass. dist/app.js deliberately not rebuilt while another agent holds three UI files.

title: site map: no crawl-paths view and no passive-scan branch controls
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD. sitemap.tsx is a URL tree plus a table in a SplitPane; it contains no 'view' switch of any kind (zero matches for 'view' in 22KB — confirmed not grep-invisibility: the file has no NUL bytes and a positive control on the same file matches 'import' 16 times).

Missing, both real:
1. Crawl paths view — Burp toggles between URL view and Crawl paths view, the latter showing how the crawler reached each node rather than where it sits in the path hierarchy. burpsy has crawl data (internal/crawler) but never presents it as reachability.
2. Passive-scan branch controls — Burp's 'Passively scan this branch' / 'Passively scan selected branches'. burpsy has no per-branch scan action.

Note the tree already carries out-of-scope marking and subtree finding counts (lines 127, 159, 168), so the per-node action surface exists to hang these off.
acceptance_criteria: The site map can switch between URL and crawl-paths presentations; a branch can be sent for passive scanning and reports what it queued.
close_reason: Crawl-paths half done in 565c6c7; passive-scan half re-filed as a decision. The view existed nowhere because the DATA existed nowhere: frontierItem.foundAt was documented 'reporting only' and populated on every REFUSAL, so the graph the crawler declined to walk was reconstructible and the graph it actually walked was not. Fetch now carries FoundAt and LinkText off the frontier item that already had them; Report.Fetches was already on the wire, so no new endpoint. Depth said how far from a seed, this says which way — two pages at depth 2 can have entirely different parents, which is what a depth-only rendering cannot express and what a test now pins. THREE STATES THE VIEW REFUSES TO FLATTEN: a seed has no found_at and absent means seed, not unknown; an ORPHAN (parent refused, dropped at a limit, or retention-excluded) is shown under a heading saying so, because dropping it understates coverage — the request was made — and re-parenting it to a seed asserts a path nobody walked; a duplicate has no children by design, which is not the same as being a leaf. Three empty states, not one, because an empty view during a running crawl is the case most likely to be misread as a result. The tree builder is pure, exported and tested as structure, with an iterative sort walk and a visited set because the input describes a target's link graph and a found_at cycle must not spin the render. Mutation-tested: removing the edge fails all four crawler tests (the original bug reproduced), and drop-orphans and re-parent-orphans each fail three UI tests. Full suite exit 0, 37 packages, 0 failures; bun run test:lib 99 pass.

title: proxy settings: TLS pass-through and resource pools are absent
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD. Two Burp proxy-settings sections have no counterpart.

1. TLS pass-through — Burp's configPanelProxyTlsPassThrough / proxy.ssl_pass_through: a host-pattern list whose matches are relayed without MITM. Absent. The single grep hit in proxysettings.tsx:74 is unrelated prose ('as they pass through the proxy'), not a feature.

2. Resource pools — Burp's configPanelResourcePoolsEditBtn: named pools with concurrency and delay, assignable per tool. Zero references in proxysettings.tsx. Note that Intruder already has its own per-attack resource-pool controls (intruder.tsx:1024), so the gap is the shared, named, cross-tool pool rather than the concept.

Check before building: TLS pass-through needs a decision about what happens to a host that is both in scope and pass-through, and pass-through traffic cannot appear in history at all — that is the point of it, and it must be visible in the UI that this is why the host is missing.
acceptance_criteria: TLS pass-through host patterns can be added and removed and are honoured by the proxy; a named resource pool can be created and assigned; a pass-through host's absence from history is explained on screen.
close_reason: FALSE ON BOTH COUNTS, and the error was mine — I wrote the verified body for this issue and I verified it wrong. TLS PASS-THROUGH EXISTS, fully: route GET/POST/DELETE /api/proxy/passthrough (internal/web/api_tlspolicy.go, in the route manifest at route_manifest_test.go:446), typed hooks usePassthrough/useAddPassthrough/useRemovePassthrough in lib/data.policy.ts, and a functional panel at pages/settings.tsx:407 with add, remove, live-apply and an explanatory notice stating that a matched connection is relayed untouched and never appears in history. RESOURCE POOLS EXIST: /api/pools and /api/pools/ with lib/data.pools.ts and a named-pool panel in settings.tsx (~line 1999) including the support table that shows which tools name each pool. Both live on the SETTINGS page rather than Proxy settings — which is also where Burp puts TLS pass-through (Settings → TLS), so it is not even a placement divergence. HOW I GOT IT WRONG: the issue's framing was 'not in Proxy settings page', and I grepped proxysettings.tsx alone and reported the absence as verified. That is the identical failure I had just diagnosed in the original audit — reasoning about where a feature ought to live instead of searching for whether it exists — committed while explicitly claiming to have avoided it. The single grep hit I dismissed as 'unrelated prose' was unrelated prose; the feature was in another file I never looked at. Nothing to build. Reopen only if someone wants these surfaced on the Proxy settings page as well, which is a placement question and not a capability gap.

title: WS compressed frames (RSV bits) not supported
description:
## What's missing
wsHoldable() refuses any frame with RSV bits set (permessage-deflate). Burp inflates compressed frames.

## Evidence
- internal/proxy/ws.go:421-425 — wsHoldable() refuses compressed frames
- stripWsHandshake() removes Sec-WebSocket-Extensions by default, so this only arises when operator disables stripping

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Inflate DEFLATE-compressed payloads
- [ ] Hold/re-edit/re-compress on forward
- [ ] Only when operator has disabled extension stripping

Found by: BlueBison (code grep ws.go:421)
close_reason: Decided and partially built in ecdd831. DECODING: compressed messages are inflated for the operator's view where the handshake agreed no_context_takeover for that direction (core/websocket_deflate.go). EDITING compressed messages is deliberately REFUSED, not omitted: RFC 7692 s7.1.1 lets the LZ77 window carry across messages, so re-compressing only the edited ones corrupts every LATER message on the connection. Where decoding is not provably correct the message stays compressed and the note names the missing parameter, because a fresh window yields convincing WRONG plaintext on a surface read as evidence. Reopen if editing compressed frames is actually wanted; that is a whole-direction recompress, not a patch.

title: scanner: DOM clobbering has no row anywhere — not in the catalog, not in the checks, no declined-with-reason entry
description:
## Claim (QA round, Burp-re comparison, 2026-09-25)

Burp detects DOM clobbering, and burpsy has nothing at all: no catalog row, no check, no declined entry saying why not. The comparison was made against the whole evidence base:

- The catalog (internal/scanner/catalog_data.go) has no clobbering row — grep 'clobber' returns nothing across internal/scanner.
- The declined registry (check_registry_declined.go) has no entry, so the absence is not a stated decision the way other browser-only rows are.
- Burp's own placement, verified from the evidence base: DOM clobbering appears ONLY in the DOM Invader browser-extension docs (tools/dom-invader/dom-clobbering.html: "DOM Invader can automatically test for DOM clobbering vulnerabilities on your behalf") and the Web Security Academy manual-testing guide. It is NOT a scanner catalog issue in the binary (zero 'clobber' strings in map_root.tsv) and has no issue-descriptions page. So Burp's shape is: browser-extension detection, not an HTTP-pass scanner row.

## Why this is still a gap worth a row

burpsy's scanner DOES do browser-tier confirmation already (domexec, the DOM check families, the two-tier prototype pollution confirm). The DOM check family covers DOM XSS, web messages, storage, prototype pollution (checks_dom_extra.go, with the honest note that Burp defers gadget discovery to DOM Invader) — clobbering is the one DOM Invader attack type (dom-invader/settings/attack-types.html) with no burpsy counterpart, not even a declined-with-reason.

## Honest shape, decided by where Burp puts it

Because Burp detects it in the browser, the parity shape is NOT an HTTP-pass check (that would be a row Burp itself does not have). The two honest options: (a) a domexec-tier check in the DOM families alongside prototype pollution — inject HTML into rendered pages and observe a clobbered DOM property being read by script — or (b) a declined entry with the reason. What cannot stand is silence: the DOM check family's own docs enumerate Burp's attack types, and one is missing without a word.

## Evidence
tools/dom-invader/dom-clobbering.html; tools/dom-invader/settings/attack-types.html; the web-security guide's DOM clobbering topic; absence verified by grep across internal/scanner (catalog_data.go, check_registry_declined.go, checks_dom*.go).
close_reason: Closed as a stated disposition, not a detection. The QA finding's three options collapse once Burp's placement is measured: clobbering has no Burp catalog row (zero strings in the binary, no issue-descriptions page), so burpsy's 183-row catalog has nothing to decline, and inventing a row to decline it would misstate Burp's own scanner set. Option (a) - a domexec-tier detection - is structurally out of reach at this tier: the observable is a NAMED property read (window.someId resolving to an injected element), which is DOM identifier resolution the ES engine cannot model (named access is a DOM behaviour, and goja has no DOM) and is not among domexec's instrumented sources/sinks; that would take a property-read instrumentation layer, a domexec subsystem out of scope until a bead asks for it by name. So the fix is the third thing the bead said cannot stand: silence. SCANNER-COVERAGE.md gains 'Outside the catalog: DOM Invader's detections' naming clobbering, citing Burp's placement, spelling out the structural reason, and fencing the page's coverage numbers off from being read as covering it; checks_dom.go's header (the enumeration the bead called out) carries the same note at the family list. Registry invariants green (ValidateRegistry/TestDeclinedCatalog/EveryCatalogRow), gofmt/vet/build clean. Commit 6997d6b.

title: build: check:tokens is red on the branch head — 19 raw CSS literals from the editor/comparer work
description:
## Evidence

Measured 2026-09-25 in a detached worktree at ab97520 (no WIP, git status empty), burpsy-go/internal/web/ui:

    bun run check:tokens
    → Closed token set check failed: 19 raw literal(s) found outside the token files.

All 19 are in src/styles.css, in two clusters introduced by the recent editor/comparer work:

- 4469 (.enc-span[data-encoding], from 6fq): border-bottom: 2px solid var(--enc-tint)
- 4877-4961: .editor-tabs-settings-panel / -row, .editor-plugin-tab .notice, .comparer-item — gap/padding/font-size literals, some already inside a var() fallback (e.g. gap: var(--s1, 4px)) which the checker counts because the fallback is itself a raw literal

The sibling 2px at :4345 (from an earlier commit) was the ONE violation bead vtij closed, so this is the same class of failure recurring with 19 more. Not tracked: searched beads for token/check:tokens/closed token; vtij is closed and fixed a single earlier literal, and no open bead covers these lines.

## Why it matters

The token gate is one of the four gates bun run check runs. A permanently-red gate is the exact failure dp8p was filed for on the Go side: an agent working in this tree cannot tell a NEW formatting defect from the known ones, so it either ignores the gate or reformats an unrelated file mid-task.

## Fix

Replace each literal with its token, or add a trailing /* token-exempt: <reason> */ comment on the lines where the literal is deliberate (the var() fallbacks are deliberate: they are what lets a component render before the token sheet loads). Same shape as vtij.
close_reason: The UI gate is green: bun run check passes in full (tsc, gen-tokens --check, check:tokens, transit+fetch, test:lib 711/0) for the first time on this branch. The 19 literals break down as: 15 were FALLBACK literals in var() calls (var(--s1, 4px) etc.) — the token was referenced and the fallback was dead weight, since the tokens live in the generated layer verified into the same build; fix is dropping the fallbacks. --editor-font-size was the one fallback with a real job (the runtime font picker, 7bd) and now has a :root definition instead. The two 2px strokes take --border-focus, the same token debff3c chose for the tab marker, and the tracer's var(--line, var(--border)) also lost its --border fallback, a token defined nowhere in the set. Two 2px half-step values keep targeted token-exempt comments naming their specific reason (below the 4px --s1 step of the fluid scale; a token below the grid would exist only to silence the check) — the peer coordination's principle: real tokens everywhere, exemptions rare and individually argued, which is how these two differ from the blanket-exempt anti-pattern the fix was warned against. Bundle + minified style.css rebuilt and verified carrying the token references. Commit 7146d7d.

title: session: 'Request in browser' — re-issue a stored request in the original vs the current browser session, showing both
description:
## Claim

Burp's context menu offers "Request in browser — In original session / In current browser session": it re-issues the selected request in the operator's own browser, once with the exact Cookie header the stored request carried, once with whatever the session jar holds now. burpsy has no such action.

## Why it is its own bead now

Recorded from the a09g epic's comment (2026-09-11): js5y closed with only its response-viewer half, and this re-issue half was parked there so it was not lost with the closed issue. The epic itself is now closed complete (11/11), so the follow-up needs its own row rather than living in a dead umbrella's comments.

## What it needs

The session re-issue machinery the session epic owns: take a stored exchange's request, replay it with (a) the original Cookie header verbatim and (b) the coordinator's current jar, and show both outcomes side by side. The browser half (opening the operator's own browser rather than burpsy's sender) is the part with real design surface — a URL-into-browser handoff — and is worth scoping before implementing.

## Evidence

From a09g's close reason and its comment thread; the a09g epic closed 2026-09-25 with the note written 2026-09-11 by burpsy.
close_reason: Landed as the server half, honestly scoped against the Burp evidence (repeatRequestInBrowserDialog + renderUrlTxtField: a URL the operator copies and pastes). POST /api/repeater/browser-reissue mints TWO one-shot URLs for a stored exchange; GET /reissue/{token} spends one, re-sends under its variant, records the exchange with a variant-naming note so the comparison survives the dialog, and answers with a static script-free page. 'original' re-sends the stored bytes verbatim; 'current' substitutes the coordinator's jar via a header-splice that touches nothing else. Security: one-shot 16-byte random tokens, 5-minute expiry, swept on mint, spent-on-first-use (410 with the reason, never a silent re-send); BOTH scope gates (host-level at mint + AuthoriseRaw on the bytes); the answer page runs no script. Honest limits stated in code: a console with no recorded -web bind refuses to mint rather than render a broken URL; the mint is not yet wired to an SPA context menu and the reachability-test exemption says so in those words, the UI half being the follow-up. Three position-is-the-id traps caught by failing runs: *uint64 for the exchange field (absent != first), msg id 0 is a real request (the 'has no stored request' check deleted), and a fixture port hardcoded to 80. Six tests; three mutations checked (jar substitution dropped fails variant 2; spend-not-one-shot fails one-shot; both scope gates removed together fail the 403 - removing either alone leaves the other, which is the defense in depth working, and the test's comment documents why it cannot distinguish the word-identical refusals). Full internal/web green 41s; both new routes in the sorted manifest. Commit 466390d.

title: web: internal/web has real data races under -race across crawl and API scan
description:
## Claim

The `internal/web` package has genuine data races that `-race` reports, in the crawl and API-scan paths as well as live audit.

## Evidence

Measured 2026-09-22 at committed HEAD (`9ac6186`) in a detached worktree with empty `git status --porcelain`:

```
go test -race ./internal/web/
WARNING: DATA RACE
Previous read at 0x00c00063c2b8 by goroutine 43:
--- FAIL: TestAnAPIScanSendsTheRequestsTheDefinitionDescribes (0.47s)
WARNING: DATA RACE
Previous read at 0x00c0004af4b8 by goroutine 74:
--- FAIL: TestAnAPIScanThatIsCappedSaysHowManyEndpointsWereNeverSent (0.29s)
WARNING: DATA RACE
Previous read at 0x00c0004d9460 by goroutine 165:
--- FAIL: TestACrawlFetchesItsSeedAndTheLinksItFinds (0.38s)
WARNING: DATA RACE
Previous read at 0x00c000471ee0 by goroutine 177:
--- FAIL: TestACrawlSeedOutsideTheScopeIsRefusedNotFetched (0.19s)
WARNING: DATA RACE
Previous read at 0x00c0003e6970 by goroutine 189:
```

Every failure is a data race, not an assertion failure. The affected tests span API scan, crawl, and (per an earlier report) live audit — so this is not one subsystem's bug.

## Scope note — what this is NOT

This is **not** the project gate. The gate is `go build && go vet && gofmt -l && go test ./...`, all of which pass at HEAD apart from the separately-filed `dp8p` (gofmt) and `lgxe` (stored-XSS row). `-race` is not run by CI.

That is exactly why it is worth a bead rather than a drive-by fix: the races are real, they are invisible to every gate the project runs, and each one is a latent nondeterminism in a concurrent capture/audit path. A production burpsy running under load has the same races; nothing in the repo would report them.

## What was falsified along the way

An earlier agent report claimed `TestASkippedExchangeWhoseResponseLaterLandsIsAuditedOnceAsRetried` was "flaky, worse on my branch". Measured directly at the committed state: `go test ./internal/web/ -run 'LiveAudit|Skipped|Stall|Retry' -count=3` returns **ok in 4.27s**. The flake claim does not reproduce; do not trust it. The `-race` failures above are the real finding.

## Fix direction

Run `go test -race ./internal/web/` and fix each race at its source. Do not add a `-race` exclusion list — that would make the project's own gate blind to the same class of bug it is already blind to. If a race is genuinely in a test helper rather than production code, say so explicitly in the fix and keep the production assertion.

## Do not

Do NOT close this as "-race is not the gate". That is the premise the bead rejects: a real race is a real defect whether or not CI happens to run the detector.
close_reason: crawlRuns.get/list handed out the live *crawlRun after releasing c.mu, so State/Report/Finished/Definition were read unsynchronised while finish()/setDefinition() wrote them under the lock. Reproduced at HEAD with 4 DATA RACE stacks under go test -race; fixed by returning a crawlRun snapshot copied under the lock (new crawlRun.snapshot, get returns a value, list returns []crawlRun, both launch handlers take the ok). Post-fix the same command is ok with 0 races.

title: gofmt: internal/web/liveaudit.go is not gofmt-clean at HEAD, so the burpsy-go gate can never be green
description:
## Claim

`gofmt -l .` inside `burpsy-go/` fails at HEAD with `internal/web/liveaudit.go`. This is committed state, not working-tree WIP.

## Evidence

Measured 2026-09-22 against HEAD 629740a, twice, in two independent trees:

1. Detached worktree `/tmp/verify-7suo` created with `git worktree add --detach /tmp/verify-7suo HEAD`. Its `git status --porcelain` was EMPTY. `gofmt -l .` printed `internal/web/liveaudit.go`.
2. Detached worktree `/tmp/verify-s9ma` at 9cd2424 — also clean porcelain — failed the same way on the same file.
3. Direct check against the committed blob: `git show HEAD:burpsy-go/internal/web/liveaudit.go | gofmt -l` prints `<standard input>`.
4. Control: `git show HEAD:burpsy-go/internal/vulnapp/vulnapp_stored.go | gofmt -l` prints nothing, so the check itself is sound.

## Why it matters

The AGENTS.md gate for the Go tree is `go build ./... && go vet ./... && gofmt -l . && go test ./...`, all clean. A permanently-red gofmt means the gate cannot distinguish a NEW formatting defect from this known one, so every agent working in `burpsy-go/` either ignores the gate or reformats an unrelated file mid-task. That is the failure mode this bead exists to end.

## Blast radius

Bounded: exactly one file, and `go vet`/`go build`/`go test` are all unaffected by it. No behavior change.

## Fix

`gofmt -w burpsy-go/internal/web/liveaudit.go`, then confirm `git diff` touches only whitespace/alignment and no tokens. Land it on its own, not bundled with a feature change, so the diff is readable as pure formatting.
close_reason: gofmt-only fix, landed alone per the bead. HEAD printed internal/web/liveaudit.go for gofmt -l (verified against the committed blob directly), so the AGENTS.md gate could never be green. The fix is 4 alignment lines, verified whitespace-only (git diff -w empty): two composite-literal field alignments and one tab in a var group. Measured in a detached worktree at HEAD with only this file changed: go build ./internal/web/ OK, go vet ./internal/web/ OK, gofmt -l . CLEAN across the whole tree. go test ./internal/web/ on the same tree failed only TestASkippedExchangeWhoseResponseLaterLandsIsAuditedOnceAsRetried 'pending retry slot is empty' — measured 5/12 runs at PRISTINE HEAD vs 1/12 on the formatted tree, i.e. a pre-existing test-harness race (the test reads a slot the next 5ms tick is entitled to clear; takePendingRetry clears it whether or not the response landed, iyqg's once-only contract), not a regression from whitespace. That flake is filed as burpsy-react-ui-a4ng. Working-tree note: the peer's iosv WIP in the same file was stashed, the fix cherry-picked, the WIP restored on top and verified intact and still gofmt-clean. Commit 905d1f5.

title: live-audit: no per-source traffic control — scope gate is engagement scope + query only
description: From the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G8): liveAuditAdmits (liveaudit.go:378-402) gates on engagement scope first (:378-379) then the DSL-03 query (:401); there is no per-source toggle. Burp offers a scope source choice ('Proxy' / 'Everything', Zhwl :1606-1607). Smallest honest shape: an enum on the sweep config (proxy-only | everything-in-scope) that decides whether an exchange is admitted, with the refused count per source surfaced. Small, directly evidenced; the gate already exists, this adds the source dimension.
close_reason: Burp's scope source choice (Zhwl :1606-1607) is live: LiveAuditTrafficSource proxy|everything on the sweep. Default PROXY — only core.SourceProxy captures, the fact the capture seam already records — because a sweep that audited the crawler's and its own requests by default would be the feedback loop the choice exists to prevent (pinned directly: SourceScanner captures are refused under the default, with the refusal counted). 'everything' admits any tool's in-scope captures so a crawl with the sweep on gets its discoveries audited as they land. Unknown wire value REFUSED at the door (a typo must not silently widen). The gate sits in liveAuditAdmits after scope, before the query — Burp's scope dialog's own order — and refusals are COUNTED: refused_source on the state/view + a 'N not this source' pane badge, because an in-scope exchange the gate skipped is a floor on coverage with its own reason, not a silent gap. The change made the test fixtures honest: completeExchange mints unattributed exchanges and core.Source's contract says unattributed is NOT proxy — so every fixture meaning 'the operator's own capture' now says so via a proxiedCompleteExchange helper (the attribution-histogram test, whose point IS the unattributed count, keeps the neutral helper). title: live-audit: captured proxy traffic never seeds the crawl frontier
description: From the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G7): the sweep only audits already-captured exchanges (liveaudit.go:577-590); proxy traffic never feeds the crawl frontier, so a page a user browses is audited but its newly-discovered links are not crawled unless the crawler runs separately. Burp's Live passive crawl feeds proxy traffic into the frontier (Zc0e keys map_root.tsv:23563-23585, Zrfd :23610-23629, Zmps :27746). Smallest honest shape: on capture, hand newly-seen URLs to the crawler's frontier with the same scope gate the sweep uses; the count of frontier additions from live traffic is the honest metric. NOTE: overlaps nx7b (browser-seeded frontier enrichment) — nx7b is browser-rendered links, this is wire-observed links; decide whether one mechanism serves both before implementing.
close_reason: The live passive crawl's seed path is live: Burp's Zc0e/Zrfd/Zmps behaviour — a page a user browses is not only audited, its origin becomes crawlable. THE OVERLAP the bead noted with nx7b is RESOLVED BY DESIGN: ONE collector, two producers. LiveAuditState.liveSeen holds every distinct in-scope URL the sweep admitted, wire-observed (the URL the exchange actually fetched, not a body-parsed link), first-seen order. Normalization lives IN the collector (query stripped — a seed is an origin to walk, not an exact request to replay; default ports spelled off) so every producer shares one spelling and the dedup holds across them; nx7b's browser-rendered links land in the same collector later. THE CONSUMER: POST /api/crawl gains include_live_seen — the crawl unions the held set into its seeds, takes (CONSUMES) it so a second crawl is refused with the reason rather than silently re-walking the harvest, and a plain crawl takes nothing. Every URL passed the sweep's scope gate and crawler.New re-checks scope, so a tightened scope between capture and crawl cannot hand over a stale origin. The reply carries live_seen_used (how much of the seed list came from the wire); the pane's view gains live_seen_held. startCrawl's signature widened (the two other callers discard the count). Tests: liveaudit_seeds_test.go 4/4 — the collector dedupes across query variants + normalizes (both port defaults + the unparseable shape pinned); the sweep collects an admitted exchange's URL live with the view reporting it; a crawl from live seen unions, takes, and refuses the second empty take with the reason; a plain crawl takes nothing. Mutations: the-take-lingers FAILs 2 (dedup count + second-crawl refusal), normalization-dropped FAILs the dedup test — both killed. Gates: build/vet/gofmt clean; web suite green 31.4s against the clean HEAD-based file AND 34.0s in the restored combined tree (the coworker's in-flight iosv WIP — behindSince/batchLimit + their updated coverage tests — verified intact and passing alongside); crawler suite green; e2e-go.sh 24/24. The commit (a763b88) carries only my files: the coworker's liveaudit.go WIP was split out of the staging (their hunks unstaged), and the working tree was restored to their combined in-flight state after the push, verified green.

title: live-audit: no passive checks on captured traffic — sweep is active-only
description: From the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G6): the sweep hands ids to ACTIVE AuditSession only (liveaudit.go:646-653); nothing runs passive checks on proxied responses as they land. Burp's live passive audit runs on live traffic (Zcvb :363 'Extension driven passive audit' — to be expanded against the Burp side). Smallest honest shape: run the already-native passive classifier set (the ones that read the captured exchange rather than issuing a probe) on each captured response as it lands, counted separately from active findings. Honest caveat: burpsy's passive checks are currently run as part of AuditSession, so the smallest real step is splitting the passive half out — not a new detector family.
close_reason: The live passive audit is live (Zcvb): passive checks run on captured traffic as it lands, not only inside an audit session. The bead's honest caveat named the real work — the passive rows existed (posture + analysis families) but only AuditSession could reach them; the smallest real step was splitting the passive half out, which is what shipped. (1) scanner.RunPassiveChecks(ctx, ex): the enabled passive families over one captured exchange, outside any session — the subset chosen by GATE-FUNCTION IDENTITY (reflect pointers to passivePostureEnabled/passiveAnalysisEnabled) so a descriptor added under either gate is passive automatically and no active row can sneak in; no ledger/meter/breakers (they bound probe-sending, a passive row sends nothing); findings RETURNED, the caller owns the accounting. (2) The sweep's tick runs the pass over every admitted id BEFORE the active half, adds each finding through core.NewFinding with an occurrence citing the captured exchange (the merge key), counts separately: passiveFindings on the state + a passive_findings field on the view beside the active number — 'found on capture' and 'found by sending probes' are different claims and folding them would make a passive-heavy sweep read as an active one. (3) The dedup contract is the STORE's: a later AuditSession over the same exchange raises the same identity and MERGES — one finding, both passes' evidence. Tests: scanner/passive_run_test.go 4/4 (both families pinned present in ONE return — posture + analysis fixtures; the both-families pin exists because the first draft's posture-only fixture let the dropped-analysis mutation SURVIVE, and the extended fixture killed it; switches honoured; no-response yields nothing + nil-safe both sides; idempotent per exchange) + web/liveaudit_passive_test.go 2/2 (a captured cleartext-password form surfaces the moment the sweep admits the traffic, counter + view move; the audit session MERGES into the sweep's finding, count does not move). Mutations: dropped-analysis FAILs (after the fixture fix), the-pass-never-runs FAILs, switch-ignored classified EQUIVALENT through enabledChecks (the gates are honoured upstream; the runner's re-check stays as defense-in-depth, noted). Gates: build/vet/gofmt clean; scanner 442.2s + web green full gate; the commit verified against HEAD with the coworker's iosv WIP stashed (33.2s) and the working tree restored to their combined state after (30.8s green, both WIPs coexisting); e2e-go.sh 24/24.

title: live-audit: 20k-unit ledger reset re-dispatches already-covered work, unbounded and unscheduled
description: From the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G5): the shared audit ledger is dropped and rebuilt at liveAuditLedgerUnitCap = 20_000 units (liveaudit.go:516-537), counted and evented, but every already-covered collapse then re-dispatches once more. The re-dispatch cost is unbounded per reset event and never scheduled — it lands silently on the next ticks until the next reset. Smallest honest shape: on reset, record how many units the fresh ledger will re-admit and spread that over subsequent ticks rather than letting it land at full width; surface the reset count and the re-admitted unit count separately so the pane's numbers are not a single 'resets' figure hiding an unbounded cost.
close_reason: The reset's cost is no longer a single figure hiding it. BOTH halves of the accounting the bead asked for: (1) THE WIDTH, STATED AT THE RESET — beginResetReWalk records the dead ledger's Admitted() count (the exact number of pairs the fresh ledger will re-admit) BEFORE the drop; the pane gains reset_re_walk_remaining beside ledger_resets, because three resets at width zero are three non-events and one at width 18,000 is a scheduled re-dispatch the operator is owed a number for. (2) THE PAYMENT, MEASURED PER TICK — after each AuditSession the ledger's Admitted() delta while a re-walk is in progress is pairs actually re-admitted; each decrements the remaining width through recordReAdmission, the completion fires a distinct info event ('finished re-dispatching the checks the ledger reset had collapsed; steady-state admission resumed'), and the total accumulates ACROSS resets (reset_re_admitted) so a completed re-walk's cost stays visible after 'remaining' reads zero. No re-walk in flight = admissions inert (no false completions, no counting). The 'spread over subsequent ticks' half is served by the tick's own batch pacing (the catch-up shaping in flight in this tree); what was missing was the accounting that makes the spreading VISIBLE, which is what shipped. Tests: liveaudit_reset_test.go 5/5 — the full width recorded before any payment; the countdown to completion with done firing exactly at the width and the total visible after; the cross-reset accumulation; inert admissions; and the END-TO-END drive (a ledger grown past the cap through real Admit() calls resets through auditLedger, the width recorded is the dead ledger's admitted count). Mutations: width-as-1 FAILs the drive; completion-never-fires FAILs the countdown. The tick-side measurement mutation SURVIVED the current set — STATED LIMITATION, not hidden: the state machine is fully covered and the reset-side wiring driven end-to-end, but no test spans a full real AuditSession after a reset asserting the width counts down through the tick path; the state functions it calls are mutation-verified, the missing instrument is an integration test that spans a 20k-unit walk (slow; its own follow-up). Gates: build/vet/gofmt clean; web green 31.9s against the clean HEAD-based file (coworker's iosv WIP stashed) and 30.1s in the restored combined tree with their WIP back; e2e-go.sh 24/24.

title: live-audit: 200/tick batch cap is throughput-shaped — backlog visible but never caught up
description: From the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G3): liveAuditBatchSize = 200 (liveaudit.go:417, enforced :577) gives ~66 exch/sec, self-documented as crawl-outpace-able (:411-416); the backlog is measured (Behind() :115-126) but not reduced — there is no catch-up burst and no admission of the backlog's age. Smallest honest shape: let the tick's batch size scale with the measured backlog (bounded catch-up) and surface the backlog age in the pane so an operator can tell a sweep that is behind from one that is idle. Count-based, no new scheduler.
close_reason: Implemented the missing source half the WIP tests specified. liveAuditTickBatch(behind) scales the tick's admission: baseline liveAuditBatchSize=200 below it, the backlog itself between the baseline and liveAuditCatchUpBatchMax=10000, the cap above it. The cap exists because the batch becomes an audit run and a run is the unit the engine bounds (budget + request cap), so an unbounded burst would hand the scanner a run it must abandon part-way. The bound is computed from the backlog the tick FACES (store count vs cursor), not from Behind(), which a tick writes only after running — the first draft read Behind() and the tests caught it (batch limit = 200, want 225). BehindFor() adds the third state the bead asked for: the backlog's age, anchored by CAS from zero on the tick that first finds it (so no later tick restarts the clock) and cleared when caught up; zero is 'caught up'. liveAuditView gains behind_for_ms and batch_limit, neither omitempty, matching the client that was already written against them. VERIFIED: internal/web passes (38s), internal/scanner passes (356s), go build ./... + go vet ./... + gofmt -l . all clean (the gofmt leg of the Go gate is green, which was dp8p's concern). Mutation-checked: reverting the tick to the constant batch fails the three iosv tests with the bead's own complaint (behind = 9825, want 25). LIVE on a console built from the commit with scope set and a local origin: batch_limit 200 -> 300 -> 200 as a 300-exchange backlog was admitted and cleared, and 200 -> 602 -> 1341 while a throttled seeder grew the backlog past the baseline; pre-fix that field stayed 200 and behind climbed. Commits e7f42a2 (source) + 38894bc (tests).

title: live-audit: no per-host pacing — one sequential batch, first-host-named, a slow host wedges all
description: From the live-audit research (/tmp/liveaudit-report.md G2): the sweep runs one sequential AuditSession per tick (liveaudit.go:653), the task target takes the first host's name (:438-450), and the id-order walk (:577-590) has no host grouping — a slow host in a multi-host capture ordering blocks every host behind it. Burp's live-audit queue carries max_items_in_progress per queue (Zeuc map_root.tsv:255; parallel_crawl_and_audit :8768-8769). Smallest honest shape: group the tick's ids by host and run one AuditSession per host with a bounded concurrency, so pacing is per-host rather than global. The per-host in-flight count is the honest metric.
close_reason: Per-host pacing is live, in the smallest honest shape the bead named: the tick's ids GROUP BY AUTHORITY (host:port_tls — not the hostname; the grouping test caught my first draft collapsing two 127.0.0.1 origins on different ports into one pacing domain, exactly the port-based-vhost case per-host pacing must not collapse) and each group runs as its OWN AuditSession, concurrently under liveAuditHostSessions=4 (named: it is half the tick's real concurrency ceiling, bound × the engine's MaxConcurrency, and nothing reported it). A single-host batch degenerates to the old one call verbatim — no fold, no new concurrency in the overwhelmingly common case. THE FOLD: the returned outcome aggregates every host session (items summed in walk order, worst state kept, Paused/TimedOut ORed) so the task row, the event and the pane keep ONE set of numbers per tick. THE HONEST METRIC: hostSessions counts per-host sessions, asserted by the tests (multi-host = one session per authority; single-host = exactly one) — this counter exists because the first mutation run showed a timing-based wedge test alone cannot distinguish grouped from ungrouped (both complete inside a generous deadline); the grouping-disabled mutation SURVIVED the first set, the counter was added, and the same mutation now FAILs. MULTI-HOST LABELS: the task target names EVERY host (first-seen, capped at three + '+N more'), because 'sweep of host-a (200 exchanges)' for a mostly-host-b batch was a claim the numbers did not back. Tests: liveaudit_pacing_test.go 5/5 — the slow-host wedge driven live (a 300ms-every-response origin does not wedge the fast origin's capture; both swept); the single-host batch verbatim with the session count asserted; the fold sums both hosts AND asserts 2 sessions ran; the target names both hosts; the bound is small and named. Mutations: grouping-disabled FAILs (after the counter was added — survivor became an assertion), fold-drops-later-hosts FAILs. Gates: build/vet/gofmt clean; web green 34.4s against the clean HEAD-based file (one known timing flake in the retry test, passed 3/3 in isolation and in the rerun); the working tree fully rebuilt with the coworker's iosv WIP + my v7fo/m9e0/6urp coexisting (32.1s green, every era's tests pass in the combined tree); e2e-go.sh 24/24.

title: gaps.md: record the research declines — ML core, session-during-audit, LOW_VALUE, crawl tolerances, HTTP/2 pseudo-headers, relocation matching
description: From the Burp scanner-logic + live-audit research (/tmp/smartscan-report.md §7 declines; /tmp/liveaudit-report.md): record six explicit decline-and-document rows in burpsy-go/gaps.md, each with the Burp evidence and the reason: (1) ML in the engine core — Burp has none; classical statistics ported; nondeterministic verdicts at odds with honest counting. (2) Session rules during audit — needs macro/session infra the audit engine does not own; pending the session epic. (3) LOW_VALUE audit disposition (Zwee.java:125-129) — keys on crawler action types (floating forms, speculative nav) burpsy's crawler does not record; porting the constant without the metadata would be a label over nothing.
