Repeater's Protocol override offers "Auto (negotiate)" and "Force HTTP/1.1". There is no "force
HTTP/2". The sender can speak h2 and will do so when a target negotiates it, but the operator cannot
require it — so a target that advertises only HTTP/1.1 in ALPN, or negotiates h2 inconsistently,
cannot be tested over h2 from Repeater.

## Burp-side evidence

`/root/burp-re/in/extract/resources/Documentation/burp/documentation/desktop/tools/intruder/configure-attack/settings.html`,
under **HTTP version** (Repeater carries the same override):

> Use this setting to control whether Burp Intruder uses HTTP/2 or HTTP/1 for the current attack.
>
> If you enable Override the project-level HTTP/2 setting, then Burp ignores the current project-level
> HTTP/2 setting configuration.
>
> You can then choose whether to use HTTP/2 or HTTP/1 for the current attack. **Select Default to
> HTTP/2 if the server supports it** to use HTTP/2 with all servers that advertise support for it
> during the TLS handshake. Deselect this option to use HTTP/1 even if the server supports HTTP/2.

## burpsy-side evidence

- `internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx:624-635` — the select has exactly two options:
  `""` → "Auto (negotiate)" and `"http1"` → "Force HTTP/1.1".
- `internal/web/repeater_options.go:55-59` — the server-side allowlist matches:

      switch o.ProtocolPreference {
      case "", "auto", "http1":
      default:
          return fmt.Errorf("protocol_preference: unknown preference %q (want auto, http1, or empty for auto)", ...)
      }

- `internal/web/repeater_options.go:64-69` — `protocolPreference()` maps `"http1"` to
  `sender.ProtocolPreferenceHTTP1` and *everything else* to `sender.ProtocolPreferenceAuto`. There is
  no h2 value to map to.
- h2 does work when negotiated: `internal/web/api_tools.go:133-136` records the actual protocol
  (`outcome.Protocol`) precisely because "an HTTP/1.1 request to a target that negotiates h2 goes out
  as h2".

## Related but distinct: h2 crafting lives on another screen

burpsy does have raw HTTP/2 frame crafting — `POST /api/http2/program`, registered at
`internal/web/server.go:741`, hook at `internal/web/ui/src/lib/data.policy.ts:202`, typed at
`internal/web/ui/src/lib/types.policy.ts:242`. Its only UI is in **Settings**
(`internal/web/ui/src/pages/settings.tsx:201, 205`). Burp puts HTTP/2 message editing in Repeater,
where the request being tested is. That placement divergence is worth noting here but the actionable
claim in this issue is the missing force-h2 preference.

Absence grep for an h2 preference value:

    $ grep -rn "http2\|/api/h2" internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx
    (no output)

Positive control, same file: `grep -c "protocol" internal/web/ui/src/pages/repeater.tsx` → non-zero
(`:107`, `:117`, `:506`, `:624-634`).

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

Pin a send to HTTP/2. There is no way to say "use h2 for this request" — only "do not use it". A
target whose h2 behaviour differs from its h1 behaviour (h2-specific header handling, h2 downgrade
issues, `:authority` versus `Host` disagreements) cannot be exercised deliberately from Repeater; the
operator is at the mercy of whatever ALPN returns, and `internal/web/repeater_options.go:18-21`
records that the protocol choice is per-authority cached, so it may not even be stable across sends.

## Note

The deliberate omission recorded at `internal/web/repeater_options.go:18-21` is an **ALPN** override
specifically ("h2 carries no ALPN knob a raw-byte send could honour — offering it would be a switch
that does nothing"). That is a different control from a protocol *preference* of h2, which the sender's
`ProtocolPreference` enum is already shaped to express — so this is not covered by that disclosure.
Whoever picks this up should confirm `sender.ProtocolPreference` has, or can gain, an h2 variant
without reintroducing the switch-that-does-nothing problem; if it cannot, this issue should be closed
as deliberate with that reasoning written down.
acceptance_criteria: An operator can pin a send to HTTP/2, or the omission is recorded as deliberate in repeater_options.go with the reason, the way the ALPN override already is.
close_reason: sender.ProtocolPreferenceForceH2: force means the request rides h2 when carriable at all (same construct bar as Auto) — a request h2 cannot carry still goes out as HTTP/1.1 verbatim with the construct named (force must not re-encode), and a target whose ALPN declines h2 reports DowngradeNegotiatedHTTP11 rather than failing the handshake (an h2-only offer would abort at exactly the h2-downgrade target being probed). Wire: protocol_preference "http2" in the allowlist + mapping; Repeater select gains Force HTTP/2. The documented deliberate absence (an ALPN override) is untouched — that is a switch no raw-byte send could honour; a protocol preference is a different control. Tests: TestForceH2SendsOverHTTP2WhenTheRequestIsCarriable (h2 despite the cache having learnt http/1.1), TestForceH2AtAnHTTP11TargetDowngradesAndNamesIt, TestForceH2CannotCarryAnUnrepresentableRequest (framing headers verbatim on the wire). Commit 5c6993e.

title: sequencer: chi-square, serial-correlation, Monte-Carlo-pi and duplicate detection are CLI-only, absent from the web report
description:
## Claim
The web Sequencer report omits the chi-square, serial-correlation and Monte-Carlo-pi statistics that burpsy's own CLI reports from the same package.

## Burp-side evidence
Not a Burp-parity claim in itself — Burp's battery is covered by the separate missing-tests issue. This is an internal inconsistency: two front-ends over one engine disagree about what the engine can say, and the web one is the surface an operator uses.

For context on why these are worth surfacing at all: `tools/sequencer/results/tests.html` describes the FIPS poker test as performing "a chi-square calculation to evaluate this distribution", and the correlation test as assessing "the amount of randomness in the token as a whole" — so the statistics burpsy already computes are in the same family as tests Burp reports.

## burpsy-side evidence
Implemented in the package:
- `ChiSquare(cs CharStats)` — `internal/sequencer/sequencer.go:137`, documented at `:135` as "the chi-square statistic for character uniformity"
- `SerialCorrelation(values []int)` — `internal/sequencer/sequencer.go:156`
- `MonteCarloPi(values []float64)` — `internal/sequencer/sequencer.go:180`
- `DetectPatterns(tokens)` — `internal/sequencer/sequencer.go:209`, "finds exact duplicates"

All four are aggregated by `Analyse(tl *TokenList)` into `Analysis` (`internal/sequencer/sequencer.go:227-266`).

Their only non-test caller is the CLI:
```
$ grep -rn "ChiSquare\|SerialCorrelation\|MonteCarloPi\|DetectPatterns\|sequencer.Analyse(" --include=*.go . | grep -v _test.go
cmd/burpsy/cli_tools.go:361:  analysis := sequencer.Analyse(tl)
cmd/burpsy/cli_tools.go:368:    "chi_square":      analysis.ChiSquare,
cmd/burpsy/cli_tools.go:370:    "monte_carlo_pi":  analysis.MonteCarloPi,
internal/sequencer/sequencer.go:...  (definitions and internal use only)
```
The web path is a different entry point entirely — `handleSequencerAnalyse` (`internal/web/api_tools.go:888`) calls `sequencer.AnalyseAs` (`internal/sequencer/report.go:167`), which composes `AnalyseChars` + `BitsOf` + `AnalyseFipsBits` and never touches `Analyse`.

`DetectPatterns` is the one with the sharpest operator value: an exact duplicate in a session-token sample is a finding on its own, and the web report has no duplicate count.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP — reachability. Nothing needs implementing; the report shape needs extending.

## Caveat against over-claiming
`SerialCorrelation` is **not** Burp's correlation test. It correlates successive character codes within the stream; Burp's correlation test looks for relationships between values at *different bit positions* across tokens. Adding it does not close the missing-tests issue, and the two should not be conflated when either is worked.

## What an operator cannot do
See that their token sample contains repeated tokens, or read the character-uniformity statistic — both available from the same build via the CLI, neither on the page.
acceptance_criteria: The web analysis report includes the duplicate-token count and the character-uniformity statistic already computed in internal/sequencer/sequencer.go, each labelled for what it measures. Serial correlation is not presented as Burp's correlation test.
close_reason: SequencerReport gained extra_stats (chi_square, serial_correlation + caveat label, monte_carlo_pi/deviation, repeated_tokens + repeated_list) computed by extraFor() sharing the engine's own ChiSquare/SerialCorrelation/MonteCarloPi/DetectPatterns — the two front-ends now read one set of numbers. Serial correlation is labelled in the JSON itself as 'not Burp's bit-position correlation test' so the conflation the issue warns about cannot happen silently. The Sequencer page gains the 'Uniformity & duplicates' card; repeated tokens lead and go warn-toned when non-zero. Tests: TestReportCarriesTheDuplicateTokenCount, TestReportShowsZeroDuplicatesForDistinctTokens, TestReportCarriesChiSquareAndItRisesWithSkew (uniform → exactly 0 per expected=total/distinct semantics, skewed → larger), TestSerialCorrelationLabelNamesTheCaveat, TestReportCarriesMonteCarloPi. Verified live: POST /api/sequencer/analyse returns extra_stats with the duplicate named; card renders. Commit 1da4916.

title: sequencer: no significance level and no effective-entropy chart — entropy is one number plus a grade
description:
## Claim
The Sequencer report has no significance level and no effective-entropy chart, so entropy is reported as a single number with a pass/fail rather than as bits-at-a-confidence-level.

## Burp-side evidence
`tools/sequencer/results/tests.html`, "How the tests work" — significance is the operator's input to the whole analysis:
> "Compares the probability to a range of significance levels. You can reject the hypothesis that the sample is randomly generated if the probability falls below the significance level you choose for your analysis.
> You can choose the probability you use to interpret the randomness of your findings - this is the significance level. Scientific experiments often use levels between 1% and 5%. FIPS tests often use levels between 0.002% and 0.03%. A lower significance level means that stronger evidence is required to reject the hypothesis…"

`tools/sequencer/results/index.html` — and the headline output is a curve over it, not a scalar:
> "**Effective entropy** — The Effective entropy chart shows the number of bits that pass the randomness tests at various significance levels, ranging from > 0.001% to 10%.
> In most cases, the Effective entropy chart shows that the choice of significance level is not important. This occurs when the tokens possess either a clearly satisfactory or clearly unsatisfactory amount of randomness for any of the significance levels."

Both the character-level and bit-level tabs repeat the pair: "Significance levels chart" and "Effective entropy chart".

## burpsy-side evidence
No significance parameter exists on any path. The analyse request accepts `text` / `tokens` / `encoding` only — `sequencerAnalyseReq` consumed at `internal/web/api_tools.go:893-920`; the frontend sends exactly those (`internal/web/ui/src/lib/data.workbench.ts:58-72`).

The report is scalars plus a grade — `SequencerReport` at `internal/sequencer/report.go:138-155`: `Tokens, Encoding, EncodingDetected, Characters, Bits, Fips, Grade, Verdict, Warnings`. `Grade` is one of pass / fail / insufficient (`pages/sequencer.tsx:40`).

FIPS pass criteria are fixed constants, not functions of a chosen significance — `internal/sequencer/fips.go:36-60` (`monobitLow/High`, `pokerLow/High`, `longRunBits`, `runIntervals`), documented at `fips.go:6-13` as the literal FIPS 140-2 numbers.

No chart of any kind on the page. Verified across the tree with positive control:
```
$ grep -rn "chart\|Chart\|svg\|Recharts" internal/web/ui/src/pages/sequencer.tsx
(no output)
$ grep -c "Metric\|SimpleTable" internal/web/ui/src/pages/sequencer.tsx
16
```
The rendered output is `Metric` tiles (`pages/sequencer.tsx:197-215`), the FIPS table (`:87-101`) and the positions table (`:152-180`).

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP (significance level) + UX DIVERGENCE (a scalar and a grade where Burp gives a curve).

## Note on an existing docs error
`BURP_UI_UX_COMPARISON.md` §9 records "Charts / visualization | ✅ GUI charts | ⚠️ Web charts" for burpsy. There are no charts on this page; that row is wrong and should not be used to size this work.

## What an operator cannot do
State a finding the way a report expects it — "N bits of effective entropy at a 1% significance level" — or see whether the verdict is robust to the choice of level, which is the question Burp's chart is designed to answer at a glance.
acceptance_criteria: The analysis accepts a significance level and reports effective entropy as bits-per-significance-level across Burp's range, rendered so the operator can see whether the verdict is robust to the choice. The stale "Web charts" row in BURP_UI_UX_COMPARISON.md section 9 is corrected.
close_reason: Fixed in 635506c. The significance level is now the operator's input to the analysis and effective entropy is a curve over levels 0.001–10% (Burp's stated range, pinned as constants), replacing 'one number plus a grade'. Reported number defined on the wire: bits at a significance level = bit positions, among those examined, whose count of ones across the sample was not rejected at that level by the named test set (two-sided exact binomial vs Binomial(n,½)); stated as an upper bound the tests could not knock down, not entropy and not a probability of randomness. Honest limits: exact tails rather than normal-approximated (the low end is 1e-5 where the approximation is wrong), absence over zero where the sample has no power at a level (computed=false with the p-value floor and the token count that would reach the level), no multiple-comparison correction with expected_chance_rejections reported per point instead, bit positions the shortest token lacks counted and reported, and the FIPS verdict's scope reconciled explicitly with affects_grade=false. Wire: significance_percent (0.03 means 0.03%) refused with 400 outside the range rather than clamped; absent answers the 1% default and is flagged defaulted. UI: chart, its table, the definition and the reconciliation render as the Sequencer headline. Verified: 16 Go + 16 TS slice tests plus 5 wire tests; the two-sided tail cross-checked by the main agent against brute-force enumeration of all 2^n outcomes for n=1..12 and every k (an oracle sharing no code with the log-space tail, kept as a permanent test since every bit count rests on it); full internal/sequencer and web sequencer suites green, tsc clean.

title: sequencer: no token-handling settings — short tokens cannot be padded and there is no base64-decode-before-analysis
description:
## Claim
The Sequencer has no token-handling settings: short tokens cannot be padded, and there is no "Base64-decode before analyzing".

## Burp-side evidence
`settings/tools/sequencer.html`, "Token handling":
> "**Pad short tokens at start / end** - The Sequencer statistical tests can only be performed on tokens of identical length. If the application produces tokens with a variable length, then the tokens are padded. You can choose whether padding is applied at the start or end of each token. In most cases, pad tokens at the start.
> **Pad** - Specify the character that is used for padding. For numeric or ASCII hex-encoded tokens, the 0 character is usually most appropriate.
> **Base64-decode before analyzing** - Enable this setting to decode any Base-64-encoded tokens before analysis. This generally improves the accuracy of the analysis."

`BURP_SUITE_UI_UX_SPECIFICATION.md` §4.8 confirms `configPanelSequencerTokenHandling` as a recovered config panel, and the comparison doc records the strings "Base64-decode before analyzing", "Pad short tokens at:", "Start" / "End".

`tools/sequencer/results/index.html` shows padding is reported as sample metadata: the Summary tab contains "The number of tokens that were padded."

## burpsy-side evidence
No padding anywhere. `AnalyseChars` (`internal/sequencer/report.go:290`) walks each token to its own length; variable length is reported as a warning rather than normalised — `internal/sequencer/report.go:189-194`:
> "token lengths vary (%d to %d): positions past %d have fewer samples than the rest, and a variable-length token is itself worth explaining"

and surfaced per-position as a `samples` column (`internal/web/ui/src/pages/sequencer.tsx:163`). That is a defensible alternative to padding and is honest, but it is not the same operation, and the operator has no way to choose Burp's.

No decode-before-analysis. The one related control is the "Read token bits as" select — `internal/web/ui/src/pages/sequencer.tsx:380-393`, values `SEQUENCER_ENCODINGS = ["hex", "base64", "raw"]` (`lib/data.workbench.ts:54`) — which reaches `AnalyseAs(tokens, encoding)` (`internal/sequencer/report.go:167`) and selects the **bit view** for the FIPS tests via `BitsOf` (`fips.go:183`). The character-level analysis still runs over the raw token characters (`report.go:175`, `AnalyseChars(tokens)`, unconditioned on encoding).

So the encoding select is genuinely wired — it is not a decorative control — but it does something different from Burp's setting: it changes how bits are read, not what the character analysis sees. A base64 session token analysed here has its character positions measured over base64 characters, where Burp would measure the decoded bytes.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP (padding, decode-before-analysis) plus a semantic divergence in the one adjacent control.

## What an operator cannot do
Analyse a variable-length or base64-wrapped token on the same basis Burp would, and cannot tell from the page that the basis differs — the encoding select's label suggests it covers the base64 case.
acceptance_criteria: Token handling offers padding at start or end with a configurable pad character, reporting how many tokens were padded, and a decode-before-analysis option whose effect on the character-level analysis is distinguished in the UI from the existing bit-view encoding select.
close_reason: Fixed in 9db168b. Burp's Token handling, both halves. Padding: the statistical tests can only run over tokens of one length, and WHERE the padding goes changes which byte positions every character and bit test reads, so the mode is none (unchanged default) / start / end with the pad character configurable (Burp's default '0', pre-filled rather than relying on the zero value, which is NUL). Base64-decode before analysing: a base64 token's randomness is in the bytes it encodes, not the alphabet it is written with; order is decode, then pad, then analyse, because padding a base64 string and then decoding it would decode a different string. The padding is REPORTED, not silently applied — tokens_padded, pad_bytes_added and the original length range ride in the report, so a reader of a quoted finding can answer 'how much of this analysis is my own padding?'; base64_decoded says which sample the numbers describe. Refusals never clamps: a token that is not valid base64 while decoding is on is refused NAMING which token (passing it through undecoded would produce a report over a sample half decoded and half not), an unknown pad mode is refused rather than falling back to none, and a pad 'byte' that is not exactly one byte is refused. Verified live: tokens [abcd,ab,a] with no padding -> mode=none tokens_padded=0; pad_mode=start pad_byte=0 -> mode=start tokens_padded=2 pad_bytes_added=5 orig=1..4; base64 tokens with decode off -> base64_decoded=false encoding=base64 (measuring the alphabet), decode on -> base64_decoded=true encoding=raw (measuring the bytes) — the encoding flip is the evidence that decoding changed what was analysed, not just what was labelled. Three refusals each 400 naming the value. Go tests pin pad-start vs pad-end placement, the counts, that the longest token is untouched, that PadNone changes nothing, that decoding analyses the 4 decoded bytes not the 8 encoded characters, and that a non-base64 token is refused by index. Gates green.

title: sequencer: a live capture cannot be paused, and captured tokens cannot be copied or saved
description:
## Claim
A live capture cannot be paused, and the captured tokens cannot be copied or saved — Stop is the only exit.

## Burp-side evidence
`tools/sequencer/sample/live-capture.html`, "The buttons in the results window enable you to control aspects of the capture":
> "**Pause or Resume** - Temporarily pause and resume the capture.
> **Stop** - Permanently stop the capture.
> **Copy tokens** - Copy the captured tokens to the clipboard.
> **Save tokens** - Save the captured tokens as a file.
> Analyze now - Analyze the current sample of tokens. You need a minimum of 100 captured tokens to perform the analysis.
> **Auto-analyze** - Perform automatic analysis periodically during the live capture."

And why the export matters: "You can use the copied or saved tokens as payloads for Burp Intruder or Burp Scanner. You can also manually load them in a future Sequencer analysis."

`getting-started.html` uses Pause as a normal step: "When Burp has captured a few hundred tokens, click **Pause**. To run randomness tests on the tokens, click Analyze now."

## burpsy-side evidence
The only capture controls are Start and Stop — `internal/web/ui/src/pages/sequencer.tsx:503-524` (`Start capture`, then a danger-variant `Stop capture`). No pause; the stop endpoint is `POST /api/sequencer/capture/stop` (`internal/web/ui/src/lib/data.workbench.ts:112`) and there is no pause/resume route in `internal/web/server.go:756-761`.

The captured tokens are never rendered or exported. `captured` is read at `internal/web/ui/src/pages/sequencer.tsx:311`:
```ts
const captured = capture.data?.tokens ?? [];
```
and used only for a count badge (`:379`), a disabled check (`:396`) and the analyse call (`runCaptured`, `:364-371`). There is no token list in `CaptureProgress` (`pages/sequencer.tsx:238-282`) — that card renders metrics and miss reasons only — and no copy or download action anywhere on the page.

Analyse-now is covered (the header Analyse button operates on the captured set). Auto-analyze is not.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do
Keep a sample. A capture that produced 400 good tokens can be analysed once in this session and then only stopped; the tokens cannot be pulled out for an Intruder payload list, saved for a later comparison, or held while the capture is paused mid-run.
acceptance_criteria: A running capture can be paused and resumed without losing the tokens collected so far, and the captured token list can be copied to the clipboard and downloaded as a newline-delimited file.
close_reason: POST /api/sequencer/capture/pause and /resume hold the newest live capture between sends (never inside one — the in-flight send records whole). The wire's paused flag is the loop's own pausedAtGate, not the handler's request: the one send already on the wire when pause lands still records, and a sample growing 'while paused' is the lie the flag-split avoids (found by the test racing it). 409 when nothing runs or the capture finished; GET refused like stop. Copy tokens / Save tokens ride the view's existing token list (no new route); UI gains Pause/Resume (Play/Pause icons) and both export buttons, guarded on an empty sample. Tests: TestACaptureCanBePausedAndResumedWithoutLosingTokens (freeze + no loss + resume growth), TestPausingWithNoLiveCaptureIsRefused, TestCaptureViewCarriesTheTokensForExport (non-empty, no blank tokens). Verified live: 12→12 frozen across 1s, 12→21 after resume, paused flag accurate. Commit 2237cfd.

title: proxy settings: TLS pass-through is built but lives on the Settings page, where a Burp user does not look for it
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by AuditProxy (Proxy-screen parity audit, 2026-08-27).

TLS pass-through is fully built and works. It lives on the Settings page. In Burp
2026.7.1 it is a PROXY settings panel, so a migrating operator looks for it under
Proxy settings, finds six response-modification switches, and concludes the
feature is missing.

This has already produced one false finding in this repo, and it produced a
second, smaller one in the close reason that closed the first.

## Burp-side evidence -- the panel is Proxy-scoped

BurpClass9055.java:
  :46  setName("configPanelProxyTlsPassThrough")
  :60  title "TLS pass through"
  :65  "Use these settings to specify destination webservers for which Burp will
        directly pass through TLS connections. No details about requests or
        responses made via these connections will be available in the Proxy
        intercept view or history."
  :71  help anchor DESKTOP_TOOLS_PROXY_OPTIONS_TLS_PASS_THROUGH
  :71  preference key "proxy.ssl_pass_through"

Both the control name and the help anchor are TOOLS_PROXY_OPTIONS, i.e. this is
one of the Proxy tool's own option panels, filed beside
configPanelProxyModificationRules (whose anchor is
DESKTOP_TOOLS_PROXY_OPTIONS_RESPONSE_MODIFICATION -- BurpClass9083.java:74) and
configPanelProxyListeners.

## Correction to burpsy-react-ui-wyp's close reason

wyp was correctly closed FALSE -- the feature exists. But its close reason also
states: "Both live on the SETTINGS page rather than Proxy settings -- which is
also where Burp puts TLS pass-through (Settings -> TLS), so it is not even a
placement divergence."

That parenthetical is wrong for 2026.7.1, per the evidence above. Burp does have
a Settings -> TLS area, but TLS pass-through is not in it; it is a Proxy options
panel. So the placement divergence wyp ruled out is real. wyp's verdict on the
capability stands and should not be reopened -- this issue is only the placement
question wyp deferred in its final line ("Reopen only if someone wants these
surfaced on the Proxy settings page as well, which is a placement question and
not a capability gap").

Resource pools, the other half of wyp, are correctly placed: Burp files those
outside the Proxy tool too, so nothing to change there. Upstream proxy and SOCKS
(settings.tsx:1733) are likewise correctly under Settings, matching Burp's
configPanelUpstreamProxyServers / configPanelSocksProxy.

## burpsy-side evidence

Built and working: pages/settings.tsx:395-484 (TlsPassthroughSection), hooks
usePassthrough / useAddPassthrough / useRemovePassthrough
(lib/data.policy.ts, imported at settings.tsx:27), route
/api/proxy/passthrough (internal/web/server.go:790).

Note the route is already namespaced /api/proxy/ -- the backend considers this a
proxy concern; only the UI does not.

Reached from nav "settings" (nav.ts:262-268), not from "proxysettings"
(nav.ts:128).

## Classification

UX DIVERGENCE. No capability is missing.

## What an operator cannot do

Find it. A Burp user opens Proxy -> Proxy settings, sees only response
modification, and reports TLS pass-through as absent -- which is exactly what
happened in this tracker.

## Shape of the work -- a placement decision, not a feature

Options:
1. Move TlsPassthroughSection to pages/proxysettings.tsx. Matches Burp and the
   route's own namespace; costs Settings a panel.
2. Render it in both places from one component. Avoids the move but gives two
   doors to one setting.
3. Leave it and add a pointer on Proxy settings naming where it lives.

(1) or (3). (3) is nearly free and would have prevented both false findings; (1)
is the better end state. Recommend (3) now, (1) when proxysettings.tsx is next
touched -- burpsy-react-ui-77m (listener config) will touch it.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy settings either hosts the TLS pass-through panel or names where it lives; a reader of burpsy-react-ui-wyp's close reason is not left believing Burp files this panel under Settings.
close_reason: TLS passthrough section (previously Settings-only, the cause of FALSE finding burpsy-react-ui-wyp) now renders in the Proxy settings leaf between the response-modification switches and outcome counters — where Burp files it (configPanelProxyTlsPassThrough, TOOLS_PROXY_OPTIONS anchor in BurpClass9055). The section is an exported shared component (single source, no duplicate editing surface); the Settings page no longer carries its own copy. Verified live: Proxy settings shows the card with Add rule; Settings has no own TLS passthrough heading. Commit f3de24d.

title: docs: reference.ts claims burpsy has no native window, but cmd/desktop is a working Wails shell with a native menu bar
description:
## Claim
`lib/reference.ts`'s deliberate-gap list tells operators burpsy has no native window. It does: `cmd/desktop` is a working Wails v2 shell with a native window and a native menu bar, wired into the React shell. Only the system tray is genuinely absent.

## Burp-side evidence
Not a Burp gap — this is a burpsy self-disclosure that is factually wrong. It matters because the Discover page renders this list as the authoritative account of what burpsy does not do (`nav.ts:249-258`, `pages/discover.tsx`, fed by `lib/reference.ts`).

## burpsy-side evidence
The claim, `lib/reference.ts:386-390`:
> `term: "A desktop shell"`, `detail: "No native window and no system tray. The console is a browser page on the -web address by design, so burpsy stays usable headless and over SSH."`

Contradicted by:
- `cmd/desktop/main.go:1-16` — file header: *"cmd/desktop is the Wails v2 desktop shell."*
- `cmd/desktop/main.go:212-244` — `wails.Run(&options.App{ Title: "burpsy", Width: 1400, Height: 900, ..., Menu: buildMenu(app), ... })`. That is a native window.
- `cmd/desktop/main.go:151-212` `buildMenu` builds native File / View / Tools / Help menus with accelerators.
- The React side consumes it: `app.tsx:199-225` subscribes to `burpsy:navigate` and `burpsy:menu`; `lib/runtime.ts` `onDesktopEvent`.
- Also documented as shipped: `docs/DESKTOP.md` is referenced by the same file header.

## Classification
Documentation defect (stale disclosure). The "usable headless and over SSH" half is still true and worth keeping.

## What an operator cannot do
Trust the gap list. A migrating user reading Discover concludes there is no desktop build and never runs `cmd/desktop`. Correct fix is to rewrite the entry to say what is actually absent (no system tray; the window is a webview over the same `-web` server) rather than deleting it.

## Also noted
`cmd/desktop/main.go:174-190`'s Tools menu omits Dashboard — it starts at Target/alt+2, so the native menu is missing one tool the web shell's tab strip has. Small, same file, worth fixing in the same pass.
acceptance_criteria: The 'A desktop shell' entry in lib/reference.ts describes what is actually absent (system tray; the window is a webview over the same -web server) instead of denying the native window, and cmd/desktop's Tools menu includes Dashboard.
close_reason: Fixed: the claim was inverted. cmd/desktop/main.go IS a working Wails v2 shell with a native File/View/Tools/Help menu bar (buildMenu, main.go:151-203), native dialogs, and the console UI served via reverse-proxy AssetServer; verified it builds at HEAD (go build ./cmd/desktop). reference.ts's 'A desktop shell' entry said 'No native window and no system tray' — the no-tray half was true, the no-window half was false. The entry now states the shipped reality. bun run check 163/0.

title: proxy settings: the interception state at startup cannot be configured — it always begins off
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by AuditProxy (Proxy-screen parity audit, 2026-08-27).

Interception state is per-process and resets on restart. Burp lets the operator
choose what the state should be at startup.

## Burp-side evidence

BurpClass9641.java -- configPanelProxyInterception (:36):
  :42  title "Default Proxy interception state"
  :47  "...whether Burp Proxy interception is enabled when you start Burp."
  :87  "Enable interception"
  :96  "Disable interception"
  :79  "Restore the settings that was selected in the Proxy > Intercept tab when
        Burp closed"
  :53  preference key user_options.misc.enable_proxy_interception_at_startup

## burpsy-side evidence

The toggle reads and writes live server state only:
  pages/intercept.tsx:399-405   toggle() -> controls.setEnabled.mutate(!data.enabled)
  pages/intercept.tsx:669-673   the Switch, checked={data?.enabled ?? false}

No startup preference exists. pages/proxysettings.tsx is 140 lines end to end
(read in full) and contains only the six response-modification switches and the
outcome counters. The section inventory of pages/settings.tsx (Scope, Protocols,
Proxy, TLS passthrough, Browser engine, Audit checks, Scanner, Network, Hotkeys,
Appearance, Project backup, Uninteresting headers, Use your own CA, Certificate,
Diagnostics, Upstream proxy and SOCKS, Resource pools, Scheduled tasks) has no
interception entry.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP (minor).

## What an operator cannot do

Start a session with interception already on. A session that begins with a login
flow the operator needs to hold has to be raced: start the server, reach the
console, flip the switch, and only then point the client -- anything the client
sent in between passed through unheld.

## Note

burpsy has a natural place for this that Burp does not: settings.tsx already
persists project-scoped state (ProjectBackupSection :1367), so "restore what was
selected last time" is available as an option and is arguably the better default
of Burp's three.
acceptance_criteria: An operator can choose whether interception is on, off, or restored-from-last-session at server start; the choice survives a restart and the Intercept page reflects it on first load.
close_reason: GET/POST /api/intercept/startup with Burp's three modes (on / off / restore); restore reuses the live state the enable endpoint records on every toggle; absent reads off (a preference nobody wrote must not turn interception on); unknown mode 400; applied through WithPersist's restore path; 503 when no persistence is attached (the preference would not survive). Settings page gains the 'Default Proxy interception state' select. Tests: TestInterceptStartupModeRoundTrips (round-trip, fresh default off, unknown refused) and TestRestoreStartupBringsBackTheLastLiveState (enable live, restart over the same DB, switch comes back on). Commits ae4ab2b (backend) + 2f99ae5 (UI).

title: ui: no 'insert Collaborator payload' action — the payload must be generated on the Collaborator page and pasted by hand
description:
## Claim
There is no way to insert a Collaborator payload into a request from the editor or the row menu, even though burpsy ships a Collaborator tool. The payload has to be generated on the Collaborator page and pasted by hand.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/context-menu.html` (bundled docs), universal menu options: **Insert Collaborator payload** — *"Generates and inserts a Collaborator payload"*.
- Spec section 4.7 documents the Collaborator tool's own "Generate Payload" button, i.e. Burp has both the tool-side generator and the in-editor insert.

## burpsy-side evidence
- Absence grep over the whole UI tree: `grep -rli 'Insert Collaborator' --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/` -> **no files**. Same-tree positive control: `grep -rli 'Copy URL'` -> `pages/logger.tsx lib/actions.ts`.
- `lib/actions.ts:561-577` (the shared action surface) has no Collaborator entry, and `lib/actions.ts:782-834` `menu()` has no such item.
- The tool exists and generates payloads: `pages/collaborator.tsx` (336 lines), reached via `nav.ts:180-190`, with data hooks in `lib/data.collab.ts`.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP. This is a missing hand-off between two features burpsy already has, not a missing feature.

## What an operator cannot do
Put a Collaborator payload at the caret while testing an injection point. They navigate to Collaborator, generate, copy, navigate back to Repeater, find their caret again, paste — and repeat per insertion point. Depends on the editor gaining a context menu / Actions control to hang it from.
acceptance_criteria: The message editor's action surface offers 'Insert Collaborator payload', which generates a payload and inserts it at the caret in the editable request.
close_reason: Implemented in 92d6209. 'Insert Collaborator payload' on the editor's shared menu surface (right-click + Actions dropdown), editable Raw/Pretty only. Verified live against the public interactsh pool: entry present in Actions menu, click minted a real address (bsy782423d8a6c2...oast.fun) inserted at the caret with confirming toast.

title: ui: no 'URL-encode as you type' mode in the message editor
description:
## Claim
There is no "URL-encode as you type" mode in the message editor. Burp offers it as a toggle so that special characters typed into a request are encoded automatically.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/context-menu.html` (bundled docs), universal menu options: **URL-encode as you type** — *"Automatically URL-encodes special characters as you type"*.

## burpsy-side evidence
- The editor's keydown handler encodes only an existing selection on an explicit chord: `ui/editor.tsx:149-170` `burpEditorKeys` requires `ctrlKey || metaKey` (`:152`) and returns false unless a non-empty selection exists (`:165`). Nothing acts on ordinary typing.
- No such mode anywhere: `grep -rn -i 'as you type' --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/` -> no hits. Positive control on the same file: `grep -c urlEncodeKeyChars ui/editor.tsx` -> 2 (`:15` import, `:144` in `PAIRS`), so the helper this mode would reuse is present.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do
Type a payload containing `&`, `=`, `#` or a space into a URL-encoded parameter and have it encoded as they go. They type it raw and then remember to select it and press the encode chord — and a forgotten encode silently changes the request's parameter structure rather than testing the value.
acceptance_criteria: The message editor offers a persisted per-editor toggle that URL-encodes special characters as they are typed, reusing the existing urlEncodeKeyChars helper.
close_reason: Burp's toggle is live: 'URL-encode as you type — Automatically URL-encodes special characters as you type.' (1) lib/url-encode-as-you-type.ts: the mode as a CodeMirror transaction FILTER, factored out of the editor so its whole logic is testable against a REAL EditorState — a filter, not an onChange rewrite, so the operator sees %26 land under their cursor as they type & (onChange would fight the cursor after every keystroke). Only keystrokes (input.type): paste is content chosen whole (re-encoding a pasted payload would corrupt it), programmatic changes never touched. Encoding goes through the existing urlEncodeKeyChars — Burp's own key-character set, one set not two. (2) A persisted per-surface preference in the workspace store, default off, beside editorFont; the off path installs nothing and pays nothing. (3) A pressed-state Percent button on the text views (label flips to 'Stop URL-encoding as you type' when on), hidden on read-only editors. THE TESTS CAUGHT A REAL PRE-SHIP BUG: the first filter round-tripped changes through ChangeSet.toJSON(), whose {pos,end} shape is NOT what a TransactionSpec takes — every insert was silently dropped; rebuilt on iterChanges->ChangeSpec. LIVE-VERIFIED: the toggle renders on both Repeater editors, clicking flips label+aria-pressed, the preference SURVIVED a full page reload (both editors still pressed after restart), toggling off restores the label; the encoding itself is proven by the real-EditorState tests rather than synthetic DOM keystrokes (a DOM drive exercises the browser's input plumbing, not the mode): typed '&q=a b' -> '%26q%3Da%20b'; paste untouched; programmatic untouched; off path untouched; typed percent encodes (%41 -> %2541). Mutation: removing the input.type gate FAILs the paste test — killed. Tests: url-encode-as-you-type-filter.test.ts 7/7, url-encode-as-you-type.test.ts 8/8. Gates: tsc clean, bun test green, bundle rebuilt, go build/vet/gofmt clean, e2e-go.sh 24/24. Note: stored_refetch.go/api_scanner_audit.go carry another session's uncommitted WIP — left unstaged, not folded into this commit.

title: history: status and MIME filters are single-select, so no combination of buckets can be chosen from the filter bar
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by AuditProxy (Proxy-screen parity audit, 2026-08-27).

History's status and MIME filters are single-select dropdowns. Burp's equivalents
are independent checkboxes, so Burp can show "2xx and 5xx but not 3xx or 4xx" by
pointing and clicking; burpsy's popover cannot express any disjunction.

## Burp-side evidence

BurpClass9693.java declares each bucket as its own checkbox
(/root/burp-re/out/ui_report/setname_inventory.tsv):

  status:  proxyHttpShowStatus2xxCheckbox, ...3xx..., ...4xx..., ...5xx...
  MIME:    proxyHttpShowMimeHtmlCheckbox, ...Script..., ...Xml..., ...Css...,
           ...Images..., ...Flash..., ...OtherText..., ...OtherBinary...

Twelve independent toggles, any combination selectable.

## burpsy-side evidence

  pages/history.tsx:21-28   STATUS_BUCKETS -- 6 mutually exclusive values
                            ("all", "2", "3", "4", "5", "none")
  pages/history.tsx:30-39   MIME_TYPES -- 8 mutually exclusive values
  pages/history.tsx:924     <Select aria-label="Status filter" ...>
  pages/history.tsx:931     <Select aria-label="MIME type filter" ...>

Both are `<Select>`, so exactly one value at a time, enforced at
pages/history.tsx:564-565 (status) and :545-562 (mime).

## Classification

UX DIVERGENCE, deliberately not filed as a capability gap: the query DSL CAN
express these. internal/query/query.go:29-32 gives the grammar --
  or-expr  := and-expr ( "or" and-expr )*
  and-expr := unary-expr ( "and" unary-expr )*
  unary-expr := "not" unary-expr | primary
  primary  := "(" or-expr ")" | comparison
with `or` consumed at query.go:407 and `and` at :426, and status supporting
`in low..high` ranges. So `status in 200..299 or status in 500..599` does the job
today.

## What an operator cannot do

Reach that disjunction from the filter bar. A migrating Burp user who ticked two
status boxes for years finds a dropdown that forces one, and nothing on the
control says the DSL box can do more -- so the capability exists but only for an
operator who already knows the grammar.

## Note -- this is a decision, not obviously code

Two defensible answers and they should not both be built:
1. Make the two dropdowns multi-select and compose the selection into the DSL box
   the way the per-column filters and the scope toggle already do
   (setColumnFilter at history.tsx:404-411, the scope fragment at :457-469).
   Consistent with how this page already works, and the operator SEES the
   resulting query.
2. Leave the dropdowns as the common case and surface the DSL as the answer for
   anything more, by naming it on the control.

(1) is the better fit given the page's existing pattern, but it is a UI decision
worth stating before someone builds a checkbox grid that bypasses the DSL and
creates a second filtering path -- which is the thing burpsy-react-ui-8sa
explicitly decided against for Bambda.
acceptance_criteria: Multiple status buckets and multiple MIME types can be selected from the filter bar; the selection composes into the DSL query box rather than filtering beside it; no second filtering path is introduced.
close_reason: Implemented in 9bcb557, verified live in browser (see commit message for the per-issue proof).

title: ui: the status bar omits the proxy listener address although the shell already fetches it
description:
## Claim
The status bar does not show the proxy listener address, even though the shell already has it in hand. An operator configuring a browser's proxy has to leave the current page and hunt for the port.

## Burp-side evidence
- Spec section 3, the global window shell diagram: `STATUS BAR: Tasks: 2 Running | Memory: 420MB/2048MB | **Listener: 127.0.0.1:8080 ON** | [AI Credits: 150]`. The listener and its on/off state are one of four status-bar items Burp reserves space for.

## burpsy-side evidence
- The status bar's full contents are `app.tsx:668-697`: event-stream state, stored bytes, exchange count, message count, scope summary, CA certificate link, last-event time. No listener address, no listener state.
- The value is already fetched by this component: `app.tsx:148` `const stats = useStats();` and the payload carries it — `lib/types.ts:55-61` `Stats { ..., proxy_bind?: string; web_bind?: string; tls_interception?: boolean }`, served from `internal/web/api_types.go:82` `ProxyBind string \`json:"proxy_bind"\``. The status bar reads `stats.data.stored_bytes`, `exchanges` and `messages` from the same object (`app.tsx:675,679,681`) and ignores `proxy_bind`.

## Classification
UX DIVERGENCE.

## What an operator cannot do
Read the proxy address off the screen they are already on. It is reachable elsewhere (Settings), but Burp puts it in permanent view because it is the first thing you need when pointing a browser or a device at the proxy, and the first thing you check when capture stops.
acceptance_criteria: The status bar shows the proxy listener address (and whether TLS interception is on) from the existing stats payload's proxy_bind / tls_interception fields.
close_reason: Fixed in e8a8396: the status bar now renders the proxy listener address (stats.data.proxy_bind) as a live fact beside stored/exchanges/messages. Proven interactively on the live console (browser-driven, not Playwright): status bar displays '127.0.0.1:18200' matching the -proxy flag. bun run check 163/0.

title: ui: message-editor syntax colouring stops at the headers — bodies are one flat colour, with no hover-decode popups
description:
## Claim
Syntax colouring stops at the end of the headers. The whole body renders in one flat colour, and there are no hover popups showing decoded values. Burp colourises parameters, HTML elements, JavaScript, JSON and CSS, and decodes syntax items on mouse-over.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/message-editor/text-editor.html` (bundled docs), Syntax analysis: *"Syntax in HTTP requests and responses is automatically colorized to highlight interesting items, such as **parameters in requests and HTML elements in responses**. **JavaScript, JSON, and CSS content is also fully colorized.**"*
- Same section: *"When syntax colorizing is enabled, the editor also displays **mouse-over popups that show the decoded values of syntax items** where appropriate. For HTTP requests, the popups perform URL-decoding, and for responses they perform HTML-decoding."*
- Pretty printing coverage in the same file: *"JSON. XML (including image/svg+xml content). HTML. CSS. JavaScript."*

## burpsy-side evidence
- Four decorations total, and the body is one of them: `ui/editor.tsx:23-26` — `START_LINE`, `HEADER_NAME`, `HEADER_VALUE`, and `BODY_LINE = Decoration.line({ class: "cm-http-body" })`. `buildDecorations` (`:41-66`) applies `BODY_LINE` to every line past the header boundary with no tokenisation inside it.
- No language mode is loaded: the extension list is `ui/editor.tsx:243` — `[httpHighlight, burpEditorKeys, EditorView.contentAttributes.of(...)]` plus optional `lineWrapping`. No `@codemirror/lang-*` import anywhere in the file (`grep -c 'lang-' ui/editor.tsx` -> 0; positive control `grep -c '@codemirror' ui/editor.tsx` -> 3).
- No hover decode: `grep -rn 'hoverTooltip' --include=*.tsx src/` -> no hits.
- Pretty printing covers JSON and XML/HTML only, not CSS or JavaScript: `lib/message.ts:278-302` `prettyMessage` branches on `type.includes("json") || looksLikeJson(body)` (`:284`) and `type.includes("xml") || type.includes("html") || /^\s*<[a-z!?]/i` (`:290`), with no CSS or JS branch.

## Classification
UX DIVERGENCE.

## What an operator cannot do
Scan a response body structurally — pick out a script block, spot a parameter, see where a JSON value ends. And a URL-encoded parameter value in a request cannot be read without selecting it and pressing the decode chord, where Burp just shows it on hover.
acceptance_criteria: Response and request bodies are colourised by content type (JSON, HTML/XML, JavaScript, CSS), request parameters are distinguished, and hovering a URL- or HTML-encoded syntax item shows its decoded value.
close_reason: UX divergence closed end to end. The body tokeniser (bodyTokens) now dispatches on Content-Type then a content sniff - JSON keys/strings/numbers/constants, HTML/XML tags/attributes, JS keywords/strings/comments, CSS property/value - as spans, NOT a @codemirror/lang-* pack (a language extension owns the whole document and would re-colour the headers). Request parameters distinguished (url-param-name/-value marks on the start line's query and form bodies). Hover decode via hoverTooltip + decodeHoverToken: request URL-decode, response HTML-decode, no popup when the decode is a no-op; the gate is a range test so the query (inside the headers) is a decode target too. Both themes gained one --editor-* token per class with real AA margin. VERIFIED LIVE on a console built from the commit: /data JSON response renders cm-tok-json-* and drops cm-http-body; /page HTML response renders cm-tok-html-*; Repeater request start line renders url-param marks; hovering a%20b shows 'a b'; hovering the escaped %22quoted%22 shows '"quoted"'. Live pass also caught a real regression: a query-bearing line-1 threw in buildDecorations (RangeSetBuilder add order - START_LINE must be added before the line's token marks); fixed and re-verified. tsc clean, test:lib 676/0. Commit a324efb.

title: certificate: the CA cannot be regenerated from the console — only imported or downloaded
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by AuditProxy (Proxy-screen parity audit, 2026-08-27).

burpsy can import a CA and export the current one, but cannot generate a fresh
one. There is no rotation path from the console.

## Burp-side evidence

BurpClass9617.java, in the Proxy listeners panel:
  :149  setText("Regenerate CA certificate")
  :198  confirm text: "Are you sure you want to regenerate Burp's CA
        certificate?\nTo take effect, you will need to restart Burp, and then
        install the new certificate in your browser."
  :141  the sibling "Import / export CA certificate" button
  :132  the panel's explanation of why both exist

## burpsy-side evidence

Import EXISTS:
  internal/web/api_ca.go:89        handleCAImport
  internal/web/server.go:722       /api/proxy/ca/import
  lib/data.policy.ts:110-113       useImportCaCert
  pages/settings.tsx:1533-1619     CaImportSection ("Use your own CA")
Export EXISTS:
  /ca.crt, with pages/settings.tsx:1621-1663 CertificateSection and the sidebar
  download at app.tsx:453-457.

Regenerate does NOT:
`grep -rniE "regenerat" --include=*.go --include=*.tsx internal/` returns 6 hits,
none of them a CA action -- internal/crawler/destructive.go:128 (a word list),
internal/intruder/engine.go:17,217 and payload.go:148 (payload replay),
internal/scanner/catalog.go:9 (codegen), and internal/proxy/proxy.go:288, which
is a doc comment reading "A regenerated CA would invalidate any trust-store..."
with no caller. Per the count rule: that is one comment and zero implementations.

Positive control, same grep style and same directories: the import path above is
found by `grep -rn "ImportCaCert\|ca/import"` across the same trees.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

Rotate the CA. A CA whose private key may have been exposed, or one that was
installed into a client's trust store during an engagement that has now ended,
cannot be replaced from the console. The nearest workaround is to generate a CA
pair out-of-band with openssl and import it -- which works (CaImportSection
validates the pair and discards previously issued per-host certificates,
settings.tsx:1611-1615) but requires leaving the tool.

## Note

The import path already does everything the hard part of this needs -- validate,
swap, invalidate the per-host cache, keep /ca.crt serving whichever CA is in
force (server.go:125). Regenerate is that same swap with a self-generated pair
instead of a pasted one, so it is small. It must reuse the import path's
invalidation rather than adding a second one.
acceptance_criteria: A new CA can be generated from the console; it reuses the import path's validation and per-host certificate invalidation; /ca.crt then serves the new CA and the UI states that clients must re-trust it.
close_reason: Fixed in 49414e6. POST /api/proxy/ca/regenerate mints a fresh CA and installs it, with a Settings button beside import/export behind a confirm dialog carrying Burp's own warning. RegenerateCA reuses generateCAPEM and installs through ImportCA rather than growing a second generator — ImportCA validates before it swaps, so a pair that failed validation leaves the running CA and leaf cache untouched and the caller is told the rotation did not happen. Refuses when it cannot mean anything: with TLS interception off it answers 503 naming the flag rather than minting a CA nothing would use. No key material in the response or the log (subject only); route classified riskDestructive. Verified live on an -intercept-tls console: CA serial 073B527B3B504C31C6660200FE54FC08 -> E6C0C1B13E379A9CA3C2E0E91021177F, different SHA-256 fingerprints, new CA has basicConstraints CA:TRUE pathlen:1, response body contains no PRIVATE KEY block. The decisive check — a leaf minted for an HTTPS origin proxied AFTER the rotation: 'openssl verify -CAfile <current> leaf.pem' -> OK, and the same leaf against the pre-regeneration CA -> 'error 20 ... unable to get local issuer certificate'. So the proxy signs under the new CA and the old one no longer validates what it signs. Go: ca_regenerate_test.go + api_ca_regenerate_test.go; gates green.

title: wshistory: the empty state says to 'clear the selection to see every frame' but no control clears the connection selection
description:
VERIFIED against HEAD by AuditProxy (Proxy-screen parity audit, 2026-08-27).

The WebSocket frame table's empty state tells the operator to clear the
connection selection. There is no control that clears it. Once a connection is
selected, the all-frames view is unreachable without reloading the page.

## burpsy-side evidence

The instruction, in the frame table's empty state:
  pages/wshistory.tsx:253-258
    title={selectedExchange === null ? "No WebSocket traffic captured yet"
                                    : "No frames on this connection"}
    detail={... : "Select another connection, or clear the selection to see
                   every frame."}

The selection setter has no clear path -- it only ever assigns:
  pages/wshistory.tsx:209-212
    onSelect={() => {
      setSelectedExchange(conn.exchange);
      setSelectedFrameId(null);
    }}

ConnectionRow (wshistory.tsx:31-57) renders a plain <button> whose onClick is
that setter; there is no toggle-off branch, no "All connections" row in the list
(the list is a bare `conns.map`, wholly at wshistory.tsx:203-216), and no clear
button anywhere in the connections column. The only Clear controls on the page
are for the FRAME selection, not the connection: wshistory.tsx:279 ("Clear frame
selection") and the frame-level X.

`selectedExchange` is initialised to null (wshistory.tsx:109) and after any click
can never return to null for the rest of the page's life.

## Classification

UX DIVERGENCE with a dead affordance -- the screen names an action the operator
cannot perform. Not a Burp-parity gap: this one is burpsy's own copy promising
its own missing control.

## What an operator cannot do

Get back to the cross-connection frame view after clicking any connection, and
they are explicitly told to do it. On a capture with several sockets this is the
view that answers "what happened across all of them, in order".

## Note

Two honest fixes, and the choice is a small design decision:
either add an "All connections" entry at the top of the connections list (makes
the all-frames view a first-class, re-selectable state), or make ConnectionRow
toggle -- clicking the selected connection deselects it. The first is clearer,
because the current all-frames state is otherwise invisible and undiscoverable.
Whichever is chosen, the empty-state copy at :257 must match it.
acceptance_criteria: The cross-connection all-frames view is reachable after a connection has been selected, via a control that exists on screen; the frame table's empty-state copy names that actual control.
close_reason: Fixed in e8a8396: two affordances keep the empty-state promise — (a) clicking the already-selected connection deselects it (ConnectionRow toggle with aria-pressed), (b) a 'Clear connection selection' X button in the detail head whenever a connection is selected but no frame is. Proven interactively: relayed two real WebSocket upgrades through the proxy to a local origin, selected a connection (frames filtered), clicked clear (all 4 frames visible again), clicked the same connection twice (deselects). bun run check 163/0.

title: ui: 'Change body encoding' only toggles chunked framing — no form-urlencoded / multipart / JSON conversion
description:
## Claim
The row menu's "Change body encoding" only toggles chunked transfer framing. Burp's item of that name converts a request body between form URL-encoding, multipart encoding and JSON — a different operation under the same label.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/context-menu.html` (bundled docs): **Change body encoding** — *"Change the encoding of any request body between **form URL-encoding, multipart encoding, and JSON**. You can also select Toggle body encoding to switch between the two most recently used encodings in the current Repeater tab."*

## burpsy-side evidence
- Menu entry: `lib/actions.ts:799` — `{ id: "body-encoding", label: "Change body encoding (chunked)", onSelect: () => void changeBodyEncoding(exchange) }`.
- Implementation is chunked framing only: `lib/actions.ts:729-749` `changeBodyEncoding` calls `isChunked(raw) ? dechunkBody(raw) : chunkBody(raw)`; `chunkBody` (`:539-549`) swaps `Content-Length` for `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `dechunkBody` (`:520-536`) reverses it.
- No form/multipart/JSON conversion exists: `grep -rn 'multipart' --include=*.ts lib/` -> no conversion helper (positive control: `grep -rn 'x-www-form-urlencoded' lib/message.ts` -> `:260`, which is a parameter-form *detector* used by the Inspector, not a body converter).

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP for the conversion; the label is separately misleading since it already carries the Burp name for a different operation. The parenthetical `(chunked)` mitigates but does not remove the collision.

## What an operator cannot do
Re-encode a JSON body as form-urlencoded (or as multipart) to test whether the server accepts both — a routine content-type confusion / parser-differential probe. Chunked framing is a useful capability and should stay, under its own name.
acceptance_criteria: The row menu converts a request body between form URL-encoding, multipart and JSON (adjusting Content-Type and Content-Length), and the existing chunked-framing toggle is offered under its own distinct label.
close_reason: Fixed in 3f236ed. 'Change body encoding' now converts the body between form URL-encoding, multipart and JSON (src/lib/body-encoding.ts, built on message.ts's parser: read into ordered name/value pairs, write from them, so order is preserved and duplicate parameters survive). The chunked-framing operation keeps its behaviour under its own label (toggleChunkedFraming), so two different operations no longer share one name. Refusals name the operator's fix rather than half-converting: no body, a type that is none of the three (no sniffing), chunked framing (points at the toggle), doubled '&', a parameter with no '=', an undecodable percent-escape, a file part, a nested JSON member, and converting to the current encoding. Four normalisations are declared in the file header with a test each (percent-encoding canonicalisation, values emitted as JSON strings, compact JSON, generated boundary); byte-exact round trips asserted for form<->multipart and JSON->form/multipart->JSON. Wiring: row-menu submenu opens a new Repeater tab per target; the Repeater request pane converts the draft in place with a per-tab Toggle back. Verified: 44 slice tests pass, bunx tsc --noEmit clean, full bun test src/lib 444 pass, plus 20 independent checks by the main agent (byte-exact form->JSON incl. Content-Length, separator escaping, both round trips with duplicates, and every refusal — including that a file part is refused rather than losing its filename).

title: ui: no 'paste URL as request' — a new Repeater tab always starts from a fixed example.com template
description:
## Claim
There is no way to turn a host or URL into a request. Burp's "Paste host / URL as request" builds a request from a copied URL; in burpsy a new Repeater tab always starts from a fixed example.com template that must be hand-edited.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/context-menu.html` (bundled docs), universal menu options: **Paste host / URL as request** — *"Creates an HTTP request from a copied host or URL. For example, ginandjuice.shop or https://ginandjuice.shop"*.

## burpsy-side evidence
- Absence grep over the whole UI tree: `grep -rli 'Paste host' --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/` -> **no files**; `grep -rli 'as request'` -> **no files**. Same-tree positive control: `grep -rli 'Copy URL' --include=*.tsx --include=*.ts .` -> `pages/logger.tsx lib/actions.ts`.
- The only new-tab path is a fixed template: `app.tsx:472-485` Repeater -> "New request tab" calls `openRepeaterTab({ name: ..., target: "https://example.com:443", protocol: "https", request: templateRequest("example.com") })`.
- `lib/actions.ts:561-577`'s action surface has no URL-to-request entry.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do
Paste a URL from a ticket, a report or a browser bar and get a working request. They open a template pointed at example.com and hand-edit the target field, the request line and the Host header — four edits for what is one paste in Burp.
acceptance_criteria: Pasting or entering a host or URL creates a Repeater tab whose target, request line and Host header are derived from it, reachable from the Repeater menu and the new-tab affordance.
close_reason: Repeater menu gains 'Paste host / URL as request'. Completed another agent's half-done work: requestFromUrl existed in lib/api.ts but was called by nothing and had no tests. Wiring it up found two defects — the pasted scheme went straight into 'target', so ws:// and wss:// built tabs that 400 on first Send (targetParts knows only http/https), and an unknown scheme (ftp:, file:) did the same instead of refusing. Both fixed. 7 unit tests + 2 browser specs that read the built request back out of the rendered tab. 01e4f30

title: settings: no font-size or UI-scaling control — editor text is hardcoded at 12px
description:
## Claim
There is no font-size or UI-scaling control. Burp offers separate font adjustment for the UI and for the message editor; burpsy's only appearance controls are Theme and Table density, and the editor font size is a hardcoded 12px.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/message-editor/text-editor.html` (bundled docs), Syntax analysis: *"You can configure this behavior, and **adjust the font**, in the message display settings."*
- Spec section 2.2 defines two independent scales: a System UI hierarchy (16/13/12/11pt) and a separate `Code / Monospace` scale (12pt, JetBrains Mono / Consolas / Menlo) for *"HTTP Request/Response headers & bodies"* — two knobs, deliberately separate.

## burpsy-side evidence
- Appearance section offers Theme and Table density only: `pages/settings.tsx:1301-1335` (`THEMES` at `:40`, `DENSITIES` at `:46`). `grep -in 'font|scal|zoom' pages/settings.tsx` -> one hit, `:1421`, an inline `fontSize: "var(--fs-sm)"` style on unrelated helper text.
- UI sizes are viewport-fluid clamps with no user input: `tokens/primitives.css:46-48` e.g. `--fs-sm: clamp(12px, 0.68vw, 14px)`.
- Editor font size is hardcoded: `ui/editor.tsx:86` `"&": { ..., fontSize: "12px" }` and `:93-94` gutters at `11px`.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do
Enlarge the HTTP message text without enlarging the tables. Browser zoom is the only lever and it scales everything together — which is precisely why Burp ships the two knobs separately. On a 4K display this is a per-session irritation.
acceptance_criteria: Settings -> Appearance offers a UI text-size control and a separate message-editor font-size control, both persisted, with the editor size driving ui/editor.tsx's theme instead of a literal.
close_reason: Store gains editorFont (12/13/14/16/18px, default 12px = the old hardcoded value) and uiScale (100/110/125/150%), persisted with theme/density in burpsy.workspace. app.tsx applies --editor-font-size and --ui-scale on <html> beside data-theme; editor.tsx's theme reads var(--editor-font-size) instead of the literal (gutters calc(size-1px) preserving the 12/11 relationship); the fluid type tokens re-derive as calc(clamp(...) * var(--ui-scale)) so the chrome scales while the editor — on its own variable — does not. Appearance gains the two selects under Table density. Verified live: 150%/16px updates both custom properties, persists, survives reload, fresh Repeater editor computes 16px. Commit a1b7bf5.

title: settings: no search across settings and no category tree — 20 sections and ~87 fields in one flat scroll
description:
## Claim
Settings is one flat 20-section scrolling page with no search and no category tree. Burp's Settings is a searchable tree, and the search box is how a Burp user finds any setting they do not already know the location of.

## Burp-side evidence
- `settings/ui/hotkeys.html` (bundled docs) navigates by path — *"Go to **Settings > User interface > Hotkeys**"* — and the whole docs tree under `desktop/settings/` mirrors Burp's category hierarchy (`settings/ui/`, `settings/network/`, `settings/tools/`, ...), i.e. a two-level tree is the addressing scheme.
- Same page also records the project/user split, which burpsy has no analogue for: *"The Hotkeys settings are **user settings**. They apply to all installations of Burp on your machine."*
- Spec section 4.12 and the tool sections consistently reference a Settings *dialog* reached from each tool's own gear.

## burpsy-side evidence
- `pages/settings.tsx:1967-1994` `SettingsPage` renders 20 sections in sequence with nothing but a `PageHeader` above them; the file is 2,627 lines with 87 `Field`s (`grep -c Field pages/settings.tsx` -> 87).
- The only search in the whole file is hotkeys-local: `grep -in search pages/settings.tsx` -> 2 hits, `:1271` *"Search hotkeys"* and `:1284` *"No matching hotkey"*. Nothing searches across sections.
- No anchor nav, no tree, no section index component is rendered by `SettingsPage`.
- No project/user distinction: config export/import is a single undifferentiated bundle (`app.tsx:279-323`, `internal/web/api_config.go`).

## Classification
UX DIVERGENCE.

## What an operator cannot do
Type "redirect" or "response modification" and land on the setting. They scroll 20 sections instead, past ~87 fields.

## Decision needed
Scope call before code: (a) add a filter box that hides non-matching sections/fields (cheap, gets 80% of the value); (b) add a left category tree plus deep-linkable section routes; (c) also introduce a project-vs-user settings distinction, which is a data-model decision about what travels with a capture and touches `api_config.go`. (a) and (b) are independent of (c).
acceptance_criteria: Settings offers a search that filters to matching sections and fields across the whole page, and sections are reachable by name (tree or deep-linkable anchors) rather than only by scrolling.
close_reason: Fixed in 3e53e05. Settings gains a search box and a section rail (styles.css rail, +122 lines) built from one list — lib/settings-sections.ts — which the page also renders from, so the rail cannot drift from the sections. Search filters rail + page together; Enter jumps to the first match and outlines it; clearing restores all sections. The palette gets one entry per section from the same list (app.tsx settingsPaletteActions). Verified live this session: 17 sections → "tls" narrows to 7 → Enter jumps and outlines → cleared restores 17; palette carries one Settings entry per section. tsc + bun test src/lib clean (settings-sections.test.ts); ui-pass.sh 53/53 with axe 0 violations on #settings on the final bundle.

title: scan launch: no pre-scan filter step to drop duplicates, static assets or unparameterized items
description:
## Claim

There is no pre-scan filter step. A scan launched from the site map goes straight to the engine, so
static assets and duplicate items consume the request budget.

## burpsy side

`lib/actions.ts:404-405` — "Actively scan this branch (crawl)" / "this host (crawl)" call
`crawlFrom(exchange, "branch"|"host")` directly; there is no intermediate dialog.
`pages/dashboard.tsx:222-236` — `submit()` calls `startCrawl.mutate` and `close()` immediately.

Absence grep: `grep -rniE "remove duplicate|no parameters|remove items with" internal/web/ui/src` -> no
match. Positive control on the same tree: `grep -rn "Actively scan this branch" internal/web/ui/src` ->
`lib/actions.ts:404`.

Note what *does* exist and is not this: the crawl form's bounds — max requests, max depth, rps
(`ui/crawl.tsx:72-83`) — cap the total cost but cannot express "spend it on the parameterized pages,
not the sprite sheets".

## Burp side

`map_root.tsv` class `burp.Zraa` is the wizard step, with the prompt *"You have selected N items to
scan. Before continuing, you can use the filters below to remove certain categories of items, to make
your scanning more targeted and efficient."* and four filters:

- `Remove duplicate items (same URL and parameters)`
- `Remove items with no parameters`
- `Remove out-of-scope items (based on current suite scope)`
- `Remove items with the following extensions` — shipped default
  `js,gif,jpg,png,ico,css,woff,woff2,ttf,svg`

Each renders a live count (the `[calculating...]` variants are in the same class).

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP.

## What an operator cannot do

Aim a bounded scan. With a 200-request budget on a site whose map is 60% static assets, most of the
budget goes to files that cannot carry a finding — and nothing on screen says so.

## Note

The extension filter is the one worth building first; it is a client-side predicate over the same tree
the site map already holds, and Burp's default list is a reasonable starting value to copy.
acceptance_criteria: Launching a scan from a site-map selection offers filters to exclude items by extension, items with no parameters, and duplicates, each showing how many items it removes.
close_reason: Premise measured, then corrected: burpsy's ACTIVE scan is a crawl from seeds, so there is no item set to filter (a crawl discovers unique URLs by construction, so 'remove duplicates' has nothing to remove). The filters landed on the passive branch sweep, which does hold an item set (every captured exchange under a host/path). Server: POST /api/scanner/passive-branch takes exclude, a query in this package's own filter grammar - extension (derived from path) and params (query-string count) already answer Burp's filters, so the shipped extension list is a query an operator can widen and what filtered the sweep is echoed back. Polarity is INVERTED from /api/history?q= (exclude MATCHES the items to drop) and that is stated in the field comment. New 'filtered' bucket in the partition, filter runs BEFORE the no-response and scope gates so an exchange is never counted twice, malformed filter is a 400 with the caret rendering rather than a silently ignored sweep. UI: a dialog with Burp's shipped list editable, a no-parameters switch, live per-filter counts, and plain text saying why out-of-scope and duplicates have no switch (already refused and counted; collapsed by the finding store's dedup). Verified: 4 Go tests, mutation-checked (ignore filter / order after gates / swallow parse error / drop echo all fail them), 18 lib tests over the composition which caught two real bugs in the first draft (not binds tighter than and, so a two-clause filter negated only the first; count ignored which switch was off). Live over HTTP on a console built from this commit: no filter 4/4 unchanged, extension filter removes exactly the 2 assets, combined clause removes 3 leaving the parameterised page, malformed is a 400. go vet/gofmt clean; go test ./internal/web/ ./internal/query/ ./internal/scanner/ green; tsc clean; bun run test:lib 676 pass / 0 fail. NOT live-verified: the dialog's DOM - the browser host is down in this session. Commit ada7a5b.

title: site map: no way to copy the URLs under a host or branch
description:
## Claim

There is no way to copy the URLs under a site-map host or branch.

## burpsy side

Absence grep: `grep -rniE "copy urls|copy links" internal/web/ui/src` -> no match.

Positive control on the same file, showing the copy family that *does* exist:
`grep -n "label:" internal/web/ui/src/lib/actions.ts` -> `:385` `Copy URL`, `:386` `Copy as curl`,
`:387` `Copy exchange id`, `:388` `Copy request to file`. All four are single-exchange; none is
subtree-scoped, and `actions.menu()` is only mounted on the contents table
(`pages/sitemap.tsx:548`), never on a tree node.

## Burp side

`map_root.tsv` class `burp.Zxut` — `Copy URLs in this host`, `Copy URLs in this branch`,
`Copy selected URLs`, `Copy links in this host`, `Copy links in this branch`,
`Copy links in selected items`. ("URLs" is what was requested; "links" is what was found in the
responses — two separate menu items in Burp.)

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP (polish).

## What an operator cannot do

Get the URL list for a host out of burpsy and into anything else — ffuf, a spreadsheet, a colleague's
message — without clicking each row and copying one at a time.

## Depends on

burpsy-react-ui-dpk (tree rows have no context menu) is where this action would live.
acceptance_criteria: A site-map host or branch offers copy-URLs-in-this-branch, putting one URL per line on the clipboard.
close_reason: Implemented in 1e6883d, verified live in browser (proof in the commit message).

title: scope: no Paste URL and no load-from-file for bulk scope entry
description:
## Claim

Scope rules can only be entered one at a time through the form. There is no paste-a-URL shortcut and no
load-from-file, so scoping a 40-host engagement is 40 manual entries.

## burpsy side

`pages/scope.tsx:163-194` — one `Toolbar` of five `Field`s (kind, host pattern, port, path prefix,
protocol) and an "Add rule" button. `addRule()` (`:43-68`) reads those five pieces of state and clears
them; it parses nothing URL-shaped.

Absence grep on the file: `grep -riE "edit|paste|load from|import" pages/scope.tsx` returns only the
`import` statements at `:1-7`. Positive control on the same file: `grep -n "Add rule" pages/scope.tsx`
-> `:192`.

## Burp side

`map_root.tsv` class `burp.Zry2` (`configPanelTargetScope`) — `Add a new item by pasting a URL`,
`Paste URL`, and `Load ...`. The same pair appears on the other scope-entry surfaces: `burp.Zh5w`,
`burp.Zrda`, `burp.Zhw_` all carry `Paste URL` + `Load ...`.

## Classification

CAPABILITY GAP (polish).

## What an operator cannot do

Turn a scope list they were handed — a text file of URLs, or a URL on the clipboard — into scope rules
without decomposing each one into host / port / path / protocol by hand.

## Note

Paste URL is the higher-value half and is nearly free: it is a URL parse feeding the five fields the
form already has. Load-from-file needs a decision on format (one URL per line? the JSON the API
speaks?) and can wait.
acceptance_criteria: A URL can be pasted and decomposed into a scope rule's arms; bulk entry from a file or multi-line paste is available or explicitly declined with a reason.
close_reason: Closed

title: ui: no hide-headers toggle in the message editor (and Settings' 'Uninteresting headers' is a different feature that hides nothing)
description:
## Claim
There is no way to hide uninteresting HTTP headers while reading a message. Burp has an eye button above each message driven by editable Hide request headers / Hide response headers lists. burpsy's similarly-named "Uninteresting headers" setting is a Comparer diffing weight and hides nothing — its own copy says so.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/message-editor/text-editor.html` (bundled docs), Hide headers: *"In the Pretty tab, you have the option to hide HTTP headers that typically don't offer much insight into the target application's behavior... Toggle whether these HTTP headers are visible using the eye button above each message. Burp hides the headers specified in the Hide request headers or Hide response headers list. You can edit these lists in the Settings dialog, under **User interface > Message editor**."*

## burpsy-side evidence
- No such control in the editor: the full toolbar is `ui/editor.tsx:323-344` (Wrap, Copy, Save). `grep -rn 'EyeOff\|<Eye' --include=*.tsx src/` -> no hits in `ui/editor.tsx`; the only "eye" string in the tree is an unrelated comment at `ui/inspector.tsx:144`. Positive control on editor.tsx: `grep -c import ui/editor.tsx` -> 14.
- The name collision is the trap: `pages/settings.tsx:1467-1530` "Uninteresting headers" is explicitly not this feature. Its section detail reads *"Differences in these headers are dimmed in: ..."* (`:1470-1472`) and its footnote states *"**Nothing is hidden.** A difference inside one of these headers is still reported and still rendered — dimmed, and counted separately"* (`:1524-1530`). It feeds Comparer, not the editor.

## Classification
CAPABILITY GAP. Flagging the naming separately: a migrating user reading the Settings tree will conclude the feature is present.

## What an operator cannot do
Reduce a 30-header response to the five that matter while reading it. Also worth a rename or a cross-reference note so "Uninteresting headers" is not mistaken for Burp's hide-headers lists.
acceptance_criteria: A toggle above each message hides the headers named in an editable request/response hide-list, and the existing Comparer 'Uninteresting headers' section is named or cross-referenced so the two are not confused.
close_reason: Message-editor eye now hides two operator-editable, persisted header lists (request + response) instead of a hardcoded set. Settings gains a Message editor section above the renamed Comparer section. Verified live both directions, ui-pass 7/7 with 0 axe violations, tsc clean; commit c7ccab7.

title: ui: no request/response layout switcher — split orientation is hardcoded per page and there is no combined view
description:
## Claim
There is no way to switch how a request and response are arranged. Burp offers three layouts (side-by-side, stacked, and a combined single-pane view with tabs) from icons in the editor's top-right corner; in burpsy the orientation is fixed per page in source.

## Burp-side evidence
- `tools/message-editor/index.html` (bundled docs): *"In the upper-right corner of the message editor, there are three icons that adjust the screen layout.
